News.title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump – how will Burnham react?
News.content:
And it is noticeable that the British government's public reaction is grounded too in the consequences of the war with Iran: the cost of living.

"I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all and that's the cost of living," the prime minister said.

"But I can't get people's cost of living pressures down until the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, the conflict between in Ukraine started by Russia."

Within government the Iran war and its consequences, particularly on energy prices, is widely seen as the biggest individual contributor among the many factors currently driving up the cost of living.

And, bluntly, it is one that puts many, including many of America's allies, in alignment with many in America, Democrat and Republican, who when asked why these elections went as they did, point at the prices displayed outside any petrol station.

Speaking before the votes in America were counted, the Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband reflected on this when I spoke to him on BBC Newscast, external.

When I asked him specifically if he feared that a domestically humiliated Trump may prove more belligerent internationally, it was to the Iran war the foreign secretary referred.

He didn't offer a direct answer to my question, but chose instead to say this: "I know that one of the biggest responsibilities of the whole government, frankly, is the cost of living situation at home, and we know one of the biggest contributors to the cost of living situation is, frankly, the conflict."

"The Strait of Hormuz being not exactly closed, but not properly open, not free flowing, and that is hitting families at home," he said.

"We know that we need a diplomatic way out of this conflict, and so that is one of the things that we're working on. It's something I talked to the U.S. Secretary of State about at the G20, and it's something we continue to work on," he added.

The foreign secretary met Marco Rubio at the meeting in Atlanta last week.

But the big question for the British government, and so many others, is does defeat at home make it more likely that President Trump gets angrier abroad?

Or, do America's traditional allies, the UK, the European Union, Canada, Australia and others feel more strident and willing to work with Donald Trump's domestic political opponents to try to challenge and restrain a weakened president?

The answers to these two final questions will determine much in world affairs in the next couple of years.

News.title: Pound rises to its highest level since the Brexit referendum
News.content:
The value of sterling fell significantly after the Brexit referendum in June 2016, and reached further lows during the Brexit process, the Covid pandemic and the 2022 mini-Budget.

Some traders said the UK was being seen in a different light given relative political stability, solid growth and the rapprochement with the European Union.

Sterling has responded strongly to Brexit developments and political uncertainty in recent years.

Jim O'Neill, an economist and former Treasury minister, said: "I'm not surprised. People were, and to a lesser extent, are, underestimating the improving momentum in the UK,"

A stronger pound can help rein in inflation, and increase buying power for consumers on imports and on holidays.

UK growth so far this year has outperformed all expectations, but there are signs that higher energy and fuel prices have now hit consumer confidence.

The Bank's nine member Monetary Policy Committee faces an important decision on interest rates on Thursday, with the first rise in three years widely expected.

On Wednesday sterling was up 0.28% against the dollar at $1.3434 and was flat against the euro at â¬1.1996 as of 23:01 GMT.

News.title: Typhoons batter East Asia as El Niño makes Pacific 'burn with fever'
News.content:
Wild weather is a way of life for people living along the coast in the Philippines, Taiwan, China and Japan. But the last few months have been extraordinary.

A wave of intense and, at times, unpredictable storms exacerbated by the El NiÃ±o weather pattern has killed dozens, shuttered major airports and wiped out crops and infrastructure across a swathe of East Asia.

In October, nearly all of Taiwan shut down as a monster storm big enough to engulf the island of 23 million roared towards its north-eastern coast. Equivalent to a category five hurricane, Typhoon Champi's 295km/h (193mph) winds had the power to flatten homes and whip up destructive waves.

Thankfully it did not make landfall in Taiwan, skirting past the island while dousing it in rain. But it had far-reaching impacts: hundreds of flights were cancelled in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan. In the Philippines' Batanes archipelago, seaside highways shut as huge waves crashed onto the shore, and in southern Japan's Okinawa islands, power was cut to 15,000 homes.

News.title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK
News.content:
A British man who has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo will be flown back to the UK.

It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.

It is not clear when the flight will take place.

Earlier, a UK government spokesperson said there were "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low.

Reuters news agency reported the infected man is a healthcare worker, citing an internal document BBC News has not seen.

Imported Ebola cases are extremely rare in the UK and have resulted in no deaths.

There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.

A UK government spokesperson said: "The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated.

"Further information will be shared in due course as appropriate. The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low."

There have been more than 10,000 confirmed cases since the recent outbreak in DR Congo started in May, which has grown to become the second most deadly recorded spate of infections, behind the outbreak in West Africa.

It has since become the deadliest in the country's history, with a fatality rate of 48.6% reported at the end of last month.

News.title: Police to escort fire crews in latest crackdown on Bonfire Night disorder
News.content:
Police officers are to be embedded in fire stations and will travel with crews to tackle potential attacks on firefighters during Bonfire Night.

The move is part of Scotland's biggest police operation since the visit of President Donald Trump last summer and a response to a "unique" combination of safety concerns.

As many as 1,700 officers could be deployed to deal with fireworks-related disorder, a European football match involving Celtic and potential protests in Glasgow.

Additional public order vehicles and drivers are being brought in from 18 English and Welsh police forces under mutual aid arrangements.

Emergency services have long recommended organised displays as the safest and often most impressive way of enjoying fireworks.

News.title: UK government to outlaw new North Sea drilling
News.content:
The UK government has moved to ban any new exploration for oil and gas in the North Sea.

The Energy Independence Bill would remove the North Sea Transition Authority's ability to grant new oil and gas licences.

The legislation will not affect the decision on whether to allow drilling at Rosebank off Shetland - the UK's largest known untapped field - which was approved in 2022 before being subject to legal challenges.

The UK government said it was upholding Labour's 2024 manifesto vow not to issue licences for new oil and gas fields, as well as underpinning its commitment to reducing global warming.

The Conservatives described the bill as "dangerous" and accused Labour ministers of being "totally oblivious to the economic and energy threats this country faces".

SNP energy spokesman Graham Leadbitter said the legislation was "designed to exploit Scotland's energy" and reinforced the case for independence.

News.title: Palestine Action ban undermined confidence in anti-terror laws, Supreme Court told
News.content:
The banning of Palestine Action has led to a "crisis in confidence" in the UK's anti-terrorism laws and triggered unprecedented civil disobedience from law-abiding protesters, the Supreme Court has been told.

Opening a major legal challenge to the group's proscription last year, lawyers for co-founder Huda Ammori said that no other protest organisation had been treated the same way.

They told the five justices that the UK's highest court had never before had to consider whether banning a group under terrorism legislation was compatible with freedom of speech and protest.

Twenty-seven protesters were arrested outside the Supreme Court on Wednesday as the hearing took place, the Metropolitan Police said.

Lawyers for Ammori told the court that thousands of elderly people, many veterans of other radical causes, had been arrested for holding up signs supportive of the group since its proscription.

Home Office figures seen by the BBC indicate that there have been more than 4,000 arrests so far at protests in which people have held up signs supportive of the group.

In practice, many demonstrators have been arrested more than once, with 1,200 charges authorised by prosecutors to date. Those trials are in limbo until the outcome of this case.

Henry Blaxland KC told the court that "far from depriving Palestine Action of the oxygen of publicity" and "far from discrediting its brand", proscription of the group has had the opposite effect.

"All it's done is to pour fuel on to a fire of one of the most publicly-contested issues of our time," he said.

"It was disproportionate to do that and in my submission completely unnecessary."

During often tense exchanges with the judges, Ammori's team accepted that Palestine Action could not be described as an ordinary and peaceful protest group.

They said that its members had carried out "direct action" protests by occupying or vandalising firms linked to Israel's military - with only three of 385 incidents assessed by the Home Secretary as constituting an offence under the Terrorism Act.

The UK's definition of terrorism includes incidents of serious damage to property for a cause - and at least two break-ins at defence firms have been described in criminal courts as having caused millions in damage.

Raza Husain KC, for Ammori, said that the judges had to put aside allegations of criminality - for which the state had many powers - and consider whether the Home Secretary's decision to label the group as terrorists had been disproportionate.

"Palestine Action was proscribed on the basis of less than one per cent of its actions over five years assessed as falling within the outer limits of a definition of terrorism," he said.

"The Home Secretary's own experts confirmed the vast majority of its direct action would not constitute an act of terrorism on the basis that any damage to property is typically more minor. Common tactics include graffiti, petty vandalism, occupation, and lock-ons."

One Palestine Action member has been convicted and jailed of fracturing a police officer's back with a sledgehammer - but the court was told that the group had never advocated such violence.

News.title: Kellogg's admits snap, crackle and pop is quieter after uproar over Rice Krispies recipe change
News.content:
Kellogg's has told the BBC the "snap, crackle and pop" sound made by its Rice Krispies may be noticeably quieter after an uproar over the cereal giant's recipe change.

Rice Krispies and Coco Pops are no longer being made with whole rice grains, with the tiny toasted puffs being made using corn flour and rice flour instead.

A Kellogg's spokesperson said retaining the iconic sound had been a "huge focus" when designing the new recipe, but that customers "might notice that the sound may be quieter and not as instant as before".

The firm was responding to complaints online that the taste of the breakfast staples had changed, with some fans adding they missed the "pop" sound.

Kellogg's said it had adapted the recipes due to "changing weather conditions" that have disrupted supplies of some grains and cereals.

The cereal giant said the new versions had been "carefully assessed for taste, appearance and texture", but some shoppers said their children would no longer eat them.

Some expressed dismay that the taste and texture were "totally different" and dubbed the change "grim" and "disgusting".

"There's no snap, crackle and pop in these," a parent named Dani wrote on TikTok. "My toddler won't eat them."

Lauren, also posting on TikTok, added that she had been eating Rice Krispies every day for breakfast "for years and years".

"I had a bowl of the new recipe and you can immediately tell the difference," she said. "They don't have the snapping sound when you put in the milk."

Jessicake meanwhile said they tasted "weird and stale".

The "Snap, Crackle and Pop" - made when milk is added to the puffed rice - has been a centrepiece of the brand's marketing since the 1950s.

Kellogg's insisted the snap, crackle and pop is "still there, but consumers might notice that the sound may be quieter and not as instant as before".

Recipe changes are notoriously difficult for big brands. Chocolate makers are constantly accused of reducing cocoa content in their products and debates rage online over whether ketchup ingredients have changed.

When Scottish fizzy drink Irn Bru cut its sugar content in 2018, fans famously stockpiled crates of the old version.

No changes are being made to Rice Krispies products in the US and Canada, which are owned by a separate company.

Kellogg's said the recipe change in the UK would help "maintain consistent quality" as extreme weather takes a toll on crops and pushes up ingredient prices.

Extreme weather in Spain in 2022 and 2023 in particular had reduced availability of the types of rice the company uses for its breakfast cereals, the company said

Rice Krispies, launched nearly a century ago, are sold around the world and come in variations such as vanilla and strawberry flavours in some markets alongside the widespread chocolate-flavoured Coco Pops version.

"We appreciate that even small changes to a much-loved product can feel noticeable and that's why we have approached this with a lot of care and consideration," Kellogg's said.

The firm said it appreciated the customer feedback and would "continue to look at ways to make [its] products even better in the future".

The cereals have already undergone some change, with reductions in salt content in the 1990s and lowered sugar in 2018. The company said Rice Krispies and Coco Pops will continue to meet UK food standards on levels of fat, salt and sugar in food.

A backlash against processed foods in recent years, especially those low in fibre and high in sugar, has put cereals generally under the spotlight from healthy eating advocates.

Kellogg's stressed the cereals contain no artificial colours, flavours or sweeteners and the nutritional benefits in each bowl, such as fibre, Vitamin D and iron are staying the same.

However, the new recipes mean packaging will now include a "contains wheat gluten" warning. It also continues to contain barley-malt extract.

News.title: Passengers thought mass train attack 'was a joke'
News.content:
Some train passengers initially remained sitting down and thought a man was joking after he told people "I've been stabbed, run", a court has heard.

Anthony Williams stabbed 10 people on the train which made an unscheduled stop in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November last year.

Cambridge Crown Court heard the first person who was stabbed, Jonathan Gjoshe, later asked hospital staff "am I going to die today?".

Williams, 33, of Langford Road in Peterborough, denies 10 counts of attempted murder, and four other alleged attempted murders in earlier incidents in Peterborough and London.

A second stabbing victim said Williams ran away when his pet cockapoo fought back, and another said he threw luggage at the attacker to fend him off.

Jurors have seen CCTV footage of Williams' attack, which took place on the York to London King's Cross LNER service, after it had left Peterborough.

The court was played a video interview with Gjoshe, who said he was on his phone in carriage J at the time and initially thought Williams was someone he knew.

"I've made eye contact with himâ¦ he's pulled a knife, but I just think it was the way he's poked me, the way he's stabbed me, it was a bit weird because it was slow."

Gjoshe said that once he felt a shock "that's when the adrenalin kicked in" and he jumped over the train table.

He said his whole arm was "drenched with blood" and went through the carriage telling people "I've been stabbed, run", but said some other people on the train remained "sitting down, thinking it was a joke".

"It was like a movie, it was quite horrific."

He spent four days in hospital and asked staff "am I going to die today or not? please tell me this".

News.title: £200m taxpayer-funded trains sit barely used for three years
News.content:
A new fleet of publicly funded trains that cost more than Â£200m still remain mostly unused more than three years after the first one was delivered.

They were initially promised to be fully up and running by 2022 but Transport for Wales' boss has said it might not be until the end of 2027 when their tram-trains will be in full service.

Data obtained by the BBC reveals that less than half of the 36 fleet - what TfW call the "final piece" in their Â£2bn South Wales Metro project - have passed rigorous statutory testing.

TfW chief executive James Price said he wants trains that work "100% well, 100% of the time" before putting them into full service.

News.title: Fourth arrest after Halloween party stabbings
News.content:
A fourth boy has been arrested after five teenagers were stabbed at a Halloween party in Hampshire.

Police were called shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday to a home in Park Road in Chandler's Ford where an "unknown group" had gained entry to the event over a garden fence.

One boy, 17, remains in hospital in a life-threatening condition. The other four boys, who all suffered serious injuries, have since been discharged.

A 16-year-old from Southampton has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. Police have been given an extra 36 hours to question a 16 and 17-year-old, also from the city, who were held on Monday morning on suspicion of the same offence.

A 16-year-old boy from Bristol remains in custody having been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder on Monday night.

Two witnesses told the BBC a fight started after a group came in over a garden fence, although they said the motive for the stabbings was unclear.

One of the teenagers said: "I was [standing] in the hallway near the exit and I saw someone I know pull up their shirt and say 'I've been stabbed'.

"And then I later saw him lying outside the front of the house with someone compressing his wound."

The other witness said: "A big group of people started shouting and then a fight broke out and then we just heard the dad tell everyone to leave.

"And that was when we saw someone injured on the floor."

Police cordoned off parts of Park Road and the adjoining Valley Road.

The five boys who were stabbed had been invited to attend the supervised party.

News.title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales
News.content:
The number of deaths from cocaine use in England and Wales has nearly quadrupled in a decade, overtaking those attributed to heroin for the first time.

Cocaine was linked to more than one in five drug poisoning deaths registered in 2025, more than any other single substance, with charities blaming its increased purity and availability.

Meanwhile a record 115 ketamine-linked deaths were registered, almost twice as many as in 2024, according to Office for National Statistics data, external.

The overall rate of drug deaths fell for the first time since 2012. But experts pointed out regional inequality was growing, with the rate of such deaths more than twice as high in the North East as in London.

There were 5,519 drug poisoning deaths registered in 2025 in England and Wales, the equivalent of 92.4 deaths per million people.

Of these, cocaine was mentioned in 1,233 cases - slightly fewer than the previous year but higher than the 1,210 deaths linked to heroin or morphine, which also marked a fall from the previous year's level.

However, deaths linked to opiate and opioid drugs combined were still higher. The ONS also said there was a lag between deaths occurring and being registered.

The fatality rate fell from 93.9 deaths per million people a year earlier, representing the first annual decline since 2012.

In September, National Records of Scotland said drug deaths there had risen by 11% in 2025 on the year before, marking the worst mortality rate in Europe,

In May the Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency said drug-related deaths rose by 7.1% between 2021-23 and 2022-24, external.

News.title: Trump’s constant companion aide Natalie Harp seems to have taken on a more personal role
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Natalie Harp, Donald Trump’s always-at-his-side executive assistant, appears to have now taken control of the president’s personal mobile phone and is deciding who can and cannot speak to him.

For months, the White House has boasted of Trump’s accessibility to reporters and pointed to the fact that numerous members of the White House press corps are able to dial the president’s phone and connect with him for brief phone interviews at all times of the day and night.

But as Trump’s approval ratings have reached a nadir and as his party was taking a humiliating drubbing in the midterm elections, it appears that his so-called “human printer” Harp, is screening his calls to prevent him from having any uncomfortable conversations with journalists — apparently at her discretion.

Multiple journalists confirmed to The Independent that attempts to reach the president over the last 48 hours have found them speaking to a young female who answers the number known to belong to Trump’s personal phone and demands to know who is calling. The Independent had a similar interaction Tuesday night as midterm returns were rolling in.

The call screener was recorded asking who was calling when Politico’s Dasha Burns tried calling Trump during an election-night live stream on Tuesday, and the voice on the other end appeared identical to Harp’s voice based on a recording of her speech to the 2020 Republican National Convention.

President Donald Trump's executive assistant Natalie Harp seems to now have a new job added to her printing duties — screening his cell calls ( Reuters )

Another journalist and longtime White House reporter told The Independent that his recent call to Trump was answered by a young woman, who only put him through to the president after Trump overheard him identifying himself to her and told her that he’d take the call.

The newly-instituted gatekeeping is a departure from Trump’s longtime practice of answering his own phone, something he and his aides have for years boasted about when referring to his accessibility and comparing him favorably to his predecessors in the White House.

But Harp’s apparent involvement comes at a time when the young White House aide appears to be exerting more and more control over the president’s consumption of news and information.

According to multiple reports, it is Harp who has repeatedly connected him with self-described “Islamophobe” and activist Laura Loomer over the objections of other senior members of his staff, and Harp was reportedly responsible for Trump’s decision to bar CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House in September.

The 30-something aide has long been known as Trump’s “human printer” for her practice of following him around and providing hard copies of fawning news coverage to boost his mood.

She has grown increasingly close to Trump, and in recent weeks is understood to have abandoned the desk where she usually sits outside of the Oval Office for a place in his private dining room, printing off hard copies of news articles and documents for the president to read.

Harp, who reportedly posts on Truth Social on the president’s behalf, has been pictured at Trump’s side on the campaign trail and is one of the small group the president has been “increasingly cloistered” with, according to The New York Times, which also reported that it was Harp to whom Trump reportedly dictated his furious 1,300-word rant about Bill Maher aboard Air Force One last week.

News.title: Trump U-turns on former MAGA ally Greg Abbott with dizzying speed after his election loss became clear
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump made a dizzying U-turn in his support of MAGA ally Greg Abbott after he lost his reelection bid for Texas governor.

As voters were heading to the polls Tuesday morning, Trump gushed over the “strong and highly respected” Republican. The president spoke about Abbott “fighting tirelessly to Champion Texas Values,” and listed a platform that seemed aligned with his national agenda, such as keeping the southern border secure and cutting taxes and regulations.

“Greg Abbott has my Complete and Total Endorsement for Re-Election. He is an exceptional Governor and man. GET OUT AND VOTE FOR GREG — HE WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

But then the votes came in.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has made a dizzying U-turn in his support of MAGA ally Greg Abbott after he lost his reelection bid for Texas governor to Democrat Gina Hinojosa ( Getty Images )

Democrat Gina Hinojosa beat Abbott, 52.8 to 45.7 percent, according to results updated by the Associated Press Wednesday evening. Hinojosa will be the first Democrat to be sworn in as governor of Texas in more than 30 years and the first Latina in state history.

Shortly after the AP called the race late Tuesday night, Trump turned against Abbott, whom he was praising just hours before.

“If Greg Abbott, the Governor of Texas, hadn’t become a RINO [Republican In Name Only] in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost. He went back to his original formula, and it wasn’t pretty!” the president wrote on Truth Social.

During his concession speech, Abbott said he had called Hinojosa to congratulate her.

“There are still votes to be counted, but mathematically we’re not going to be able to win this election,” Abbott told his supporters. “I let Gina know that I would assist her and her team in a period of transition.

“But I also want everybody to know that the thing that I’m most proud about is that you all helped me to be your governor for 12 years. Thank you very much.”

James Talarico also beat Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in their Senate race, adding to remarkable wins by Democrats in the ruby red state.

Other Democrats, including Roy Cooper in North Carolina, Annie Andrews in South Carolina, Josh Turek in Iowa, Adam Hamilton in Kansas and Sherrod Brown in Ohio, won key Senate races.

open image in gallery 'If Greg Abbott, the Governor of Texas, hadn’t become a RINO [Republican In Name Only] in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost. He went back to his original formula, and it wasn’t pretty!' the president wrote on Truth Social following the electoral defeat ( Getty Images )

The party is now poised to take control of the Senate as well as the House in what people are calling a blue tsunami.

Trump is coping with his party’s brutal election losses by shifting the blame onto other Republicans, despite telling his supporters to pretend that he’s on the ballot, and trying to deflect by focusing on his unpopular White House renovations.

In his first public appearance since the crushing defeat, Trump stood on the floor of his under-construction, multi-million-dollar ballroom in the demolished East Wing.

“This is the safest place in Washington,” Trump said. “It’s good for me. It’s relaxing.”

News.title: UK agrees to talks to address 'historical harms' of slave trade with Commonwealth leaders
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The UK has committed to entering a "structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue" with nations impacted by the slave trade, a joint communique from Commonwealth leaders has revealed.

The statement declared that the moment had arrived for a "meaningful, truthful and respectful conversation towards forging a common future based on equity".

This follows moves by prime minister Andy Burnham to consider a formal UK apology for its historic part in the transatlantic slave trade, though he dismissed paying direct reparations.

In the document, leaders stated: "We welcome the agreement of the Government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms."

open image in gallery A demonstrator holds a placard that reads ‘Reparations now!’ during a protest on the day Britain's King Charles meets a range of communities representing Bahamian culture by Parliament Square, as part of a autumn tour of Caribbean nations, in Nassau, The Bahamas, October 28, 2026 ( Reuters )

The UK has faced mounting demands to pay reparations for its role in the slave trade. Earlier this week, Burnham signalled that he was “open” to a formal apology and approved £40m in aid funding for the Caribbean.

He said that the Commonwealth is “more important today than ever before” amid “such volatile times” globally as he met his Antigua and Barbuda counterpart Gaston Browne.

King Charles told a summit in the Caribbean this week: “The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth.

“As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow.”

A small protest was seen near the perimeter of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting area with activists holding a sign that read “You say you regret so apologise”, and “Apologise for the greatest crime against humanity and let’s have reparatory justice”.

open image in gallery King Charles and Queen Camilla have met with Commonwealth leaders ( AFP/Getty )

Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has insisted that British taxpayers will not pay a penny more as a result of Mr Burnham’s “new approach” to the Commonwealth.

Speaking to BBC Newscast, he accused previous governments of having had a tendency to “sweep under the carpet” the issue of slavery, and echoed his boss in ruling out extra financial contributions, as well as the prospect of reparations, for the UK’s historical role.

In 2006, Sir Tony Blair expressed “deep sorrow and regret” for Britain’s involvement in the slave trade when he was serving as prime minister, but stopped short of an official apology.

Mr Miliband criticised what he described as a “sorry, not sorry” from Sir Tony, and suggested that the Government might reach the point of a formal apology by the time it hosts the G20 leaders’ summit in Manchester next November.

Calls for an apology and reparations have grown in recent years, with St Lucia’s Prime Minister Philip J Pierre, chairman of the 15-member Caribbean Community (Caricom) reportedly saying the economic and political bloc was “ready to engage” in the “structured dialogue” Mr Burnham had proposed.

The Commonwealth leaders’ summit coincided with a visit by the King, who is the head of the group, to the Caribbean.

News.title: Lockheed Martin to pay $29.5 million settlement for discrimination against white workers
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Lockheed Martin has agreed to a $29.5 million settlement with federal authorities over allegations from President Donald Trump's administration that its internal diversity and equity initiatives led to reverse discrimination against white workers.

The defense contractor will hand over $22 million to the U.S. government to resolve claims that it breached anti-discrimination rules tied to its federal contracts, according to an announcement issued late Tuesday by the Department of Justice and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.

An additional $7.5 million will be paid to more than 1,000 affected employees under a separate agreement with the EEOC.

The agency had been investigating Lockheed Martin over allegations that it violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which prohibits employment discrimination based on race.

In an official statement, Lockheed Martin rejected the government’s allegations but explained that it "agreed to resolve this matter with the Department of Justice and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission to avoid the distraction and expense of prolonged litigation."

"We did not admit liability, determining it would be best for all involved to put these matters behind us so we can remain focused on our critical national security mission," the defense contractor added.

The outcome highlights the Trump administration's continued reliance on the 1863 False Claims Act to compel government contractors to abandon their diversity, equity, and inclusion programs.

The Civil War-era statute imposes steep financial liabilities on contractors that submit fraudulent claims to federal authorities.

Historically used to prosecute financial fraud, the administration has instead applied the law to companies it claims engage in racial discrimination under the guise of workplace inclusion.

The Department of Justice has previously reached comparable legal settlements with major corporate contractors, including IBM, Deloitte, and Accenture.

Civil rights organizations have strongly criticized the Trump administration's enforcement actions, maintaining that they attack long-standing mechanisms designed to prevent both intentional and unintentional bias against traditionally marginalized groups during hiring and promotion.

Lockheed Martin is the prime contractor in the manufacture of the F-35 jet fighter, which can cost up to $100 million apiece. Former flight instructor Richard Roland Jones III is now suing the company and a supervisor there over claims of unceasing bigotry and harassment. ( AFP via Getty Images )

A number of civil rights groups have launched legal challenges against the administration’s anti-DEI directives.

The specific allegations against Lockheed Martin stem from an internal bonus initiative introduced in 2021 that offered salary increases and promotion opportunities to the company's top 20% of employees.

Under the system, managers submitted nominations that were subsequently analyzed to "flag" demographic outliers based on race and sex.

When nominations raised these flags, supervisors were requested to review their selections and the "merit-based basis for the selections, without asking them to take any protected characteristic into account."

However, federal officials alleged that company staff actively "exerted pressure on leaders in their business group to resolve race-related ‘flags’ by directing them to add or remove particular employees based on race."

Prosecutors maintained that management was pressured to exclude nonminority employees from consideration while adding racial minorities.

The joint settlement follows a whistleblower action brought by former Lockheed Martin vice president Tim Booher, who will receive $4.4 million from the government under the False Claims Act.

Booher resigned in May 2023, stating in an October 2025 court filing that he "felt that he could no longer be complicit in LMC’s illegal discrimination."

Booher met with EEOC Commissioner Andrea Lucas in July 2024 to present his claims. Lucas, who was appointed EEOC chair after Trump took office in January 2025, launched a commissioner's charge that prompted the federal inquiry.

Booher’s legal team issued a statement praising the "amicable conclusion that avoids prolonged litigation and ensures statutory compliance in federal contracting."

Lucas, a prominent opponent of DEI initiatives, has repeatedly called on white male employees to file complaints with the EEOC and has initiated similar charges against corporate giants including Nike.

"Title VII protects every worker from employment discrimination on the basis of race — and that protection does not yield when discriminatory decisions are framed as diversity initiatives," Lucas said in a statement accompanying the settlement.

News.title: CBS News is dead last in network ratings coverage of midterms, Nielsen data reveals
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

All the major networks were vying for viewers as midterm election returns rolled in Tuesday night — and CBS News unsurprisingly came in distant last.

After David Ellison, who has reportedly courted President Donald Trump, took over Paramount and named Bari Weiss as editor-in-chief of CBS News, the network has seen dismal ratings. Even on a night when Americans were glued to their TVs, CBS News struggled with its viewership, suggesting just how far the network has fallen during its overhaul under Ellison and Weiss.

CBS News’ election night coverage was the least watched of major broadcast networks, which include NBC and ABC, Brian Steinberg, a senior TV editor for Variety, wrote on X Wednesday, citing people familiar with early Nielsen data. It was also behind cable networks such as CNN, Fox News and MS NOW, according to the data.

CBS News had around 2.6 million viewers, including 715,000 in the key 25-to-54-year-old demographic during primetime. In comparison, the three big cable news networks each garnered an average of roughly 3.9 million viewers, Steinberg said in a follow-up post.

open image in gallery All the major networks were vying for viewers as midterm election returns rolled in Tuesday night — and CBS News unsurprisingly came in distant last with around 2.6 million viewers ( CBS News )

CNN’s Chief Media Analyst Brian Stelter shared the average primetime viewership for each network in a new X post. NBC came out on top with 6.52 million viewers, followed by ABC with 4.91 million, then CNN with 3.93 million, MS NOW with 3.92 million, Fox News with 3.88 million, and CBS with 2.63 million.

NBC News has said it also drew a record 29 million views across social media platforms thanks to the network’s chief data analyst, Steve Kornacki. Kornacki — known for frantically tracking race results using an interactive board — spent 10 and a half hours on Americans’ screens, drawing twice as many live viewers on his “Kornacki Cam” as its main competitors.

Coming in last is something CBS News has gotten used to. Its evening show has struggled with Tony Dokoupil at the helm.

CBS Evening News averaged 4.04 million total viewers last season, down 3 percent, Adweek reported in September, citing Nielsen data.

While the news program saw 4.63 million viewers the week of October 19, a 10 percent increase, according to Nielsen data reported on by Adweek in late October. But it still lagged behind NBC’s Nightly News with Tom Llamas, which brought in 6.72 million viewers and ABC’s World News Tonight with David Muir, which brought in 8.84 million viewers.

open image in gallery After David Ellison, who has reportedly courted President Donald Trump, took over Paramount and named Bari Weiss as editor-in-chief of CBS News, the network has seen dismal ratings ( Getty Images for Uber, X and The Free Press )

Dokoupil’s move from CBS Mornings to the flagship night program last January was met with criticism, with one network staffer telling The Independent at the time that Dokoupil has turned the Evening News into “state TV.”

Weiss has faced her own backlash over controversial editorial decisions, including her choice early on in her tenure to pull a 60 Minutes segment about Venezuelan migrants sent by the Trump administration to CECOT, an El Salvadoran prison accused of having inhumane conditions. The segment aired nearly one month later.

The team at 60 Minutes also saw a major shakeup last May during a day dubbed “Black Thursday,” during which Executive Producer Tanya Simon was ousted, along with her deputy, Draggan Mihailovich, and correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi.

One network insider complained about Weiss to Page Six last month: “She doesn’t hear anybody. If you don’t agree with what she’s saying or doing, it doesn’t matter. She pretends to hear ideas, but she really doesn’t listen to anyone.”

News.title: Amy Acton let Vivek Ramaswamy’s concession call go to voicemail after repulsive attack ad featuring her estranged mother
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Democrat Amy Acton declined to answer a phone call from Republican Vivek Ramaswamy when he reached out to concede the Ohio gubernatorial race, following a contentious campaign marked by an aggressive political  involving her estranged mother.

Ramaswamy confirmed the unanswered call during his election night address to supporters, as reported by Newsweek.

“We left her a message,” Ramaswamy said. “It’s a tough night for us here in Ohio.”

The victory makes the 60-year-old physician the first woman elected governor of Ohio, ending 16 years of Republican leadership in the state. Acton is the first Democrat to win the governor's office since Ted Strickland was elected in 2006, halting a rightward shift in a state that voted for Donald Trump in three consecutive presidential elections.

The contest escalated last month when Ramaswamy ran a $4 million campaign  featuring Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, who called her daughter a liar regarding her upbringing. Arthur lost custody of Acton following the indictment of Acton’s stepfather for allegedly raping Acton when she was 12 years old.

open image in gallery Following a bitter race that featured a commercial targeting her childhood, Democrat Amy Acton reportedly let a concession call from Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy go to voicemail as election results came in ( Getty )

The ad faced widespread bipartisan criticism. Outgoing Republican Gov. Mike DeWine described the ad as “deeply, deeply troubling” and requested its removal, though he maintained his endorsement of Ramaswamy. Trump and Vice President JD Vance initially supported the campaign effort before it was discontinued.

Acton addressed the controversial ad directly during an October 24 campaign rally in Cleveland with former President Barack Obama.

“My opponent has chosen to exploit, intentionally, my childhood to save his struggling campaign, but it’s not going to work,” Acton told the crowd.

Speaking at another campaign event in northwest Ohio after the commercial aired, Acton described the situation as the “big elephant in the room.”

“The reason I talk about my childhood when I do is just one: I started to realize it might give other people hope that you can, you know, get out of your circumstances,” she said.

open image in gallery Ramaswamy ran a $4 million campaign  last month featuring Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, who called her daughter a liar regarding her upbringing. Arthur lost custody of Acton following the indictment of Acton’s stepfather for allegedly raping Acton when she was 12 years old ( Getty )

During her victory speech on Tuesday, Acton reflected on her personal history before stepping into the role of governor, where she previously served as health director under DeWine during the early stages of the Covid-19 pandemic.

“I know what it’s like when people look the other way when you’re struggling,” Acton said. “As a child, I experienced abuse and neglect. And I could have never imagined going from homeless to being a doctor. Let alone that I would be standing here, the next Governor of Ohio.”

Walking out to the song “You’ve Got the Love” by Florence and the Machine, Acton framed the election results as a turning point for state politics.

“Ohio has chosen unity and decency over division and hate; the healing begins today,” she told supporters.

“I’m so incredibly honored that I have earned the trust of Ohioans to be the next governor of Ohio,” she said. “It has meant the world to me and my family. This entire campaign has been a movement by and for the people; this win is for every Ohioan who has longed for public servants again, who solve problems instead of making them and do not mistake kindness for weakness.”

open image in gallery Reflecting on her journey to becoming the first woman elected governor of Ohio, Acton promised to serve ‘for every Ohioan who has longed for public servants again’ ( Getty )

Acton pledged to govern across party lines despite the hostility of the campaign, which featured no face-to-face debates between the candidates.

“We must never give up on one another,” Acton said. “I wanna make something very clear to the people of Ohio. I will be a governor for all Ohioans. I am in this fight for all of us.”

She added: “To those who voted for me, and those who did not, I will work with anyone and everyone.”

In his concession speech, Ramaswamy offered support for the incoming administration.

“I wish her well to lead this state to hopefully greater heights in the future,” Ramaswamy said, calling it a “tough race” that was “bitter at times in both directions.”

“I have hope and confidence that she will do what is required to bring Ohio together,” Ramaswamy said. "We are rooting for the success of this state; we’re rooting for your success, and that means all of us in this room should be rooting for the success of her administration, and we’re hopeful for Ohio to achieve great things regardless of what happened tonight in this election.”

open image in gallery Despite a hostile campaign with no debates, Ramaswamy acknowledged a ‘tough night’ and expressed confidence that Acton would bring the state together following the election outcome ( Getty )

According to figures from the Associated Press with 95 percent of the vote counted, Acton secured 51.9 percent of the vote compared to Ramaswamy’s 44.8 percent.

Donald Kissick of the Libertarian Party received 3.3 percent.

Earlier tallies at 81 percent counted showed Acton leading with 50.7 percent to Ramaswamy's 46 percent when the former Republican presidential candidate conceded.

The result coincided with broader Democratic gains in the midterm elections, in which the party secured control of both chambers of Congress after flipping U.S. Senate seats in Texas, Kansas, North Carolina and South Carolina.

Acton succeeds DeWine in leading a state currently navigating policy decisions regarding the economy and the expansion of AI data centers. Former Lieutenant Governor Nancy Hollister previously served as Ohio's governor for 11 days in 1999 following George Voinovich’s transition to the Senate, making Acton the first woman elected to serve a full term in the office.

The Independent has contacted both campaigns for comment.

News.title: Champions League power rankings: PSG remain a joke – but who is catching them?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

It was largely business as usual in matchweek four of the Champions League as Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona kept on scoring and Arsenal and Bayern Munich returned to winning ways while remaining unbeaten.

But the story of the round belonged to Como, who made history by beating Lens 9-1 away from home and equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game. Cesc Fabregas’s impressive side now sit fourth in the league phase standings, behind PSG, Real Madrid and Arsenal.

Meanwhile, there was a frustrating defeat for Liverpool at Fenerbahce, but Manchester United produced a stunning comeback to beat Roma and potentially save Michael Carrick’s job, with Matheus Cunha scoring twice on a remarkable night at Old Trafford.

We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season.

Agree or disagree with our standings? Let us know and have your say in the comments below.

↔️ 1. Paris Saint-Germain

Results: 6-1 vs Slovan Bratislava, 4-2 v Man City, 4-2 v Barcelona, 6-0 v Villarreal

Fixtures: Roma (h), Aston Villa (a), Como (a), Galatasaray (h)

The reigning champions are making a mockery of suggestions that they are slow starters in the Champions League. Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions finished outside the top eight in both of their previous successes but have started this campaign on fire in Europe. PSG were 4-0 up after just 17 minutes at Villarreal, and that was without Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. The French champions will be without the brilliant Georgian for the rest of the season after he suffered a ruptured ACL but they remain the team to beat.

open image in gallery Fabian Ruiz scored twice in the 6-0 demolition of Villarreal ( Getty )

↔️ 2. Barcelona

Results: 5-1 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Galatasaray, 2-4 v PSG, 3-0 v Aston Villa

Fixtures: Sabah (a), Manchester City (h), Sporting (a), Como (h)

Defeats to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in LaLiga ended their winning start under Hansi Flick and perhaps raised the same concerns over whether their defence holds up come the knockout stages. But Lamine Yamal is arguably the world’s best player on current form and Raphinha isn’t too bad, either. The Brazilian made it an astonishing 19 goals and three assists in just 13 matches across LaLiga and the Champions League with his double in the 3-0 win over Aston Villa at Camp Nou.

open image in gallery Lamine Yamal and Raphinha are on stunning form for Barcelona ( Getty )

↔️ 3. Arsenal

Results: 1-0 vs Napoli, 3-0 v Lille, 2-2 v Bayern Munich, 2-1 v Slavia Prague

Fixtures: Borussia Dortmund (h), Real Madrid (h), Real Betis (a), Sabah (h)

Mikel Arteta’s got the result they needed in Prague, even if a difficult second-half performance made it a bit of a struggle. An entertaining draw last time out at Bayern Munich, who have such a strong home record, gave a good account of whether the Premier League champions can take the next step against a heavyweight side in the business end of the Champions League.

open image in gallery Noni Madueke was on target in Arsenal's win in Prague ( PA )

↔️ 4. Bayern Munich

Results: 5-0 v Bodo/Glimt, 3-3 v Viking, 2-2 v Arsenal, 2-0 v Atletico Madrid

Fixtures: Lille (a), Slavia Prague (h), Manchester United (a), Real Betis (h)

Bayern returned to winning ways with a professional win against Atletico Madrid – and the big surprise was that Harry Kane was not on the scoresheet. The Ballon d’Or holder’s 10-match scoring run in the Champions League came to an end at the Metropolitano, missing the chance to equal Cristiano Ronaldo’s record. But Bayern rolled on.

open image in gallery Lennart Karl, 18, and Konrad Laimer scored in Bayern Munich's 2-0 win at Atletico Madrid ( AP )

⬆️🟢 5. Real Madrid (+1 from 6)

Results: 2-1 v Inter Milan, 4-3 v Roma, 4-1 v RB Leipzig, 3-2 v AEK Athens

Fixtures: PSV (h), Arsenal (a), LASK (h), Shakhtar (a)

Perhaps chaos is the new normal under Jose Mourinho. Real Madrid trailed late on in Athens but Kylian Mbappe equalised before Fede Valverde scored a stunning winner in stoppage time. Jude Bellingham also scored an outrageous flick. Somehow with maximum points, despite trailing Roma 3-1 at the Stadio Olimpico, and Inter and RB Leipzig spurning chances to take the lead at the Bernabeu, the 15-time Champions League winners continue to find a way.

open image in gallery Real Madrid players celebrate Fede Valverde’s stoppage-time winner ( Getty )

⬇️🔴 6. Man City (-1 from 5)

Results: 2-0 v Porto, 2-4 v PSG, 5-1 v AEK Athens, 3-2 v Leipzig

Fixtures: Napoli (h), Barcelona (a), Lens (a), Sporting (a)

Back-to-back defeats in the Premier League have the shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well. But a battling win at RB Leipzig, with a customary Erling Haaland goal, was a good response, even if City have now gone seven games without a clean sheet. Next up: the return of Kevin De Bruyne with Napoli, followed by a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona.

open image in gallery Erling Haaland scored Manchester City’s winner in Leipzig ( Reuters )

↔️ 7. Liverpool

Results: 2-1 v Atletico Madrid, 6-3 v LASK, 4-3 v Villarreal, 2-3 v Fenerbahce

Fixtures: Club Brugge (a), Porto (h), Inter (a), Lens (h)

Liverpool have conceded three goals in three consecutive games in the Champions League or European Cup for the first time and the manner of their “messy” collapse against Fenerbahce was a concern. The nature of Liverpool’s squad means Andoni Iraola has needed to rotate in Champions League but Liverpool’s performance in Istanbul underlined the task he faces. In-form Club Brugge can’t be taken lightly after the international break.

open image in gallery Liverpool lost their 100 per cent start in Istanbul ( PA )

⬆️🟢 8. Aston Villa (+1 from 9)

Results: 3-2 v Club Brugge, 6-0 v Fenerbahce, 3-1 v Viking, 0-3 v Barcelona

Fixtures: Galatasaray (a), PSG (h), Borussia Dortmund (h), Slavia Prague (a)

Despite defeat in the Camp Nou, you get the feeling that Unai Emery’s new-look Aston Villa will have learned a lot from their meeting with Barcelona. They had moments of threat, too. Bright showings from the refreshed attacking line-up of Nicolas Jackson, Johan Manzambi, Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson have helped the Europa League winners retaining their identity under Emery despite the huge squad turnover in the summer.

open image in gallery Emery accepted that Aston Villa have ‘work to do’ to match the Champions League’s elite ( AP )

⬆️🟢 9. Inter Milan (+1 from 10)

Results: 1-2 v Real Madrid, 3-4 v Club Brugge, 1-0 v Shakhtar, 3-0 v Feyenoord

Fixtures: Stuttgart (h), Borussia Dortmund (a), Liverpool (h), Slovan Bratislava (a)

After starting with back-to-back defeats, how badly Inter needed to respond with back-to-back wins. A comfortable win at Feyenoord also came after Saturday’s Milan derby defeat, with Pio Esposito stepping up amid Lautaro Martinez’s continued absence.

open image in gallery Inter’s group-phase fixtures were rated as the easiest of the 36 teams in this season’s competition ( Getty )

⬆️🟢10. Como (+5 from 15)

Results: 4-1 v RB Leipzig, 2-3 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Manchester United, 9-1 v Lens

Fixtures: AEK Athens (h), Real Betis (a), Paris Saint Germain (h), Barcelona (a)

WOW. If Como announced themselves by thrashing Manchester United, the Champions League debutants stole the show this week with a NINE-goal dismantling of poor Lens. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side became the first team to score nine goals away from home in the Champions League or European Cup since 1971. The Italian side are certainly making a name for themselves. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase are going to be fascinating.

open image in gallery Como thrashed Lens 9-1 in a statement Champions League result ( AP )

News.title: Man City have a striker who will not be stopped and a defence that cannot be trusted
News.content:
“You can look at it that it’s difficult to keep concentrated for 100 minutes or you can look at it like it’s only 100 minutes you have to stay focussed to get a chance - you can look at it in a few different ways and I look at it in the second option,” Haaland added.

This was a victory to bounce back from losing in the Premier League at the weekend, but the question will be how can City mount a title challenge with such a brittle defence. Champions League winners do not leave themselves open at the back like this, and City have now gone seven without a clean sheet.

Maresca insisted last week that his starting line-up is Donnarumma plus 10 others, but the reality is that Haaland is the guaranteed name on the team sheet. And his goalkeeper’s errors are becoming a problem.

This one added to the goals against Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain that were also on his watch. He could have claimed the cross that led to Brighton’s winner at the weekend too.

Here he went from hero to villain in the space of a few minutes at the start of the second half. Firstly, from kick-off Christoph Baumgartner got close with his angled drive heading towards the top corner until Donnarumma’s fingertips turned the ball around the post. It was a save that had the Italian celebrating like he had scored a goal.

But he had his head in his hands after Leipzig’s next move. Nico O’Reilly could have done better after losing the ball in midfield, then failing to track the overlapping run from Baku. With Red Bull Arena waiting for a cross, Baku had spotted Donnarumma slightly out of position and beat him at the near post. It was superb improvisation, but without doubt a goalkeeping error.

News.title: Complacent Arsenal hang on in Prague as Gyokeres revival continues
News.content:
Those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing of his players. So smooth at first, Arsenal then became remarkably open as the game wore on. Slavia deserve credit for that, but there is no doubt that Arteta’s side became complacent. They were perhaps a little fortunate not to be punished for it.

Wiktor Nowak’s 90th-minute goal was hard-earned by the Czech side, who had found a way to rattle the Arsenal defence with long balls and direct runs. It was not enough, though, to steal the limelight from Madueke, who is developing nicely in the absence of the injured Bukayo Saka, and from Gyokeres.

It was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and there were plenty of reasons for them to feel confident upon their return here.

Among those reasons was Slavia’s poor form in Europe’s premier competition. The Czech side came into the match on a run of 22 games without victory in the Champions League, and in the knowledge that one more game without a win would equal the European Cup record.

To make matters worse for the home side, they recently banished their star striker from the club due to a series of disciplinary failings. Tomas Chory, Slavia’s top scorer for the past two seasons, has been chucked out of the team after showing his middle finger to the referee in a recent game. This sort of sanction would have earned Arteta’s nod of approval, no doubt, but it probably did not increase Slavia’s chances of hurting the Premier League champions.

Overall, then, this was always unlikely to be the most challenging contest of Arsenal’s European campaign. Arteta being Arteta, though, he still picked many of his favourites. There was no rest for Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa or Gabriel Magalhaes, who all started in the Prague chill.

News.title: Liverpool calamity hands Iraola his most chastening night yet
News.content:
Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

“Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found issue had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

News.title: Oil prices plunge after Republicans suffer midterms defeat
News.content:
Oil prices fell sharply after JD Vance blamed the Republicans’ election rout on the Iran war.

The price of a barrel of Brent, the global benchmark, fell as much as 10pc to $93 a barrel by Wednesday evening, while WTI was down more than 8pc to $88.

It marks the first time since Oct 7 that Brent has fallen below $100 a barrel.

The decline came after the vice president said that voters had abandoned the party owing to dissatisfaction with Donald Trump’s war in the Middle East.

This has boosted traders’ hopes that the US President could seek to de-escalate his conflict in the Gulf, which would increase global oil supplies.

Posting on social media, Mr Vance said: “The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.”

Mr Trump later admitted Mr Vance’s comments were “largely true”.

He said he expected oil prices to “go up a lot more” than they did because of the war, reaffirming that “Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon.”

“If I had it to do again, I’d have to do it again, because long term, it’s the only answer. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.

“I thought the oil would go up a lot more, and I did it on that basis.

“You have no choice. You have to do it. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon, or everything that you see here someday might not exist.”

Traders also responded to the prospect that the Democrats could restrict Mr Trump’s funding for the war.

Claudio Galimberti, chief economist at Rystad Energy, said the President is now likely to come under “greater institutional pressure” to strike a peace deal with Iran.

This will ease pressure on economies around the world after oil prices have risen by roughly 70pc since the war broke out in February.

The Republican rout also prompted Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX to lose nearly $159bn (£118bn) in market value when trading opened in New York amid fears the Democrats’ success will derail the AI boom.

The carmaker and rocket company both fell 5.8pc as Wall Street opened after the Democrats swept to victory although they pared losses later.

Mr Musk, the billionaire boss of both companies, was the leading donor to the Republicans during the election campaign as he hoped for light-touch regulation of his AI ambitions.

However, analysts said the Democrat victory would slow down the pace of the rapid build-out of data centres.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the race for Texas Governor and is expected to oppose the rapid build-out of AI.

A sharp decline in the value of data-centre developers Tesla and SpaceX, both based in Texas, would wipe billions off Mr Musk’s nearly $900bn fortune. He spent $446m on backing failed Republican candidates.

As the Democrat victory emerged, Mr Musk wrote on X: “Data centres in space looking pretty appealing right now.”

He later wrote: “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time.”

News.title: Ebola risk to UK remains ‘low’ despite evacuation of infected Briton
News.content:
Authorities have insisted that the risk to the UK is low after it emerged that a UK humanitarian worker infected with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of Congo to Britain for treatment.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said it would not disclose the identity of the worker but confirmed a British citizen currently in the DRC has tested positive for the viral haemorrhagic fever.

“The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated. Further information will be shared in due course as appropriate. The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low,” the FCDO said in a statement.

The patient is due to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday, according to Reuters, and will be transferred to one of the UK’s high-consequence infectious disease units based at the Royal Free Hospital in London and the Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle.

The worker had been responding to the outbreak currently raging in the Ituri region of DRC. The first cases of the Bundibugyo strain of the disease were first reported in May and there have now been more than 10,000 cases and 5,000 deaths.

It is the second largest outbreak in history and is taking place in a region racked with conflict and where mistrust of authorities is widespread.

Several aid agencies are working in the area including Médecins Sans Frontières, Oxfam and Unicef.

There are no specific treatments or vaccines for the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus and the backbone of treatment is supportive care. In July the World Health Organization launched the Partners trial in DRC to test whether the monoclonal antibody MBP134, the antiviral remdesivir, or a combination of both can improve survival. Another monoclonal antibody will soon be added to the study.

Researchers are also testing multiple vaccines, two of which were developed specifically for Bundibugyo. These are ChAdOx1, developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna’s mRNA-1469.

News.title: Budget cuts and ministerial churn has weakened aid spending transparency, report finds
News.content:
The UK has become less transparent in how it spends its aid budget, amid repeated cuts and ministerial turnover, according to a new report.

The 2026 Aid Transparency Index, the world’s only independent peer-reviewed assessment on aid transparency evaluates how well major donors, development banks, and UN agencies disclose their spending and activity data. In the latest ranking the UK’s transparency score fell 13.9 points from “very good” to “good”.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) lost points for its lack of “comprehensive forward-looking country and organisational budgets and strategies, and project objectives”.

Twenty of the 33 ranked international organisations, over 60 per cent, scored “good” or “very good”, with just three rated “poor” or “very poor”. Germany, the US and the UK gave over 40 per cent of all overseas development aid in 2025, yet all three saw their transparency scores fall, according to the index.

“It’s not like [the FCDO] made a conscious decision to do anything badly or to miss anything… Our gut feeling is they’ve just taken their eye off the ball,” said Gary Forster, CEO of Publish What You Fund, a global campaign for aid and development transparency, which published the index.

“The FCDO hasn’t had a meaningful strategy since 2023,” he told The Telegraph.

For over two decades, the Department for International Development (DFID) operated as its own cabinet level ministry after it was set up in 1997 by Tony Blair, then Labour prime minister. In 2020, Conservative prime minister Boris Johnson merged it with the Foreign Office to create the FCDO.

The responsibility for aid was downgraded from a secretary of state to a minister of state position. Even then, there has been rapid ministerial turnover, with four international development ministers in the past two years.

The UK’s development budget, which funds programmes to tackle poverty and is a lifeline to millions around the world, has been repeatedly cut in recent years.

The UK historically prided itself on committing to spend 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on Official Development Assistance (ODA). In 2020 that figure was cut to 0.5 per cent and last year, Sir Keir Starmer, former prime minister, cut the target to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

News.title: Emery endures heaviest European defeat as Villa manager to old foes Barcelona
News.content:
“[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”

Barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

“We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which showed it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”

Team news from Nou Camp to follow shortly.

News.title: Man Utd show fight on night of chaos to give Carrick a glimpse of hope
News.content:
So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

Roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

And then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

United fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

Sports.title: Premier League cult hero, 55, officially announces plan to stand against Gianni Infantino for Fifa presidency
Sports.content:
Next

PREMIER LEAGUE hero Ramon Vega has officially announced his candidacy for the Fifa Presidential election.

The former Tottenham and Switzerland defender, 55, last month announced his plans to challenge controversial Fifa chief Gianni Infantino for the presidency next year.



Infantino has been weathering calls for him to step down since his disastrous plans to sell off shares in the World Cup were revealed earlier this year.

Uefa are pushing to oust the executive, but Vega has become the first figure to publicly step into the ring with the incumbent ahead of Fifa‘s election in Rabat in March.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans right to tell Sir Jim Ratcliffe where to stick new stadium, says ex-chairman who hired Sir Alex Ferguson
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED have been told to splash the cash on new players — rather than plough it all into a new 100,000-seater stadium.

Ex-Red Devils chairman Martin Edwards warned his old club the priority must be to beef up their underachieving squad so they can get out of relegation trouble.



United plan to move from Old Trafford into a state-of-the-art £2billion venue next door within the next decade.

But Edwards, 81, — chairman from 1980 to 2002, when he enjoyed huge success with Sir Alex Ferguson — rapped: “There’s no point in having a wonderful stadium if you can’t fill it.”



Michael Carrick’s side are fourth from bottom of the Prem but ended a nine-game winless run with a 3-2 Champions League comeback victory over Roma on Tuesday.

United fans have chanted “You can stick your new stadium up your a**e” in protests against co-owners the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Edwards said: “The crowd have been vociferous about what they could do with the new stadium. And I tell you what — I can sympathise with that.

“You can talk about new stadiums and everything else but the most important ingredient is always the players and what’s happening on the field — and success.

“Now the last thing the United fans want to hear is a new stadium when they’ve got a team that’s languishing 17th in the league, below Coventry.

“The priority has to be the team. Concentrate on getting that right. United now needs investment. I mean, they probably need investment on the stadium itself.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“So the club needs investment spending. The team definitely needs investment, doesn’t it?

“When I look at the team sheet, I think, why isn’t it performing? You know, there’s some good individuals on that. It’s down to choice. Did they need midfielders? Do they need a left-back or centre-forward?”

Edwards is unsure whether the Glazers and Ratcliffe should stick with Carrick.

Speaking on the latest episode of Keys & Gray Unleashed, he said: “I can’t judge, you need to be inside to know.



“I was on the inside. I had knowledge the supporters didn’t, which enabled me to make the right decisions. I still go to games. It’s always special for me.”

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Eze struggles to impose himself after getting reprieve as Gyokeres gives Arteta food for thought
Sports.content:

ARSENAL survived a late scare to notch a win over Czech outfit Slavia Prague to get back to business as usual in the Champions League.

Mikel Arteta‘s men remain unbeaten in the competition but could not look after a precious clean sheet as they look set to cruise into the knockouts.



Viktor Gyokeres was the standout for the visitors – but it was not a night where everyone shone.

Here’s how SunSport’s Mitchell Hall rated the travelling Gunners...



David Raya – 5

A quiet night for the Arsenal stopper as he did not face a shot on target in the entire first half.

Much of his game was relegated to speculative long balls to Gyokeres, which in fairness led directly to the opener.



Looked a little nervy while dealing with Slavia’s crosses and big men in the box in the second half, and should have dealt with the late cross to protect his clean sheet.

Ben White – 5

Had some promising involvements in the early stages, especially going forward.

Went missing a bit in the middle of the match as Arsenal found more luck progressing through central areas.

Was called upon again to defend late on, but overall failed to leave his mark on the match.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Ezri Konsa – 6

Had a lot of work to do against Slavia’s speedy wide threats, especially with Hincapie and White pushing up as high as they did.

Threw himself into a reckless challenge to get himself a yellow card but didn’t make any silly errors in dangerous areas.

Was hooked for Cristhian Mosquera in the 62nd minute, possibly to protect him from a second caution.

Gabriel Magalhaes – 6

Stepped up behind Piero Hincapie on a few occasions and found himself caught high for a ball in behind.

Did well to recover and hold up his runner when called upon.



Piero Hincapie – 5

Found his opposite number quite a handful at both ends of the pitch and was caught high on a couple of occasions, though Konsa was in position to cover more often than not.

Lost his man late on for a header that went mercifully wide.

Declan Rice – 8

Took the armband in the absence of Martin Odegaard and looked every bit the leader on the pitch.



Swept up Slavia’s long balls in behind with relative ease and never looked troubled by their attempts to press him.

His forward thinking helped produce Arsenal’s second as he picked out a line-breaking ball to Gyokeres in a dangerous area.

Martin Zubimendi – 6

Kept things ticking over in midfield and didn’t need to cover the same amount of ground as his midfield partner Rice.

Not a spectacular performance by any means but recycled the ball well when Slavia tried to clear their lines to help Arsenal keep the pressure up.

Noni Madueke – 7

Took his goal well as he slotted home at the end of a clever run behind the defensive line.



Didn’t see as much of the ball on the right flank but looked dangerous when he got it, and had some success darting to the touchline before standing it up towards the back post.

Mikel Merino – 7

Played as the most advanced player in a midfield three – and at times appeared to be backing up Gyokeres as a second striker.

Was on his toes to roll the ball through for the Swede’s goal, and came close to adding one of his own from close range.



Eberechi Eze – 5

Couldn’t fault the wide man’s effort levels as he charged around the pitch, but as has been the case for much of the season, something was not clicking for the former Crystal Palace star.

Had a wonderful chance to double his side’s advantage after sitting his man down with a feint, but toothlessly rolled his effort into a covering defender.

Other than that, not much seemed to come off for him.

Viktor Gyokeres – 8

The Swede took hold of the opportunity to show Mikel Arteta what he can offer.



He bullied the Slavia defence and produced a fantastic bit of strength and awareness to play Noni Madueke in behind for the opener.

Then he got himself on the scoresheet with a delicate finish over a sliding defender and in off the post to get himself off the mark in the Champions League this season.
