A helpful injection of energy into a back line that had been run ragged by electric winger Emmanuel Ayaosi.

Looked clumsy going into the last quarter of an hour and at one point managed to take out two Slavia stars at once.

Christos Tzolis (for Eze 62′) – 5

Barely had a touch of the ball after coming on and was not able to do too much with it as attentions turned to protecting the clean sheet.

Sports.title: RB Leipzig 2 Man City 3: Erling Haaland spares Donnarumma’s blushes as City get back to winning ways
Sports.content:
Next

GIANLUIGI DONNARUMMA owes his big pal Erling Haaland a huge thank you for sparing his blushes.

The pair – both part of the captaincy group at the Etihad – sat together on the flight out to Germany on Tuesday afternoon.



But as skipper for the night, the striker would have been dismayed to see his keeper drop another clanger to gift Ridle Baku an equaliser early in the second half.

Yet Haaland loves playing against Leipzig and sure enough he had the last word in another high-scoring game between these two old foes.



He tapped in the late winner to finally break Leipzig’s resistance – after a superb run and cross from Elliot Anderson.

These two teams know each other well having met six times in the last five years and if there is one thing guaranteed when they do meet it is goals.

A total of 30 have gone in during their previous meetings – making it the second-highest scoring fixture in the competition for goals per game.

And we were not disappointed here – although it took a while to get going.



Enzo Maresca and Martin Demichelis are close friends – almost like brothers after playing together at Malaga – and together they served up a treat.

Rayan Cherki – one of four changes to the team from the defeat by Brighton – took a pass from Enzo Fernandez but pulled his effort past the far post.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Red Bull had been slow starters but found their wings after that early scare and had chances to go ahead.

Antonio Nusa, an international team-mate of Haaland, fired a shot from 20 yards that was pushed over the bar – slightly unconvincingly – by Donnarumma.



Then David Raum saw his effort blocked by Matheus Nunes after the visitors had failed to clear their lines.

While City had most of the ball, Leipzig were creating the best chances and another opening saw Christophe Baumgartner curl a shot beyond Donnarumma but just wide of the post.

England hopeful Phil Foden had talked on the eve of this game about how he wanted to chip in more goals to take the heat off Haaland.

He had the chance to do just that when he pounced on a poor clearance and created space for himself but then steered his effort narrowly off target.

However, City did not have to wait long for their opener as eight minutes before the break Nico O’Reilly crossed from the left looking to pick out Fernandez.



But Castello Lukeba slid in to get there first but in doing so, he could only direct it into his own net.

Leipzig boss Demichelis – who was a title-winning centre-back with Man City and Bayern Munich as a player – looked on in despair as his team did not deserve to be behind. They soon put that right though.

Donnarumma showed what he can do when he made a flying save to deny Baumgartner.

But then came another moment to forget. Brajan Gruda saw Baku’s run on the outside and played him in. The full-back spotted a gap at the near post and rolled his shot there.



It was a clever idea from the Germany international full-back – but surely the keeper should not be beaten from there?

The game was back in the balance and City edged ahead again when Iliman Ndiaye’s cross to the back post was headed home emphatically by Fernandez.

The record signing has had some underwhelming displays recently but it was a sweet moment for the Argentina internatonal.

He didn’t have long to enjoy it though – just three minutes to be exact. His old Chelsea team-mate Christopher Nkunku made a quick impact – spraying a pass to Nusa who brought it down and finished superbly.

The Frenchman was banished to the “bomb squad” at Stamford Bridge by Maresca – so it was the perfect answer for him.



And Nusa – who starred with Haaland at the World Cup – looked set to get one over on his mate.

But the main man – who had been quiet against his favourite opponents – had the last word scoring against Leipzig for a 13th time in eight games.

Maresca wants more of his players to chip in with goals but he won’t mind too much with the Norwegian in this kind of form – that’s 14 for the season now.

Even so there was time for both teams to hit the woodwork with Raum curling an effort against the bar – with Donnarumma nowhere.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cherki thumped an effort against the post while home keeper Maarten Vandevoordt scrambled another Haaland effort around the post.



Demichelis and Maresca shared a big hug at the end – fans will hope they can meet more often if it produces second halves like this.

Sports.title: Slavia Prague 1 Arsenal 2: Gyokeres and Madueke keep Gunners on course for top-eight finish as Arteta rings the changes
Sports.content:
Next

ARE you watching Thomas Tuchel?

Noni Madueke was left out of the England manager’s last squad in September – but he will surely be in the one named tomorrow.



The winger has been in fine form over the past few weeks, and he kept that up with a brilliant showing last night as Arsenal eventually eased past Slavia Prague.

Madueke scored the Gunners’ opening goal after nine minutes – and they should have won by far more.



Viktor Gyokeres added a second in the 38th minute to ultimately secure the win and the Gunners had a nervy finish as Wiktor Nowak pulled one back at the death.

Tuchel will be delighted with the way Madueke has responded to being left out of his previous squad.



This goal in Prague came after the winner for Arsenal at Nottingham Forest last month and the winger has stepped up with Bukayo Saka out injured.

Mikel Arteta must have feared the worst when Saka pulled his quad in the Gunners’ 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich two weeks ago.

But Madueke has answered the call and will surely be rewarded with the chance to play for England next week when they face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League.

Those will be tough tests, certainly far greater than the one Arsenal had here.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

They won the same fixture exactly a year ago 3-0 and since then Slavia’s winless run in the Champions League had extended to 22 games.

The host’s last victory in the competition was in 2007, two years before Max Dowman was even born.

The teen star had been expected to start this clash, given he is one game into a three-match domestic ban.

Dowman became the youngest player in Champions League history at this very ground last season after coming on as a sub.

And he would have to settle for a spot on the bench again this time, with Arteta naming a strong side.



There were six changes to the team that beat Liverpool 1-0 last Sunday, but the likes of Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and Gabriel all kept their places.

Konsa and Gabriel starting in the heart of defence meant William Saliba, on the bench for the first time this season after a back injury, would have to wait for his comeback.

Slavia’s side lacked the quality of Arsenal’s.



Nazar Domchak, 19, was given his Champions League debut in goal and striker Tomas Chory was absent from the squad.

Slavia’s top scorer in the past two seasons has been banished by the Czech club until further notice after swearing at a referee when sent off during a game last month.

But the home fans did not let that dampen their spirits.

They gave it the big one before kick-off, backed up by a choir singing pitchside and fireworks going off on the roof.

Perhaps the Sparta supporters had seen Arsenal humbled by Fleetwood Town last week in the Carabao Cup and so anything felt possible.



The Gunners swiftly took control of this game, however, as the midfield ran the show.

Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Rice rotated their roles with ease and Sparta struggled to cope.

Arsenal’s opener actually came from bypassing the trio, though, as a long ball from David Raya found Gyokeres on the halfway line.

The Swede chested it down and managed to hook a pass into the onrushing Madueke.



The winger had plenty of ground ahead of him, yet composed himself to finish with ease.

It was then a case of how much Arteta’s side would kick on from there.

Eberechi Eze was causing chaos on the left flank, drifting inside and beating defenders with ease.

The right was still Arsenal’s most dangerous side, however, and twice Merino wasted good chances from crosses into the box.

The second goal finally came shortly before the break and Merino made amends by playing in Gyokeres to score.



It was a superb touch and finish from the Swede, who after a slow start has two goals and three assists in his last five games.

That was no more than the Gunners deserved for a commanding 45 minutes.

Rice, captain for the night, was at the heart of it and typified how Arteta’s side were able to boss so much of the possession.



Slavia at least showed some signs of life early in the second half.

Left-back Oskar Kubiak finally forced Raya to make a save and the hosts had a dangerous free-kick strike the wall.

Arteta was becoming agitated on the touchline, clearly frustrated by his team loosening their grip on the game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Spaniard responded by bringing on Cristhian Mosquera and Christos Tzolis, who gave some freshness to a performance that was getting a bit stale.

Slavia continued to push for a goal and got one back late on as Nowak tapped home from a wicked cross.

Sports.content:
Como make Champions League history to prove Man Utd thrashing was no fluke

Como secured a thumping 9-1 win in Lens as they continued to thrive in Europe with their margin of victory equalling Champions League history

View 2 Images Nico Paz scored as Como demolished Lens

Cesc Fabregas' Como made Champions League history with an incredible 9-1 win at Lens as their European fairytale continued.

‌



‌



The Italian team are playing in the tournament for the first time but have not been overawed. They have enjoyed a rapid rise in recent years and on Wednesday night hammered their French opponents on their own patch.

‌



Como have won three of their four games to sit fourth in the league phase at the halfway stage - above the likes of Barcelona, Manchester City, Liverpool and Bayern Munich.

‌



Just weeks after hammering Manchester United Como reached new eights and their win in France equals the margin for the biggest victory ever in the Champions League.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola gamble backfires as familiar Liverpool failing returns in Fenerbahce collapse
Sports.content:
Liverpool twice led but found a way to lose at Fenerbahce as their perfect record in the Champions League came to an end on a rain-soaked night in Istanbul.

Vedat Muriqi ultimately had the decisive moment in a five-goal thriller that saw Liverpool's defensive flaws exposed again as they failed to control a game they had within their grasp.

Trey Nyoni's deflected volley had the Reds in front as they looked to respond following their loss to Arsenal on Sunday, but their lead didn't last long as Mason Greenwood's effort, which was also deflected, levelled the game.

Alexander Isak came off the bench with half an hour remaining and needed just minutes to put the Premier League side in front, but Andoni Iraola's side again failed to keep hold of their advantage as Nathan Brown got Fenerbahce back of level terms.

‌



Muriqi, who replaced Romelu Lukaku, would later head home from a looped cross as questions were asked of Alisson's failure to come and claim.

Greenwood was Fenerbahce's biggest threat and the ex-Manchester United forward was sent clear but went down under pressure from Kostas Tsimikas, but the penalty appeals from the home side were waved away.

That frustration was compounded only minutes later as Liverpool teenager Trey Nyoni opened the scoring. His volley from the edge of the box went in via a deflection, leaving Ederson with no chance as the jeers rained down from the home fans.

‌



The Turkish side hit the bar moments later as Ismail Yuksek's effort hit the woodwork, denying the hosts an immediate equaliser, but they weren't to be denied as Greenwood did level the contest. Liverpool led for just four minutes with the forward's free-kick flying in off on Jeremy Jacquet.

The Reds had won just four of their 11 visits to Istanbul, but were coming up against Fenerbahce for the first time. Dirk Kuyt, a man who scored 71 times for the Reds and played in 2007 Champions League final for them, is currently in charge of the Turkish outfit.

Virgil van Dijk's header was Liverpool's first major chance of the second-half, and had his effort been either side of Ederson then he may well have been in trouble. Isak though was on hand to convert when he had his chance from close range, nodding Liverpool in front for the second time on the night.

View 4 Images Vedat Muriqi scored Fenerbahce's winner

‌



Much like the first-half though, the Reds lead was short lived. Brown, who came through the ranks at Derby, scored four minutes later at the back post to restore parity. And things would get even better for Kuyt and Fenerbahce - who saw Muriqi head home the winner with 11 minutes left.

FAMILIAR FLAWS HAUNT REDS

Liverpool had a night where they simply didn't want to hold onto a lead - and they ultimately left Turkey with nothing as their game management and their defence were again called into question.

A team who were beaten 6-0 at Aston Villa less than a month ago showcased their powers of recovery on numerous occasions across the evening, but for all their good work Liverpool will wonder how they twice led but ultimately ended up losing.

Iraola's side were only in front for a total of eight minutes despite twice putting themselves in front as Fenerbahce continued to hit back at speed. Whilst their determination and fight can be admired, a Liverpool team boasting the likes of Van Dijk have to look at themselves and question why they didn't keep things tight.

‌



They say you're at your most vulnerable when you've just scored and Liverpool certainly proved that to be the case. They also showcased their defensive frailties again - this was the fourth time they've conceded three goals in their last eight games - with the issue clearly not being addressed.

BARCOLA PLAN FLOPS

Irrespective of the result, it was soon apparent that having Barcola as the central point of Liverpool's attack was not going to be a long-term thing.

The Frenchman was given the nod in one of the more surprising selection calls of the night. Him playing wasn't a surprise. Him playing as the No 9 with Alexander Isak on the bench was.

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola was deployed centrally, but struggled to make an impact

‌



Barcola's USP has long been his pace, and that is best used out on the flanks. Either challenging full-backs or having the license to make those out to in runs which allow him to find himself in central spaces.

Naturally the ex-PSG man is not the most physical, nor he is renowned for his ability to bring others into play. Both of those are assets for someone leading a line. There's no doubt it stunted Liverpool's attack, which relied heavily upon the individual quality of Rio Ngumoha.

If Iraola was looking to see how he'd manage if Isak was a long-term absentee as Hugo Ekitike remains sidelined, then its fair to say he can conclude that Barcola will not be his answer. The natural No 9 needed only three minutes to find, what would be, the winner.

TREY PUSHES HIS CASE

In a Liverpool midfield that has Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch, Nyoni continues to enjoy the backing of his manager and he's more than repaying that faith.

‌



View 4 Images Trey Nyoni has continued to showcase his quality in midfield

Iraola knows how to unlock the potential of a young midfielder, just ask Bournemouth's Alex Scott, and Nyoni continues to flourish and scored the first goal of his career In Istanbul as he made the most of the space he was afforded on the edge of the Fenerbahce box.

Eyebrows were raised when the 19-year-old was given the nod at the weekend, but getting picked again suggests his presence in the Liverpool midfield could become increasingly regular. Performing in the cauldron that is a European away day in Turkey is as good a gauge as any.

Despite his age Nyoni never looked overawed and the most pressing problem for Iraola could be explaining to one of his most established stars why a teenage star has leapfrogged them in the pecking order. There's no doubt he outshone Szoboszlai in the middle of the pitch, with the Hungarian's displays increasingly coming under scrutiny.

‌

Sports.title: Ally McCoist fumes over controversial Mason Greenwood incident during Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Ally McCoist fumes over controversial Mason Greenwood incident during Liverpool clash

Mason Greenwood was involved in a controversial incident during the early stages of Liverpool's Champions League clash against Fenerbahce

View 2 Images Mason Greenwood was controversially denied a penalty against Liverpool (Image: (Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP via Getty Images))

Ally McCoist was left stunned that Fenerbahce were not awarded a penalty for a foul on Mason Greenwood. After 20 minutes of Liverpool's Champions League clash against the Turkish giants, Greenwood was played through on goal, but a firm shove from Kostas Tsimikas knocked him off balance and prevented him from shooting.

‌



‌



Claims for a penalty from Greenwood and the home support were waved away with VAR also failing to review the incident. Upon watching replays of the potential foul, McCoist was adamant that a penalty should have been given.

‌



He said on TNT Sports: "It's a penalty, it's two hands, not even one hand. That prevents him for me getting a shot on goal. Both hands. I think it's a penalty, I really do. It's a shame because it's a great ball and an exquisite touch.

‌



"I think so (got away with one), I really think so. He pushes him both hands when he's in the process of having an attempt on goal just because it doesn't look like it, doesn't make it not a penalty."

Liverpool went straight up the other end, and Trey Nyoni put them in front with a deflected effort which further angered Fenerbahce. However, Greenwood equalised moments later with his free-kick wrong-footing Alisson after a touch from a Liverpool player.

‌



The set-piece from Greenwood appeared to be going wide but a stray touch from Jeremy Jacquet changed the trajectory of the ball ,which left Alisson fuming.

Analysing the goal, McCoist added: "He [Greenwood] gets a break doesn't he? I think the goalkeeper will not be too happy with his wall.

‌



"Does somebody turn their back on it? It's the perfect answer. It's Jacquet and he's livid, does he turn his back? He certainly does, you've got to face it. The goalkeeper is livid, absolutely livid and with justification as well. He's (Jacquet) is side on for someone who has had a good start to the season."

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet was blamed for the goal Liverpool conceded to Fenerbahce

‌

Following Liverpool's opener, Fenerbahce dominated proceedings with Irfan Can Kahveci striking the bar before Greenwood's goal. The latter also went close with a left-footed effort from close range.

‌



Greenwood arrived at Fenerbahce from Marseille this past summer in a €39million (£32.5m) deal. He had spent two years in France with a loan spell at Getafe coming before that.

The United academy product was free to join the La Liga club on a temporary basis after he was no longer in the plans of his boyhood club.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand makes fresh demand to Man Utd star who 'hasn't been doing it enough'
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand makes fresh demand to Man Utd star who 'hasn't been doing it enough'

Matheus Cunha's late brace saw Manchester United see off Roma in the Champions League - with Rio Ferdinand demanding the Brazilian maintain that level

View 2 Images Rio Ferdinand has laid out his demands for Matheus Cunha (Image: Getty Images)

Rio Ferdinand hopes that Matheus Cunha's match winning brace for Manchester United serves to kick on his career at Old Trafford as he concedes the Brazilian has not delivered enough.

‌



‌



Cunha is into his second year in Manchester having moved from Wolves for £62.5million, but has been part of a team that's been regularly criticised following a nine-game winless run. That was snapped with a comeback win over Roma on Tuesday night.

‌



Cunha scored twice in the final 10 minutes as United came back from 2-0 down to win 3-2, leading to huge celebrations at Old Trafford. The Brazilian was sent off in the final moments of the game, but Ferdinand still sees it as the benchmark going forward.

‌



Last term Cunha impressed in patches, scoring 10 times, but his display in midweek was his most defining in a red shirt to date and Ferdinand is now hoping for more.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said on his YouTube channel: "I think for Cunha this could be liftoff where he starts to catch fire,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel. ‘I think he’s a hugely talented footballer and he showed glimpses, especially last season.

"Could this be the game that unlocks him? Because I haven’t seen it enough yet with him. You see moments, and you go, 'Oh, look at that, that’s why we paid the big money for him', but not enough.

‌



"He needs to be watching back that performance and go, where were the fans feeding off me there? Where was I getting them going? Where was I getting the team and being the pressure point for the team? It was without the ball a lot of the time. And keep bringing that every game."

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha was Man Utd's match winner on Tuesday (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Cunha has had to show his versatility this season with United's only genuine No 9, Benjamin Sesko, out injured. That has seen the ex-Wolves man having to lead the line on occasion.

The 28-year-old acknowledged their recent struggles, but maintained he needed to be the type of player who stood up when the chips were down.

‌



He said: “I think everything, when we tried to do it, being part of Man Utd is very hard because in these kinds of moments in the season, we know we always have these kinds of comparisons with the past. We need to have these kinds of games like today, and then we’ll pass the hard moment. But today was a blessed day for me.

“Being part of this, I have a responsibility. I always talk inside about that – I need to be this kind of guy – to have the responsibility in the hard moments and the good moments. I always need to show up and be there for nights like today.”

Sports.title: Inside the rise of Will Lankshear: Harry Kane and Alan Shearer comparisons as England squad beckons
Sports.content:
"Will Lankshear is as good a finisher as I've seen since Alan Shearer".

If you've started to hear the hype around Middlesbrough's record £20m striker, get ready for even more.

England manager Thomas Tuchel is reportedly sending one of his scouts to see if Lankshear can add to his 13 goals in 13 Championship games against Wrexham on Wednesday night, with Friday's England squad an outside possibility.

Pundits are already queuing up to make classic number 9 comparisons, with veteran EFL manager Neil Warnock heaping praise on the 21-year-old's "unbelievable, special finishing".

‌



Lankshear, who has 15 goals for Boro in all competitions this season, also scored on his England Under 21s debut in September.

And his Tottenham origins, predatory goalscoring instincts, and humble, hard-working personality are allowing commentators to make the obvious Harry Kane references.

How Michael Carrick channelled Sir Alex Ferguson to turn around 'embarrassing' Man Utd display READ MORE :

Lankshear missed Wednesday night's game with Wrexham ahead of the upcoming international break, but with the lack of up and coming English forwards behind Kane, could Lankshear eventually jump the queue and gatecrash Tuchel's Euro 2028 plans?

‌



'Baffling decision for Spurs to sell Lankshear'

Football London's Tottenham correspondent Alasdair Gold has described Spurs' decision to sell Lankshear as "baffling" and expects him to pass the 20-goal mark "within weeks".

Gold makes the stark contrast to Tottenham's underperforming forwards and says Boro fans must be "laughing at their fortune".

In fact, since joining the Boro, Lankshear has only scored one fewer goal than Tottenham have as a whole team.

Tottenham sporting director Johan Lange made the decision to cash in on Lankshear in the summer - reportedly £8-10m up front and the rest in add-ons.

‌



Gold said: "Lankshear's second goal in the victory against Charlton was reminiscent of a certain Ballon d'Or winner he looked up to in training.

"He will become a very good Premier League striker and it's mind-boggling that Spurs did not simply loan out a player who was not desperate to leave permanently, or even heaven-forbid, give him a chance to prove himself."

However, Gold says the north London club have matching rights on any future offers for Lankshear as well as a 20% sell-on clause that would benefit them regardless of whether they or another club signs him down the line. It is against the rules to have a buy-back clause with EFL clubs so that not an option.

'He had offers from bigger clubs'

After Middlesbrough manager Kim Hellberg arrived in November 2025, no team created more chances in the Championship - but no team in the Championship missed more big chances either. They needed an elite finisher to go again for Premier League promotion.

‌



In the summer, Hellberg, head of football Kieran Scott and head of recruitment Chris Jones drew up their transfer shortlist, with Lankshear described by one insider as a "dream" target.

The Spurs man had been a long-term target for Boro after they tracked his progress for many years. They tried to sign him in January, but he opted to honour his loan at Oxford.

Scott told Teesside Live: “We have to use our sales pitch. Someone like Will for example, he has a burning desire to be in the Premier League and play at the top level.

“I don't want to embarrass the lad but he had several opportunities that were financially a lot more rewarding for him. I would argue that some clubs were bigger because they were playing in Europe.

‌



“But he bought into this, really liked what we were about. He saw himself as a No.9 here and he's about feel. He gets a good feel Will, and the more time I spent with him you realise he's not flash, he's not looking for the biggest and best training ground."

Everyone at Boro has been blown away by just how successful he’s been so far.

‌



A one-touch finish expert

Lankshear's instinct in the penalty area is ‘elite’ already.

That might feel like a big claim given he’s only playing in the Championship, but that trait doesn’t really matter what division you’re in. Lankshear just has that knack of being in the right place at the right time, as shown by the fact that 10 of his 13 league goals have been one-touch finishes.

‌



Coaches I’ve spoken to say that instinct is hard to teach. Lankshear just has it.

Hellberg is a coach who focuses massively on individual development.

‌



Lankshear has yet to register an assist this season, and Hellberg has spoken a lot about working on other sides of Lankshear's game, in terms of his pressing and his back-to-goal stuff.

And it’s not just on the pitch where Lankshear has impressed. People behind the scenes at Boro talk of a young lad who’s mature and has his head screwed on, but is also humble too.

‌



He’s also said to be a really driven character, and obsessed with improving all the time. A typical centre forward, Hellberg and his team-mates have joked about his intensity in front of goal in training.

Hellberg added: "He even celebrates if he scores a small goal on a possession drill - he still celebrates all his goals with a fist. I think that's why he scores so many goals. Even if he touches the ball very few times in a game.

‌



"He's come here and is taking a massive development through the season. I think he was top from the first day in the box and how he finished, but he has increased his quality in the run-and-turn game.

"It comes from massive pressing. He has taken big steps, and he works so hard every day to improve, and that's what's taking him here. But at the end of the day, also having fantastic teammates that set it up in a brilliant way helps.

Team-mate Riley McGree jokes: “In training he loses his head when he doesn't finish and score! It's really good to see, because I can relate to that as well.”

This is a young player that’s been compared to fellow former Tottenham striker Harry Kane for many years. Even moving to Boro for a record fee brought with it attention and therefore pressure.

‌



He’s handled everything so far with class and maturity. Let's see what happens next.

Sports.title: INEOS sack manager as Man Utd co-owners make brutal decision after 'lengthy talks'
Sports.content:
INEOS sack manager as Man Utd co-owners make brutal decision after 'lengthy talks'

INEOS' decision to sack the manager came after Sir Jim Ratcliffe put Swiss club FC Lausanne-Sport up for sale

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS have sacked FC Lausanne-Sport's manager

FC Lausanne-Sport have parted company with manager Luka Elsner after five months in charge as Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s INEOS plans to sell the Swiss club. Lausanne, who are part-owned by INEOS, confirmed on Tuesday that they had reached a mutual agreement with the 44-year-old.

‌



‌



A statement read: "After lengthy discussions about the current sporting situation, FC Lausanne-Sport and Luka Elsner have mutually agreed to end their collaboration."

‌



Elsner was appointed on 1 June but leaves with Lausanne bottom of the Swiss Super League. His departure comes as INEOS have put the club up for sale.

‌



The reported decision to sell Lausanne-Sport comes after INEOS abruptly ended its sponsorship agreements with New Zealand’s All Blacks rugby team and Tottenham Hotspur last year.

‌



Meanwhile, Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has also been under pressure at Old Trafford following a disappointing run of results. United eased some of the pressure on Carrick by coming from two goals down to beat Roma 3–2 in the Champions League on Tuesday, ending a nine-game winless run.

Much of the supporters' frustration has been directed at Ratcliffe and the Glazer family. In the 21st minute, fans threw green and gold balloons onto the pitch and chanted against the owners.

‌



Roma had gone 2-0 up inside 17 minutes, but United hit back in the second half. Bruno Fernandes scored from the penalty spot before Matheus Cunha struck twice to complete the comeback.

Cunha was booked for taking off his shirt as he celebrated the winner in front of the home fans. A later challenge on a Roma player earned him a second yellow card.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester United came from behind to beat Roma but Michael Carrick remains under serious pressure

‌



Speaking after the game, Carrick said: "Disappointed with how it finished, but again just shows how much he cares and willing to do, and when he's in that frame of mind, he's in that mood and he plays like that, that's what we want from him."

On the game, the Reds Devils manager added: "It was a challenging game. I think we started OK in the game, we knew it was going to be tough — they’ve only had one defeat all season. They’re a very, very good team.

‌



"So we talked about what we wanted to do in the game, we started OK and then the goal came from nowhere. We caused ourselves a few issues. In some ways, understandable with the run we’ve been on, a little bit anxious and a few nerves at times.

"This place [Old Trafford] does it. No matter what situation you’re in, how tough it can seem, the supporters are desperate to get behind you and we gave them something to go on. We gave them other opportunities to score and it was close, and you’re thinking, 'That’s another chance gone by,' but we kept looking, kept pushing for answers and we found them in the end."

Sports.title: Wolves hit back to beat Bristol City after late Neave double
Sports.content:
Substitute Sean Neave scored a late brace as Wolves came from behind to secure a 2-1 Sky Bet Championship win over Bristol City at Ashton Gate.

The hosts took a 34th-minute lead when Scott Twine was fouled 25 yards out and got up to fire in an unstoppable right-footed free-kick, sending the ball curling away from Jose Sa's dive and into the top corner.

But Wolves piled on the second-half pressure and were rewarded after 82 minutes when Kieran Trippier volleyed in a cross from the right, Adam Armstrong's first-time shot was saved and Neave pounced to net the rebound.

Six minutes later Neave was on target again, nodding home from close range after Ladislav Krejci had headed a Trippier free-kick across goal.

Wolves were deserved winners and move up to second in the table, but the result was cruel on the Robins, who defended with great tenacity.

City boss Michael Skubala made two changes from the team that won 3-2 at Bolton, promoting striker Sam Bell and midfielder Twine from the bench, while Wolves brought in Jean-Ricner Bellegarde for the injured Jordan James.

Until Twine's spectacular strike, the only fireworks had come from a display before kick-off.

Wolves looked the more dangerous side in the opening half-hour but had only an Armstrong shot, comfortably saved by Brad Collins, to show for their efforts.

Lorent Tolaj headed wide for City from a 29th-minute cross by Rio Cardines, but his side were equally goal-shy at the end of some promising attacks.

Skubala's men were clearly boosted by the goal and were quicker into the challenge for the remainder of the half without creating clear openings.

Wolves began the second period attacking the end where their travelling fans were massed and looked certain to equalise in the 57th minute.

Rodrigo Gomes, only just introduced as a substitute for Marshall Munetsi, who had needed treatment for a head injury just before the break, broke clear down the middle only to delay his shot and be denied by a brilliant recovery tackle from Cam Pring.

Collins spilled a low shot from Rafiki Said after 61 minutes, recovering to smother the rebound effort from Armstrong.

Wanderers fashioned another good chance four minutes later when Bellegarde rose to meet a Trippier corner and saw his downward header parried by the diving Collins.

City were dangerous on the break and Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto made a triple change in the 73rd minute, sending on Mateus Mane, Neave and Tommy Doyle for Said, Fer Lopez and Bellegarde.

It made the difference. City had late efforts from Dom Ballard and Tolaj, but Neave's opportunistic double settled the outcome.

Sports.title: Arsenal survive second-half scare to beat Slavia Prague
Sports.content:
Arsenal held off a second-half fightback from Slavia Prague to win 2-1 at the Fortuna Arena and continue their unbeaten start to the season in the Champions League.

The Gunners, runners-up last term, appeared on course for an emphatic victory after scoring twice through Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres in a one-sided first half.

But Slavia roared back into the contest in the second period and gave Arsenal a scare as Wiktor Nowak's late goal from close range set up a nervous finale for Mikel Arteta's side.

Arsenal hung on to claim their third win in four Champions League games but needed a goal-line clearance from Gabriel Magalhaes and several saves from David Raya, who brilliantly pushed an Oskar Kubiak header against the post shortly before Slavia's goal.

Image: Noni Madueke celebrates putting Arsenal in front at Slavia Prague

Slavia had 17 shots in the second half, having only had one before the break as Arsenal were made to work for a result which looked a foregone conclusion after their dominant start.

Arteta freshened up his side with six changes from Sunday's 1-0 win over Liverpool and Arsenal scored their early opener when Madueke finished coolly having been put through on goal by Gyokeres.

The striker added the second with a sumptuous, curling finish after combining with Mikel Merino but Arsenal missed chances to extend their lead before the break and Slavia responded.

A switch from a back four to a back three allowed the hosts to commit more bodies forward and they tested Arsenal's resolve with a succession of chances. Raya's goal was eventually breached but the win sees the Gunners move up to third in the league phase table.

Saliba back in squad William Saliba returned to Arsenal's squad for the first time this season as an unused substitute following his back injury.

Analysis: Gyokeres finding form

Gyokeres didn't score a single goal in his first 10 appearances of the season for Arsenal but his brilliantly taken effort against Slavia Prague makes it two in his last three following his goal in the Carabao Cup tie against Fleetwood Town last week.

He will need to do it against stronger opposition if he is to prove he should usurp Kai Havertz as Arteta's first-choice No 9. But this was an encouraging display which suggests the Sweden international might be turning a corner after a tough start to the campaign.

Image: Viktor Gyokeres celebrates his goal with his team-mates

His goal, immaculately dispatched into the far corner from the left-hand side of the box, will be his biggest source of satisfaction. But there were signs of improvement in his all-round game too.

Gyokeres created the opener with a smart pass around the corner for Madueke and had plenty of other bright moments with his back to goal, linking the play tidily, bringing others to play, and ultimately making an invaluable contribution to a hard-fought victory.

Arteta: Our second half was very sloppy

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports:

"Obviously we need to value that winning away in the Champions League is extremely difficult. We knew that - and we knew the players and the opponent that we had in front of us.

"Two very different halves, the first one we played a really high level - exceptional at times, I would say. The scoreline should have reflected three or four goals. We didn't do it.

"And at half-time, I told them that they [Slavia] are a team with huge spirit, they will keep running and keep believing. They will become more chaotic. We didn't control that at all, right from the beginning.

"We were on the back foot, very sloppy, we gave so many balls away, so many bad clearances. We didn't keep the ball in our structure at all. And then you have to suffer because teams in the Champions League are really good. A lot to learn."

Sports.title: Boro struggle without Lankshear as Wrexham beat Championship leaders
Sports.content:
Championship leaders Middlesbrough suffered only their second league defeat of the season as Wrexham eased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a much-needed 2-0 win.

George Thomason rifled Wrexham in front in the 71st minute and substitute Oli Rathbone sealed it with an 84th-minute header to give Wrexham only their fourth win of the season, coming after back-to-back defeats against Blackburn and Sheffield United left the Red Dragons hovering just above the drop zone.

Boro arrived in Wales unbeaten in 11 league games, but with top scorer Will Lankshear out through injury they looked a far cry from the side who had scored 13 goals in their previous four matches.

Lankshear's return of 15 goals this season was as many as the entire Wrexham squad prior to kick-off, and his absence through injury told on the league leaders as they struggled to make much of an impression before the break.

Kyle Joseph's ambitious bicycle kick dribbled wide before Adilson Malanda failed to get enough power on a header from Sebastian Berhalter's free-kick - the first effort on target from either side 29 minutes in.

Callum Brittain then cut in from the right and beat two defenders, but having done the hard work he mis-hit a weak shot straight at Anthony Patterson.

Parkinson had said his Wrexham players needed to have an "honest self-assessment" after Friday's 1-0 loss to Sheffield United and responded with four changes, bringing in Thomason and Max Cleworth following injury, along with George Dobson and Ben Whiteman.

The response was clear. Although Wrexham took time to grow into the game, they ended the first half looking the more dangerous side.

Right after Brittain's chance for Boro, the lively Thomason dragged a low ball across goal but Lewis O'Brien could not stretch far enough to turn it in.

Cleworth then went close with a first-time strike from range which had Radek Vitek scrambling to push clear.

Wrexham thought they had scored less than 40 seconds into the second half, but O'Brien was narrowly offside when he tucked in the rebound after Vitek spilled a low strike from Kieffer Moore.

Parkinson's side looked full of energy as they harassed Boro into mistakes, prompting a triple change by Kim Hellberg, though it did little to help them.

Boro were gifted a chance in the 66th minute as Patterson's terrible clearance went straight to Amario Cozier-Duberry but he sliced a shot wide.

Five minutes later the league leaders trailed. Cleworth launched a long ball into the box and Malanda's clearance fell for Thomason to lash home from the edge of the box.

Jeremy Sarmiento then fired into the side-netting for Boro but this was not their night, and moments later Rathbone, who had replaced Thomason seven minutes earlier, settled it as he nodded in O'Brien's chipped cross at the back post.

Sports.title: Humphries recovers from food poisoning to win Players Championship title
Sports.content:
Luke Humphries revealed he lost over a stone due to food poisoning but still stormed to his fourth Players Championship title of 2026 with an 8-4 victory over Niels Zonneveld as Dutch legend Raymond van Barneveld took a huge step towards world championship qualification.

Humphries has now prevailed in three of his four Players Championship appearances in Leicester this season, marking the perfect preparation for the upcoming Grand Slam of Darts admitted he was forced him to pull out of the European Championship last month and then struggling with huge weight loss and a lack of practice.

It was also a terrific day for Van Barneveld, who took a huge step towards world championship qualification with a run to his second ProTour quarter-final of 2026, while Gary Anderson moved him into the provisional Players Championship Finals field with a run to the last four.

"It was more about coming back and seeing what my energy levels are like because I've obviously been very ill for the last two weeks," admitted Humphries.

"I've had food poisoning and I've not really moved about a lot for three and a half weeks.

"I've lost a stone. Well I did when I went on the scales after eight or nine days. I weighed myself and I'd lost 15 pounds. Jesus, what the hell. I couldn't eat.

"I'd never miss a major if I could. I think that's the first one I've ever missed. I was devastated to miss the European Championship because I was on a good run after winning the Grand Prix.

"I didn't win the Swiss trophy but I played really good. So I thought to myself I feel like I'm a little bit back here and I can maybe go on and do something great this year and that's a backward step when you have to miss a tournament.

"I didn't practice for two weeks. I had a few throws the last four days. It re-evaluates that confidence again that makes you think you carried on from where you left off.

"To come here and win it takes you back a little bit. So obviously I know the game's there to win these things. But the way I've been the last few weeks it's an unexpected win for myself.

"I've had a good year. I still want to win another major. If it's not the Grand Slam or Players Championship, I want it to be the World Championship.

"I think that's the thing I really search for now. Put my name in the legacy of some of the greats that's ever been."

The world No 3 maintained his charge with back-to-back 6-2 victories against Steve Lennon and Gerwyn Price, before defying a 106.75 average from Anderson to triumph in an epic semi-final.

Humphries produced a brace of 12-dart breaks to seize the initiative against Zonneveld in the showpiece, before capping off a classy display with an 11-dart hold to triumph with a 103.77 average.

Sports.title: Haaland nets Man City winner to haunt RB Leipzig again
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland haunted RB Leipzig again to earn Manchester City a thrilling 3-2 victory in the Champions League.

Haaland netted 12 minutes from time, tapping in from Elliot Anderson's low cross, for his 13th goal in nine appearances against the Bundesliga side, his most against any opponent in his career, which returned City to winning ways after their defeat to Brighton on Saturday.

City made hard work of the tie in which they led twice, having been gifted a first-half opener when Castello Lukeba comically turned the ball into his own net after Leipzig had been on top with Christoph Baumgartner and Antonio Nusa going close.

Gianluigi Donnarumma made a top save to deny Baumgartner at the start of the second half but seconds later the Man City goalkeeper was caught out at his near post by Ridle Baku's smart finish, the right-back tucking the ball in from a tight angle when everyone expected him to cross low into the middle.

The tie burst into life from there with Haaland, a bystander in the first half with just three touches, denied with his first chance, before Enzo Fernandez gave City the lead again, arriving in the box to power a header home from Iliman Ndiaye's perfect cross.

But within three minutes, Leipzig were level once more as Nusa grabbed himself a deserved goal, firing low across Donnarumma into the bottom right corner from inside the box.

City were spurred into their best spell of the game after that, helped by the introduction of Jeremy Doku, as Anderson set up Haaland, who couldn't miss from close range.

Leipzig's David Raum and City's Rayan Cherki still rattled the woodwork at both ends in a frantic finale as the visitors held on to move up to seventh in the league phase table.

'Donnarumma unconvincing again'

Sky Sports' Lewis Jones:

"Manchester City may have escaped Leipzig with three points but Gianluigi Donnarumma is doing little to convince that he is the reliable last line of defence.

"Another night, another collection of uncomfortable moments for the Italian. He was directly culpable for Leipzig's opening goal, getting himself into a muddle when the situation demanded composure from a cross from the right. It was a strange goal to concede.

"And it was hardly an isolated wobble. His handling looked uncertain on several occasions, while his decision-making invited pressure rather than easing it. David Raum nearly punished another moment of indecision when his free-kick rattled the crossbar, with Donnarumma looking anything but convincing."

Haaland: We have to step up

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland:

"I think it is the most I have scored against a club. I have played so many times against them in the Champions League with City and Borussia Dortmund too. Leipzig is a good team so I am happy."

On Elliot Anderson: "He has had an amazing start to his City career and that is what you expect. You have to come straight in and perform. It is not easy to come in, you need to adapt and new players and a new coach, so he has been impressive. Respect."

On Man City performance: "Not sure how many touches I had today, not the most but what is the most important is that I managed to help the team to win. I think we need to step up a bit. When we were 1-0 up I think we needed to go at it, go for the second goal and then the third - that's what we have to do. We have to work on that."

Maresca: We need to be careful with transitions

Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca:

"Tough game in some moments. We controlled quite well but some moments we struggled. Champions League, Germany away, it's tough so happy with the three points.

"They are well organised, they were aggressive and dangerous with the wingers. We needed to be careful on transition. Happy with the three points and now we recover and move on."

Sports.title: Djokovic out of ATP Finals race after shock Paris exit along with No 1 Zverev
Sports.content:
For just the second time in 20 seasons, Novak Djokovic has failed to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals after a shock defeat in the second round of the Rolex Paris Masters.

The 39-year-old, who also failed to make the 2017 edition due to a elbow injury, needed a run to the semi-finals to keep himself in with a chance of clinching a spot at the season-ending showpiece in Turin.

Djokovic, a seven-time champion in Paris, started well against 25-year-old Australian Rinky Hijikata, the world No 83, but faded badly in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat.

With two places still available for the season-ending championship, Djokovic needed a run to the semi-finals in Paris to stay alive in his hopes, but his exit leaves the door open for the remaining contenders, including 12th-placed Taylor Fritz and 13th-placed Tommy Paul.

Hijikata told Sky Sports: "It took a lot. I was getting outplayed in the first set and had to hang tough.

"In the end I was glad I maintained my level and trusted myself in the big moments. I felt I had to take it to him and play aggressive."

Alexander Zverev became the first male player in the history of tennis to lose in straight sets on his debut match as world No 1.

The 29-year-old German, who won the French and US Opens this year, was elevated to top spot in the ATP rankings for the first time on Monday.

However, he blew a 5-2 lead in a first-set tie-break on his way to a surprise 7-6 (7-5) 6-2 defeat by Italy's Lorenzo Musetti at the Paris Masters.

Speaking in his press conference, Zverev said: "To put it simply, he played really well and I played really badly. It was perhaps one of my worst matches in the last few months.

"I was a bit annoyed the last couple of days because achieving the world No 1 status is something that every player dreams of. But then I feel like I'm the only world No 1 in history who has to explain why it's normal for me to be No 1, which I find quite difficult because I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today.

"I don't think anyone has had to explain themselves as much as I have in the last couple of days, which is annoying."

Musetti, a former world No 5, seized the initiative by winning six of ​the final seven points of the opening-set tiebreak before taking command of the second set.

The 24-year-old Italian broke Zverev for a ​2-1 lead and struck again to move ⁠5-2 ahead on his way to ⁠victory.

"It's pretty shocking the level I was able to play in front of (Zverev), who was serving really well, especially in the first set," Musetti, 24, said in his on-court interview.

"It was really close. It could have gone both ways. The key was to stay there at 5-2. I played five great points in a row."

Sports.title: Lions' Campbell has full movement in lower body after neck injury
Sports.content:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell says he has full movement in his lower body after he was taken to hospital with a neck injury during Sunday's NFL win over the Minnesota Vikings.

Campbell was face down on the turf and not moving after hitting tight end TJ Hockenson early in the fourth quarter of the Lions' 19-15 victory on Sunday.

The 26-year-old was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto the cart to a round of applause.

Image: Campbell signed a contract extension with the Lions in May that takes him through 2030

Detroit's entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart.

Campbell offered his own injury update on Wednesday, noting that he also has movement in his upper body.

In a statement, he said: "My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days.

"It means more to us than words can express. I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body.

"I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan.

"I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this.

"I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me.

"The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can't say enough about the incredible care I've received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They've been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I'm truly grateful for everything they've done.

"To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

"One thing I've learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That's exactly how I'm going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can't thank everyone enough."

Sports.title: Muriqi caps Fenerbahce comeback to make Liverpool pay for defensive lapses
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola arrived in Istanbul seeking improvement from Liverpool’s attack but departed with sudden cause for concern at the opposite end of the pitch. Fenerbahce ignited Dirk Kuyt’s interim spell with a tumultuous victory after Liverpool detonated their 100% Champions League record with several defensive lapses.

Liverpool’s second successive defeat left Iraola exasperated for entirely different reasons to Sunday’s loss to Arsenal. Blame was found only in the mirror this time around. It was so careless and so unnecessary.

The visitors led twice, through Trey Nyoni’s first senior goal and a header from substitute Alexander Isak, but Fenerbahce twice hit back quickly and snatched victory when Vedat Muriqi emerged as the strongest player from a pack of red shirts. Fenerbahce’s first goal came from a free-kick, their second from a corner and their third from a long throw-in.

“Cheap goals, messy goals,” as the Liverpool head coach put it. “We knew set pieces were one of the strengths of Fenerbahce. We have been dealing with them well, both this season and today, it has been something we have been working on since pre-season, but it cost us today. The last goal was maybe because they are strong and tall but the other two we have to control better.”

Ronald Araújo resting on the bench offers one explanation for Liverpool’s weak defensive display but does not cover every fault. The visitors enjoyed large spells of control and, despite an anonymous display from Bradley Barcola as the central striker, should never have given hope to an ageing, average Fenerbahce side packed with familiar names from the Premier League.

As expected, Turkish supporters tested the eardrums with incessant whistling whenever Liverpool took possession. They were a test for structural engineers too with their constant bouncing in the upper tier of the home end. Liverpool sought to dilute the atmosphere by controlling possession. Rio Ngumoha was prominent and N’Golo Kanté should have been booked for halting one promising run by leaping on the teenager’s back. Referee Clément Turpin was in a lenient mood with both sides.

View image in fullscreen Fenerbahce’s Archie Brown celebrates their victory. Photograph: Murad Sezer/Reuters

Fenerbahce had struggled to hold up play in the Liverpool half or create a chance of note when Archie Brown exposed the visiting defence with a superb ball from left-back. The pass sailed over the struggling Kostas Tsimikas and was controlled well by Mason Greenwood, before he was pushed over by the Liverpool defender. Neither Turpin nor the video assistant referee deemed it a penalty kick.

The decibel levels cranked up and went even higher when Liverpool took the lead moments later. Ngumoha was heavily involved with a darting run and shot that was charged down into the path of Dominik Szoboszlai. Brown, under pressure from Virgil van Dijk, headed the midfielder’s cross clear but only as far as Nyoni. The young midfielder swept a low volley beyond Ederson with the aid of a slight deflection off Kojo Peprah Oppong. It was a memorable milestone in the continued rise of Nyoni; the first goal of his career at the highest level.

It was also the cue for Fenerbahce to rouse themselves. The hosts almost levelled straight from the restart when Brown’s low centre was turned against Alisson’s crossbar by Irfan Can Kahveci, who may have been ruled offside. They did not have to wait long for the equaliser. After Szoboszlai was penalised for a foul on Kanté, Greenwood’s resulting free-kick took a huge deflection off Jérémy Jacquet’s stomach and sailed past the wrongfooted Alisson. The Liverpool keeper did not hide his anger at Jacquet turning away from the free-kick and leaving a costly hole in the wall.

The second half mirrored the first with Liverpool in control until scoring and provoking a reaction from the Turkish side. Substitutes Cody Gakpo and Isak had only been on the pitch three minutes when they combined to restore the visitors’ advantage, the Swedish striker heading past Ederson from Gakpo’s left-wing cross.

But Fenerbahce again levelled swiftly when Kanté swept in a cross following a corner and Gakpo, attempting to head clear, glanced the ball away from Alisson’s grasp to give Brown a simple tap-in at the back post. “In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate,” Iraola admitted. “It was difficult for me to give instructions and the communication must have been difficult between Cody and Ali.”

Worse was to come for Liverpool when Birmingham-born Brown looped a cross into the heart of Liverpool’s box. Muriqi, a second-half replacement for Romelu Lukaku, managed to hold off three Liverpool players – Jacquet, Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni – and plant a header into the bottom corner. Iraola added: “It’s so frustrating because this is a difficult place to play and we were winning twice. We need to look at how we conceded the goals.”

Sports.title: Viktor Gyökeres the difference as Arsenal claim nervy win against Slavia Prague
Sports.content:
Another away day, another victory for Arsenal. This time, the much-maligned Viktor Gyökeres stole the show as poor Slavia Prague matched the longest winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history despite a spirited late comeback. That now stands at 23, equalling the mark set by AEK Athens and FCSB – formerly known as Steaua Bucharest – while Arsenal are now unbeaten in their last 10 away European trips. After last week’s wobble against Fleetwood, there was no prospect of Arsenal making the same mistake again as soon as Noni Madueke fired them ahead early on after being superbly set up by Gyökeres.

That was his third assist in his last five appearances, although Mikel Arteta will have been even more encouraged by the emphatic finish that had seemed to put the game beyond Slavia’s reach just before the break. While Kai Havertz remains his undoubted first choice, having another striker in form will only boost Arsenal’s challenge and it was noticeable that there was an extra spring in the 28-year-old’s step after his goal.

Slavia’s solitary victory in this competition came in their first-ever match in 2007 and, after losing 3-0 to Arsenal here exactly a year ago, the Czech champions knew their chances of avoiding the unwanted milestone were extremely slim. While Fleetwood’s giant-killing against the Premier League champions in the EFL Cup last week may have given them some hope of an upset, Arteta’s side has developed a killer instinct on their travels in Europe. Not since May 2025, in the second leg of their semi-final against Paris Saint-Germain, have Arsenal lost an away game. The 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich two weeks ago underlined their credentials as genuine contenders once again.

After their exploits at Anfield on Sunday that took them three points clear at the top of the Premier League, Arteta heavily rotated his side again with six changes. Martín Zubimendi was handed only his third start of a frustrating campaign for the Spain World Cup winner, while Gyökeres led the line for the third time in Arsenal’s past four matches.

The Sweden striker finished as top scorer last season with 21 goals and finally got off the mark against Fleetwood with a scrappy finish, although he has clearly been struggling for form and confidence. Yet there was no doubting the quality of his assist for Madueke’s goal after just eight minutes. David Raya’s long ball should have been dealt with by the Slavia defence but they made the criminal error of allowing it to bounce. That was the cue for Gyökeres to come alive as he beat his marker to the ball, chested it down and played the perfect pass for the England forward to run on to and score. Arteta’s reaction on the touchline suggested he enjoyed it too.

Mikel Merino was Arsenal’s hero here last year with two goals and he could have extended their lead on three occasions before the half-hour mark. The lively Madueke created his best opportunity after cutting the ball back to Merino but he could not beat Nazar Domchak in Slavia’s goal.

With Martin Ødegaard watching from the bench next to William Saliba, on his return from a long-term back injury, Arsenal lacked some of their usual fluency in attack. But Slavia were still no match for them and their task became almost impossible seven minutes before the break. Gyökeres exchanged a smart one-two with Merino inside the area before curling a brilliant shot into the far corner. It needed a goalline clearance from Michal Sadilek to prevent a rampant Arsenal inflicting more damage before half-time.

View image in fullscreen Noni Madueke, who scored Arsenal’s first goal, and Declan Rice applaud the travelling fans. Photograph: David W Černý/Reuters

To their credit, Slavia started the second half with much more aggression after introducing their record signing Ange N’Guessan from the bench. The hosts came within a few centimetres of being awarded a penalty when Emmanuel Ayaosi was brought down by Ezri Konsa on the edge of the area. The England defender and Rice both found themselves in the book as Arsenal struggled to recapture their rhythm from the first half without ever looking in danger of conceding.

But that all changed in the last 20 minutes after David Jurasek let fly from long range and his effort was deflected just wide of Raya’s goal. From the resulting corner, Gabriel Magalhães somehow managed to clear two goalbound headers off the line in a matter of seconds. The Brazilian celebrated with a massive fist pump.

Mikulas Konecny should have done much better with another headed chance as Arsenal’s formidable defence was put to the test in the final 15 minutes. A spectacular save denied Oskar Kubiak as Raya managed to push the ball on to the post at full stretch. Slavia eventually scored the goal all their endeavour deserved in the final minute of normal time when Wiktor Nowak fired in at the far post. There were a few nervous moments in stoppage time and Arteta breathed a sigh of relief at the full-time whistle as Slavia were condemned to their fate.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland settles thriller for Manchester City to end RB Leipzig resistance
Sports.content:
Feed Erling Haaland and Manchester City’s totemic No 9 will score. The problem, recently has been a paucity of openings for him.

This was true again before, on 77 minutes, Elliot Anderson crossed and Haaland slid home for a priceless winner for Enzo Maresca’s disjointed unit, Rayan Cherki hitting a post late on.

The win ends City’s sequence of two losses in three games yet the manager has major issues. He has to plug a leaky defence and drill his midfield to exert control.

And there is a shaky Gianluigi Donnarumma: City’s goalkeeper was culpable for Ridle Baku’s first equaliser for Leipzig, as he was for Nicolas Jackson’s winner in the recent defeat at Aston Villa, plus two more in last month’s Paris Saint-Germain loss.

Still, after going down to Villa and Brighton in the Premier League, this win is a certifiable tonic ahead of Saturday’s trip to Nottingham Forest.

City’s quest to return to victorious ways featured an XI of four changes from Saturday’s Brighton reverse. Most noteworthy was Maresca’s dropping of Rúben Dias as Abdukodir Khusanov’s pace was preferred at centre-back with the captain, Haaland taking the armband.

This may have been with an eye on Antonio Nusa, Leipzig’s fleet-footed left forward, Martin Demichelis’ main ploy being to carve City open on the counter.

A cute inside Enzo Fernández pass did precisely this – to the Germans: instantly Cherki was in, his shot curving wide of Maarten Vandevoordt’s right post, a first warning of City intent.

While the 2,000-plus travelling support were stationed in a quadrant to the right of Donnarumma’s goal, the noise came from the congregation behind Vandevoordt’s where a sea of red and white bounced to the tempo of a booming drum. They could roar particularly loud when Nusa flitted across City’s D and unloaded and what should have been a regulation gather for Donnarumma became a fumble – and corner for Leipzig.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández heads home for Manchester City in the second half. Photograph: Matthias Schräder/AP

The Italian tipped this away but those in white soon, again, threatened. A break along the right closed with David Raum’s effort being blocked by Matheus Nunes, the visitors’ right-back.

As can be with this Maresca unit, control was difficult to find and administer for any prolonged passage: Phil Foden twice losing the ball when turning into traffic naively was no aid, the second time meaning Nusa could prosper, zigzagging towards goal.

The Brighton defeat featured close to zero service for Haaland and City’s 13-goal man was again hard to find, Nunes’ loose cross, when the captain lurked, emblematic. So, too, as a sign of Leipzig’s ascendancy, was Marc Guéhi scrambling to clear danger, Nusa firing in the ball from the left, and Christoph Baumgartner having space to shoot marginally wide of Donnarumma’s left post.

“Keep the ball and shift it faster” might have been Maresca’s instruction and when this happened City fashioned the breakthrough.

Cherki speared a diagonal right-left into a galloping Nico O’Reilly, whose instant cross caused Castello Lukeba to panic and inadvertently turn home, via a trailing left knee. City had forced the issue and, now, twice went close to a second moments later.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

First, O’Reilly floated the ball into Leipzig’s area but Haaland’s header faltered. Then the left-back was set up by Iliman Ndiaye’s cross only for O’Reilly to miss with the same part of his anatomy, too.

View image in fullscreen Castello Lukeba scores his first-half own goal to give Manchester City the lead. Photograph: Annegret Hilse/Reuters

Yet as the second half began Leipzig were staring at a fifth defeat in the fixture, having won only once in six previous meetings, all in this competition.

So, intent was signalled by Nusa’s mazy run along the left, his chip causing Donnarumma to push away when he might have caught. This roused the home fans and better followed for their team – but not Donnarumma.

Anderson’s loose ball for O’Reilly near halfway was snaffled by Leipzig, who marauded down the right before Brajan Gruda fed an overlapping Baku.

Now, came Donnarumma’s folly because, while the right-back’s shot was true, it was steered along a very tight angle, yet City’s No 1 allowed it to go in between him and his left post.

Here was the latest goal-costing error from the Italian and one for Maresca to ponder. Yet 1-1 was still a fair result away from the Etihad Stadium so relief emanated from those in black when Ezechiel Banzuzi’s shot hit side-netting only. Donnarumma’s wobble continued, though, as he fumbled another Baku attempt, narrowly recovering.

City were about to show character and quality: Ndiaye’s pinpoint cross from the left had Fernández arriving to head home supremely and Maresca’s team led again. Not for long. For a countless time Leipzig waltzed through with ease and with Nunes out of position, Nusa finished expertly from the left.

After Anderson skied over from close-range, Haaland did what makes him so lethal: net his sole chance.

Sports.title: Valverde’s late winner breaks AEK Athens hearts as Real Madrid twice come from behind
Sports.content:
Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday in the Champions League and preserve their 100% start in the group phase.

José Mourinho’s side twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side.

Aboubakary Koïta sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes before Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners.

Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappé swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde’s late winner.

Madrid have now won seven straight games across all competitions.

Mourinho started with Vinícius Júnior on the left flank, after he missed the team’s previous two La Liga matches through suspension.

The hosts started with huge energy at the Agia Sophia Stadium and it was not overly surprising when they took an early lead. Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois saved well from former Los Blancos striker Luka Jovic before Koïta sent AEK ahead.

The Mauritanian winger shifted cleverly inside Marc Cucurella and thumped home at the near post, catching out Courtois.

The Belgiun goalkeeper saved again from Jovic as AEK tried to make their strong start count. However they inevitably began to tire and Madrid began to take the reins in the Greek capital.

Mbappé fired over and Bellingham netted from close range but was shown to be offside. But moments later the England international scored again and nobody could deny him that one. Cucurella fired in a low cross and Bellingham produced a brilliant flicked finish to beat goalkeeper Alberto Brignoli.

Former Chelsea defender Cucurella tested Brignoli and Bernardo Silva nodded off-target before the interval as Mourinho’s team controlled the game.

Brignoli pushed away Éder Militão’s long-range effort early in the second half and Lazaros Rota blocked superbly to deny the heavily-involved Cucurella.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Mbappe bent a shot narrowly wide of the top corner with Italian stopper Brignoli at full stretch. The France forward was frustrated by the AEK defence when Vinícius turned sharply and found him with a high pass, but the striker’s shot was blocked.

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé makes it 2-2, but another twist was to follow. Photograph: Thanassis Stavrakis/AP

AEK reclaimed the lead in the 75th minute when the impressive Koïta gently nudged the ball into Pilios’s path and the Albania international finished through Courtois’s legs from close range.

Madrid immediately responded with Bellingham playing Denzel Dumfries in down the right. The Netherlands defender rolled a low ball across the six-yard box and this time Mbappé was able to finish. It was the Frenchman’s fourth goal in four Champions League games this season, and his 16th across all competitions.

Madrid substitute Endrick sent Mbappé through on goal with five minutes remaining but Brignoli produced a sensational save to tip his strike against the crossbar.

However, Valverde refused to give up on the three points and in the 92nd minute he lashed home across Brignoli to keep up Madrid’s perfect record.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: West Ham stage dramatic comeback on Scott Parker’s opening night
Sports.content:
Scott Parker’s return to West Ham had had looked like beginning in painful fashion but instead featured a stunning comeback from 3-0 down. The east London club’s new head coach had watched Cardiff’s Jack Moylan help himself to a first-half hat-trick, before a rousing response after the break ended with Max Kilman levelling the scores at 3-3 eight minutes from time. Elsewhere in the Championship, leaders Middlesbrough went down 2-0 at Wrexham.

Parker had been confirmed as West Ham’s head coach earlier on Wednesday, taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday. The club’s former midfielder was appointed on a two-and-a-half year contract.

Moylan halted the initial feelgood factor among the visiting support in the 11th minute at Cardiff City Stadium. His right-foot drive from the tip of the D left visiting goalkeeper Mads Hermansen helpless as it sped into the top left corner. Moylan was then brought down for a penalty – the Ireland midfielder got up to spank it home to the left as Hermansen dived right in the 37th minute.

Within two minutes, Will Fish thought he had turned in a corner for Cardiff’s third – the centre-back deftly headed towards goal, but Moylan was directly behind him and claimed his hat-trick after making the final touch.

After the break, a completely different story. Divine Mukasa reduced the deficit in the 58th minute, finishing calmly over the stranded Nathan Trott after a fine ball over the top from Jarrod Bowen, before Arne Engels capitalised on a mix-up in the home defence to make it 3-2.

In the 82nd minute, Bowen was again the supplier, curling in an inviting cross from the right that was turned in by centre-back Kilman to make it 3-3 from close range.

At the Racecourse, Wrexham waited until the 70th minute to break the deadlock against Middlesbrough, before George Thomason smashed a shot into the ground from just outside the area, which rocketed past a crowd of defenders and through the unsighted visiting goalkeeper Radek Vítek. Oli Rathbone then made it 2-0 in the 84th minute.
