World.title: Ukraine raises death toll from Russian strike on Zaporizhia to 40 people
World.content:
Dozens may still be under the rubble in Komyshuvakha, say officials, noting that rescue efforts are continuing despite interruptions by Russian drones.

Ukrainian authorities have raised the death toll from a Russian attack on an aid centre in the Zaporizhia region in the southeast of the country to 40 people.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the raised toll on Wednesday, adding that some bodies had not yet been accounted for and that more than 30 people may still be under the rubble.

The strike on Monday was one of the deadliest strikes on civilians of Russia’s nearly five-year-long war on its neighbour. It came as Kyiv prepares to attend ceasefire talks with Moscow next week that have been brokered by the United States.

Local officials had earlier confirmed 37 deaths, adding that they estimate about 38 people could remain trapped following the attack, in which Russia dropped several bombs on a school building in the village of Komyshuvakha, near the front line, which was being used to distribute aid.

Ukraine said that a strike then hit an underground shelter filled with people in a follow-up attack. Four police officers and two members of a rescue crew were among the dead.

Zelenskyy condemned the “vile terrorist strike” and declared that it showed that Russia did not want de-escalation of the conflict. He added that the attack had wasted an opportunity created by a ceasefire and humanitarian mission last week in the front-line village of Oleshky.

Ukrainian police have released body-camera footage from one of the four officers killed, showing people being ushered into the underground shelter as the officer receives a radio warning of incoming guided aerial bombs.



People were then seen inside the shelter before the footage cuts to black and silence.

The United Nations human rights mission in Ukraine said on Tuesday that the bombing likely violated international law.

Local authorities said that Russian drones were hampering the search for victims in Komyshuvakha. Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the regional military administration, insisted, however, that operations would continue.

The US has announced a new round of talks aimed at ending the war for next week. Special envoy Steve Witkoff has said delegations from Ukraine and Russia will meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 to discuss post-war security agreements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures and ending the war.

Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to the talks after meeting Witkoff in St Petersburg on October 21. However, previous such meetings have secured little progress, with Moscow refusing to compromise on hardline demands, including that Kyiv give up territory, demilitarise, and guarantee it will not seek to join NATO.

The Trump administration has appeared to offer support for Russia’s position, stoking concern in Kyiv and across Europe.

Zelenskyy has in the past sought to sway the US president by outlining the suffering of his country, and appeared to try to repeat the trick concerning the Zaporizhia atrocity.

“Unfortunately, there has been very little reaction from the world to this insane attack,” the Ukrainian president said in a social media post. “But it, like thousands upon thousands of other war crimes Russia has committed against Ukraine and Ukrainians, demands a strong response. Evil always goes further if it is left unanswered.”

World.title: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat
World.content:
Inside the Republican Party, initial shock at the stunning election results on Tuesday night quickly gave way to anger with US President Donald Trump.

After Democrats won upset after upset in deep-red states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina, some Republicans focused their ire on Trump, arguing that his focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost the party control of Congress.

"It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told the BBC. "This is a disaster of the first magnitude. Nobody saw it coming like this."

Most Republicans expected to lose control of the House and were clear-eyed about the challenge of holding onto the Senate in a tough election cycle that favoured the party out of power.

But some said in interviews that Trump dragged them down with unpopular policies, a low job approval rating and obsession over construction projects in Washington.

"It was just one mistake after another," said Gregg Peppin, a Republican strategist in Minnesota. "Clearly, in state after state, people did not like the president's policies."

A White House ally said public disapproval with Trump over the Iran war, tariffs and the administration's immigration crackdown created a "perfect storm" in November.

"There's palpable frustration [within] the party about how this has all played out," the person said, and much of it is directed at Trump. Anger with Trump "is extremely high".

The BBC spoke to a dozen party operatives, campaign officials, White House allies and others, many of whom spoke on background to offer a candid assessment of Trump's approach to the midterms.

Trump and Republicans had a lot riding on the outcome on Tuesday night. A stronger showing by the president's party - as happened in 2022, when Democrats under then-President Joe Biden lost just nine seats in the House, and gained one in the Senate - would have given Republicans some momentum heading into 2028.

But Trump will instead face a motivated Democratic majority in Congress that is eager to investigate the administration, block his judicial nominees and stymie the rest of his agenda.

The midterms have ushered in an uncertain new phase in Trump's second term and may force Republicans to start grappling with their post-Trump future.

World.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
World.content:
It was the midterm result that many in Canada had hoped for - a Democratic sweep that was in part a repudiation by American voters of Donald Trump's tariff on close trade allies.

"I was doing cartwheels down the street," said Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Wednesday morning, calling it "a victory for Canada".

Tuesday night's result is unlikely to grant Canada relief from those tariffs any time soon, but there is anticipation that the political shifts could create a more favourable environment for Ottawa to get the best deal now that on-again-off-again trade talks are back on.

US voters cited affordability as a main concern heading into the midterms and a survey by the Cato Institute in September, external suggested that about 75% believe the tariffs have raised prices.

In states like Maine and Michigan, tariffs played a significant role in the hard-fought races.

In Maine, incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins clashed with the White House over tariffs.

She successfully lobbied to have some duties that directly affected the state removed, including on road salt, refrigeration equipment and seaweed, but in the end lost to Democrat Troy Jackson.

A similar story played out in Michigan, where state's the automobile manufacturing industry is deeply intertwined with Canada's - and where Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers.

In Ohio, Senator-elect Sherrod Brown, who defeated Republican Jon Husted, called the levies a "disaster" and vowed to slash costs for voters by getting rid of them, external.

Democratic leaders like Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer, now newly empowered, have both pushed to rein in the tariffs on Canada in recent months.

Still, Democratic control of Congress might not do much to move the needle on tariffs. Trump's levies have been largely enacted using executive orders without approval from Congress.

And speaking to Fox News on Tuesday night, Trump touted his "ultimate power" of veto to shut down bills passed by Congress that he does not like.

Some Democratic lawmakers have also supported certain tariffs in the past as a way to protect American manufacturing jobs, and could back keeping some in place.

World.title: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
World.content:
The bodycam footage was released by Ukraine's national police on Wednesday.

It shows huge devastation after the first bomb strike on the village in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, as shocked local residents stare at the rubble.

Severely damaged buildings are also seen.

A voice of a military official is then heard on a two-way radio warning police on the ground of more glide bombs being launched towards Kamyshuvakha.

"Quickly [go] to the shelter!" one of the police officers tells local residents, who are seen walking into the shelter - at least two floors underground.

Seconds later the shelter is hit, and the recording stops.

Ukraine said the shelter was near a local school, which was being used to distribute humanitarian aid.

BBC Verify has confirmed the video was filmed in the same place as footage released by the Ukrainian state emergencies service DSNS showing the aftermath Monday's attack in Komyshuvakha.

In a post on social media on Wednesday, Zelensky said that "nine aerial bombs were dropped by the Russians.

"First, they hit people who came to receive humanitarian aid, and then rescuers and police officers who arrived at the scene."

The Ukrainian president added that "unfortunately, there has been very little reaction from the world to this insane attack", describing it as yet another of "thousands" of war crimes committed by Russia.

Ukraine's DSNS earlier posted another video showing a huge crater left after the attack on Kamyshuvakha.

The Russian military has not publicly commented.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In a separate development on Wednesday, Zelensky said he talked "in great detail for an hour-and-a-half" with US President Donald Trump's peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner ahead of trilateral negotiations between Ukraine, Russia and the US on 10-11 November in Abu-Dhabi.

The Ukrainian leader - who is currently making a surprise visit to Spain - also said his team had a separate "meaningful" meeting in Brussels with representatives from the US, the EU, France, Britain, Germany, as well as Nato and the World Bank about "post-war reconstruction".

He added that the meeting in Belgium's capital would continue on Thursday to discuss "security guarantees" for Ukraine.

Since the trilateral talks aimed at ending the war were suspended in February, Moscow has stepped up attacks as Kyiv virtually ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles.

Analysts expect no major breakthrough when the talks resume in the capital of the United Arab Emirates.

Additional reporting Paul Brown, BBC Verify

World.title: French blood storage impacted by freezer hacks as theories swirl about culprits
World.content:
French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers.

The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers, with temperatures set to rise - but staff intervened to protect blood supplies.

"No health impact has been identified and no loss of blood products is to be reported," the EFS said.

Up until now, only supermarkets were known to have been impacted by the hacks.

Meanwhile rumours have been circulating online about Russian hacktivist groups claiming they worked together to hack one of the systems that was used in the attacks which have affected European supermarkets.

Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance posted that they successfully hacked Danfoss which led to speculation that they were the culprits behind the freezer hacks.

But analysts now question whether or not that meant they were behind the supermarket cyber-attacks.

While Russian groups are not being ruled out, experts say Iranian hacktivists or nation state hackers - or even teenagers pulling pranks - could also be the culprits.

Cyber-security researchers at multiple firms are poring over evidence gathered from so-called "honeypots" to provide clues as to who is behind the waves of freezer hacks.

Three separate cyber-security firms have deployed fake freezer software traps to monitor how hackers attempt to use them for attacks.

In cyber-security, a "honeypot" is a digital decoy - such as a fake computer network or file - deliberately set up to look like a vulnerable target to lure and trap hackers.

By monitoring these traps, security experts can safely study an attacker's methods without putting real systems at risk.

According to activity gathered after the first wave of cyber-attacks, the second wave which hit several European countries was highly targeted.

"The fact that all these fridge freezers were hit simultaneously suggests planning and coordination," says Ryan Dewhurst from Spanish cyber-security company Previdian.

The entry point to the affected freezer software products was not difficult to exploit as they were poorly protected, with known attack methods already floating around online.

But experts like Dewhurst say the hacker or hackers had to gather the information about the devices' public IP addresses to create a target list then take time to plan which methods to use and when to execute them.

"Given the reported timing of when the devices had their temperatures increased, which seems to have been overnight for maximum damage - this is further evidence that the attack was planned and co-ordinated," he said.

Another cyber firm which has deployed similar honeypot tech to lure the hackers into revealing their tactics is Strathclyde-based Lupovis.

It had honeypots which appeared to be located around the world, and started seeing activity 10 days before the second wave of cyber-attacks.

Intriguingly, the team saw hackers scanning and probing their fake freezer sites only in Europe.

"We saw none of our honeypots in places like Africa or South America targeted at all," said Lupovis founder Dr Xavier Bellekens.

"Even pots in Ukraine were left alone."

World.title: 'Most difficult days of my life' for keeper Owono
World.content:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" after the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Tenerife player De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competition this week.

Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on Wednesday, explaining the 25-year-old "wishes to share a few words personally".

"These are the most difficult days of my life," Owono says in the statement.

"I struggle to find the words, and it is very hard for me to come to terms with what has happened.

"I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him.

"I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are all experiencing.

"Rest in peace, Jesus."

Earlier on Wednesday, FC Andorra team-mate Lautaro Spatz defended Owono and said he "would never intentionally hurt anyone" and had been "deeply affected" by De Miguel's death.

Writing on social media, centre-back Spatz said Owono was devastated.

Spatz paid tribute to De Miguel, then said of Owono: "Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

"In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no-one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences."

Players from FC Andorra held a minute's silence before a voluntary training session on Wednesday. Owono was not at the session.

World.title: Israel's president begins consultations with parties after election deadlock
World.content:
In the election on 27 October, Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.

Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That makes them potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.

The role of Israel's president is largely ceremonial, but after an election they have the role of inviting a Knesset member to form a government. That person will be given 28 days to do so, with a potential 14-day extension.

The president has wide discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition. They do not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.

On Wednesday morning, Herzog was presented with the official results by Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg at a ceremony in Jerusalem.

"In recent days, we have heard voices trying to cast doubt on the election results and to undermine their legitimacy. This is a real danger," Sohlberg said.

"One of the foundations of democracy is the ability to have a peaceful transfer of power. This stems from the understanding that the will of the electorate obligates us all."

Herzog announced that he would begin the consultation process on Wednesday evening.

"In order to prevent another round of elections and to build a stable and good government here for the people of Israel, I expect the factions and their representatives to understand that, in the current reality, not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled," he said.

The president also expressed confidence in the Shin Bet's ability to investigate the allegations of foreign interference in the election and appealed for patience.

But he warned that Arab Israelis - who make up about one fifth of the population and often refer to themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel - "must not be smeared".

"I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently. There is no place for them toward any community in Israel," he said.

World.title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force
World.content:
Delhi is once again battling worsening air pollution as the onset of winter brings a familiar deterioration in air quality to India's capital.

The city's air quality index (AQI) - which measures PM2.5, fine particulate matter that can clog lungs - has crossed 300, entering the "very poor" category and raising health concerns for millions of residents.

Breathing such polluted air over prolonged periods can cause respiratory problems and worsen existing illnesses, with children and older people particularly vulnerable.

Authorities have responded by invoking Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), introducing measures to curb dust, vehicle emissions and other sources of pollution.

GRAP is a set of emergency measures that become progressively stricter as pollution levels rise. The latest restrictions include more intensive road cleaning, higher parking charges to discourage private vehicle use and increased public transport services. Delhi Metro has introduced 20 additional weekday train trips, while authorities have been directed to stagger government office timings to ease traffic congestion.

Officials said the measures were introduced after forecasts suggested air quality would remain very poor over the coming days.

Delhi and neighbouring parts of northern India grapple with hazardous air every winter, particularly around Diwali, one of India's biggest festivals, which is just days away.

The festival is celebrated with lights, lamps and fireworks, which often worsen the city's already poor air quality by releasing fine particles and harmful gases into the atmosphere.

The annual pollution crisis is driven by a combination of factors, including vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, falling temperatures, low wind speeds and the burning of crop stubble in neighbouring states.

The sharp rise in pollution follows an unusually clean October, when Delhi recorded its lowest average AQI for the month in eight years.

Experts have attributed the sudden deterioration to falling temperatures, slow winds and an increase in crop-residue burning in the neighbouring states of Punjab and Haryana.

A recent storm had brought rain and stronger winds, helping clear the air. But as the weather settled, northwesterly winds returned, carrying smoke from burning fields towards the capital.

India's pollution watchdog classifies AQI readings between 301 and 400 as "very poor", while anything above 400 is considered "severe". On Wednesday morning, Delhi's AQI stood at 377.

The index takes into account eight major pollutants, including PM2.5 - tiny particles about 30 times smaller than the width of a human hair that can penetrate deep into the lungs.

World.title: Secret police files released in Hungary, 37 years after fall of communism
World.content:
Hungary has opened communist-era secret police files to the public, in a controversial move the government says will help Hungarian society heal itself from the traumas of 45 years of communist rule.

Critics say the move comes too late, that the files themselves are incomplete, and that the move risks sowing division and causing unnecessary anguish to family members.

The date of the opening is symbolic - on 4 November 1956 Soviet tanks rolled through Budapest and other cities, to crush Hungary's short-lived revolution.

"I ask everyone to treat this long overdue publication of documents with dignity and humanity," Prime Minister PÃ©ter Magyar told reporters at the state archives in Budapest.

"Many families will now face difficult information, often related to a deceased relative," he added. "It is impossible to process a trauma without discussion and asking questions."

Magyar defended the move, which was a central promise of his election campaign ahead of his landslide victory in April elections, as the fulfilment of a promise made by those who toppled the Communist party in 1989 in Hungary.

World.title: 2027: APC flags off Enugu campaign in Nsukka, vows to deliver Mbah, Tinubu, others
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State on Wednesday officially flagged off its campaign for the 2027 general elections, with party leaders and stakeholders pledging to mobilise voters across the state for the re-election of Governor Peter Mbah and President Bola Tinubu.

The campaign flag off, which held at Nsukka Township Stadium, witnessed a large turnout of party faithful, political office holders, traditional and community leaders, as well as supporters from across the three senatorial districts.

Speakers at the event described the mammoth crowd as a demonstration of the APC’s political strength in Enugu State, insisting that the party was determined to consolidate its presence and secure victory for all its candidates in the forthcoming elections.

Addressing the gathering, Governor Mbah highlighted his administration’s investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic development, revival of moribund assets and completion of abandoned projects.

He urged the people to assess his government’s performance through its achievements and ongoing projects, noting that the opposition had not even presented any manifesto.

Reflecting on his journey to Nsukka ahead of the rally, Mbah said the ongoing dualisation of the Penoks–T-Junction – Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road had significantly reduced travel time and improved safety.

“I left the office a few minutes past 1pm. It took me two to three minutes to get to T-Junction from Penoks. And it just reminded me of how motorists could have spent so much time, sometimes up to 30 minutes or hours if we did not dualise that road.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“From T-Junction all the way to Nsukka, I noticed that work was going on right left, green, what have you. The contractor assured me that a realistic commissioning date is before the end of this year.

“Another thing the road reminds me is that we have kissed empty Mondays goodbye. Once upon a time, we dreaded traveling on that road because of fear of attack are gone. Today, we have kissed it goodbye,” he stated.

According to him, the administration’s infrastructure programme is not merely about constructing roads, but also about reconnecting communities, expanding economic opportunities and promoting greater integration across the state.

He cited the 40km Owo-Ubahu-Amankanu-Umualor-Ikem virgin dual carriageway, which connects to Obollo-Afor road as another intervention designed to improve connectivity, and now links communities in the northern part of the state, while also serving as a new gateway to the North Central part of the country.

On education, Mbah said the Smart Green Schools initiative was fundamentally designed to transform the quality of learning and prepare children for a productive future and modern economy.

He disclosed that the government had recruited more than additional 6,000 teachers, who were undergoing training at the state’s Centre for Experiential Learning and Innovation, as part of the efforts to move education in the state away from the traditional emphasis on memorisation and repetition towards critical thinking, creativity, innovation and problem-solving.

In the healthcare sector, the governor said his administration was constructing Type-2 Primary Healthcare Centres across the state’s 260 electoral wards, with each facility provided with healthcare personnel and accommodation, including a two-bedroom residential unit.

On economic development, Mbah listed the reopening and operations of the Presidential Hotel, International Conference Centre, United Farm Products Limited, Songhai Enugu Integrated Farm and Sunrise Rice Flour Mill, among other investments, as evidence of the state’s efforts to stimulate economic activities and create employment opportunities.

He also described Enugu Air as more than an airline, saying it represented the state’s readiness to attract investment, tourism and business opportunities.

“Enugu Air represents more than an airline to us. It is our statement that we are open for business and we are open for tourism. We are open for people to come here and live.

“So, in a few weeks, Enugu Air will have a direct flight to London. Before the end of the first quarter next year, we will also have a flight to the United States and China,” he enthused.

The Governor, however, acknowledged that more work remained to be done, particularly in road infrastructure, reiterating his administration’s commitment to its 10,000-kilometre road construction target.

“We are not measured by our words; we are measured by our results. We don’t say things that we don’t deliver on. What we commit to, we deliver,” he said.

The governor also highlighted his administration’s efforts to clear inherited pension and gratuity liabilities, disclosing that the state had approved N32 billion and started paying gratuity arrears dating back to year 2000.

He also acknowledged the role of President Tinubu’s economic reforms in creating additional fiscal opportunities for state governments, which he said his administration had leveraged to invest in infrastructure, social services and employment generation.

The governor further commended the President for federal interventions in the South-East, particularly the establishment of the South East Development Commission, approval of regional gas pipeline projects, road infrastructure and appointments of indigenes of the zone into key positions.

He specifically referenced the appointment of an indigene of Nsukka as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Nigeria, saying the development addressed a long-standing aspiration of the university’s host community.

Earlier, Deputy Governor Ifeanyi Ossai said the forthcoming elections presented an opportunity for the people to sustain the development programmes of the current administration and accused the opposition of disinformation.

Top party members who graced the event include the Director-General of the Enugu APC Campaign Council, Chief Charlie Mbah; elder statesman and former Governor of old Anambra State, Jim Nwobodo, represented by the Commissioner for Local Government Matters, Okey Ogbodo; APC Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Ben Nwoye, who represented the party’s National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda and the Enugu State APC Chairman, Dr Martin Chukwunwike.

Others include Senator Osita Ngwu, representing Enugu West Senatorial District; Senator Ikeje Asogwa of Enugu North Senatorial Zone; Minister of Innovation , Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Udeh; Secretary to Enugu State Government, Prof Chidiebere Onyia; member representing Nkanu West/Nkanu East Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Nnolim Nnaji; Member representing Igboeze North/Udenu Federal Constituency; South East Zonal Woman Leader of the APC, Dr Oby Ajih; Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon Uche Ugwu; and Chairman of Nsukka Local Government Area, Jude Asogwa.

Meanwhile, with the official flag off, the Enugu State APC said it was set to commence a statewide campaign tour, taking its message to nooks and crannies of the state.

World.title: NNPC ex-director launches book on failure of family businesses
World.content:
A former Director of Internal Audit at the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd), Wosilat Adebayo, on Wednesday unveiled a book examining why businesses, particularly family-owned enterprises, often fail to survive beyond one or two generations.

The book, titled “Igniting Entrepreneurship: Your Guide to Build a Successful Business”, was launched at an event in Abuja attended by NNPC Ltd directors, members of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN), including its president, Queensley Seghosime, and members of the public.

Tope Omage, a former director of finance at the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and current director at First Bank Plc, reviewed the book at the event.

Mrs Omage described the publication as a well-structured and methodical text that bridges the gap between academic business theory and the practical realities of running an enterprise.

She said the author made the book engaging by presenting business ownership as a problem-solving lifestyle rather than merely a series of corporate financial calculations.

“What makes ‘Igniting Entrepreneurship’ an interesting read right from the start is how the author frames the mindset of a business owner. She doesn’t treat business as a series of cold corporate spreadsheets. Instead, she presents it as a dynamic, problem-solving lifestyle,” she said.

A practical guide to building businesses

The book is structured into 11 chapters that cover the different stages of establishing, managing, and sustaining a business.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It draws on Mrs Adebayo’s professional experience and her upbringing, particularly the practical intelligence and collaborative strategies she observed in her late parents, Alhaji Tijani and Alhaja Hamdalat.

The first two chapters introduce a framework for assessing an entrepreneur’s skills and abilities, encouraging readers to identify their technical and interpersonal strengths before starting a business.

The author argues that existing talents and ideas can form the foundation of a business, challenging aspiring entrepreneurs’ tendency to prioritise access to capital over identifying viable opportunities.

Chapters three to five examine the mechanics of starting a business, including assessing market size, analysing competitors, understanding customer expectations and developing a business plan.

Chapters six to eight focus on financial discipline, drawing on Mrs Adebayo’s experience in corporate finance. The chapters explain cash flow management, cost minimisation, working capital and record-keeping in accessible language.

The final three chapters address business expansion and sustainability, with particular emphasis on why Nigerian businesses, especially family-owned enterprises, often struggle to survive beyond their founders. Mrs Adebayo discusses how entrepreneurs can establish a sustainable business culture and plan for leadership succession to ensure that their enterprises outlive them.

Businesses Nigeria needs

In her address at the unveiling, the ICAN president, Mrs Seghosime, commended the author for contributing to knowledge, enterprise development and national progress.

Represented by Nyakno Oluokun, a member of the institute’s council, the ICAN president said knowledge, discipline and integrity were essential to building successful businesses.

“The title of this book speaks to something fundamental about human potential. Every successful enterprise begins with an idea, but not every promising idea becomes a successful business.

“An idea may start a business, but it takes knowledge, discipline and integrity to build an enterprise that endures. That is why this publication is particularly timely,” she said.

She argued that Nigeria needed entrepreneurs who could identify opportunities in difficult situations, turn challenges into solutions and build enterprises capable of creating value beyond their founders.

“Nigeria does not merely need more businesses. We need more businesses that survive, grow, create employment, compete successfully and contribute to national prosperity.

“We need entrepreneurs who can recognise opportunities where others see difficulties, transform challenges into solutions and build enterprises capable of creating value beyond their founders,” she said.

Mrs Seghosime also expressed concern about the number of Nigerian businesses that have collapsed, attributing some failures to weak foundations.

She said poor financial management, inadequate planning, weak internal controls and the failure to separate personal finances from business resources could undermine even promising enterprises.

“But ambition alone is not enough. Passion may ignite an enterprise, but sound financial management keeps its flame alive. Too many promising businesses struggle, not necessarily because their ideas lack merit, but because their financial foundations are weak,” she said.

She said the accountancy profession had a responsibility to help entrepreneurs understand their finances, manage risks, meet tax obligations, access funding and strengthen corporate governance.

“Chartered Accountants do more than prepare financial statements. We help entrepreneurs understand their numbers, manage risks, fulfil their tax obligations, access finance, strengthen governance and make decisions that support sustainable growth,” she said.

Family businesses struggle to survive beyond founders

Nigeria has a long history of family-owned businesses that flourished under their founders but struggled to survive after their deaths, with some collapsing before reaching the third generation.

The disappearance of several once-prominent business empires has raised concerns about succession planning, family disputes and the absence of strong management structures in businesses that depend heavily on their founders.

One notable example is the Ekene Dili Chukwu Group, founded by the late transport mogul Augustine Ilodibe. The company, which operated a major fleet of luxury buses and haulage trucks, was a leading player in Nigeria’s transport industry. After Mr Ilodibe died in 2007, the business declined amid disputes among family members over his estate and the company’s management.

Another example is the Concord Group, founded by the late businessman and politician Moshood Abiola. The conglomerate included Concord Newspapers, Concord Airlines, Abiola Farms and Wonder Loaf Bakery. After Mr Abiola died in 1998, the businesses gradually declined, with the newspaper eventually ceasing publication and several other ventures disappearing.

The Henry Stephens Group, founded by businessman Henry Fajemirokun, also experienced a similar fate. The conglomerate had interests in engineering, banking, insurance, shipping and oil, but its fortunes declined after his death in 1978.

These examples illustrate the challenges of sustaining family businesses beyond their founders.

World.title: Methane Emissions: Ogun, FG intensify investigation in Ijebu-Ode, pledge lasting solution
World.content:
The Ogun State Government has intensified collaboration with the Federal Government to investigate and address recurring methane emission incidents in Ijebu-Ode and neighbouring communities, assuring residents that concrete measures are being taken to establish the source of the emissions and prevent future occurrences.

The intervention follows four reported incidents of gas emissions in Ijebu-Ode and its environs, which have generated persistent unpleasant odour and raised concerns among residents about possible environmental and health implications.

In a statement issued on Tuesday and signed by the Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to Governor Dapo Abiodun, Kayode Akinmade, the government disclosed that a joint team of experts from the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), alongside development partners, had commenced investigations into the incidents.

The team, led by the Commission’s Deputy Director, Mr Omonedo Prosper, is currently examining emission patterns and possible sources of the gas, following preliminary briefings by state government officials on interventions already undertaken.

According to the statement, the NUPRC delegation expressed its readiness to work with the Ogun State Government and other relevant agencies to establish the cause of the emissions and develop a sustainable solution.

Akinmade said the state government was committed to making the findings of the investigation available promptly, implementing appropriate preventive measures and providing necessary health support and monitoring for affected communities.

He identified Ijebu-Ode, Ijebu East and Odogbolu, as well as other communities across Ogun East, as areas requiring attention as investigations and monitoring continue.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We believe that collaboration with the Federal Government and research institutions is crucial. The Ogun State Government is resolute in its decision to implement the recommendations of the investigating team once investigations are concluded and to take concrete steps to ensure that the emissions do not recur,” he said.

The government stressed that the welfare, safety and well-being of residents remained its paramount responsibility, assuring communities that it would sustain its engagement with relevant federal agencies and technical experts until the matter was comprehensively addressed.

It would be recalled that following the incidents, the Head of the Department of Earth Sciences at Olabisi Onabanjo University, Professor Ikhane Phillips, explained that geochemical analysis would help determine the composition and source of the gas, while geophysical investigations would establish its possible underground origin and movement.

He noted that findings from ongoing site inspections and laboratory tests would provide the scientific basis for determining the appropriate interventions.

Similarly, the Commissioner for Environment, Mr Ola Oresanya, had disclosed that the state was working closely with the Federal Government to tackle the situation.

Oresanya also called for improved information sharing to address public concerns, while advising residents on precautionary measures during periods of unpleasant odour. He had also assured residents that the gas was not lethal.

Meanwhile, Ijebu Para’po Info Media has commended Governor Abiodun and the NUPRC for their intervention and efforts to find a lasting solution to the recurring emissions.

The group praised the state government for responding to the concerns of residents and maintaining engagement with relevant authorities, expressing optimism that the ongoing investigation would produce a permanent solution.

World.title: Nigerian lawmakers propose six-month jail term for doctors, nurses who delay emergency treatment
World.content:
The Senate on Wednesday passed for second reading a bill seeking to amend Nigeria’s National Health Act to prescribe a six-month jail term or an option of a fine of up to ₦300,000 for hospitals and healthcare workers who delay emergency medical treatment.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio announced the passage during plenary after a majority of senators supported it by voice vote.

After its passage, the bill was referred to the Senate Committee on Tertiary and Primary Health for further legislative scrutiny and a public hearing.

The proposed legislation is titled “A Bill for an Act to Amend the National Health Act, 2014 to Provide for Emergency Medical Treatment Standards and Referral Protocols in Healthcare Facilities and for Related Matters”.

The bill, sponsored by Abdulaziz Yar’adua (APC, Katsina Central), seeks to establish mandatory standards for hospitals and healthcare providers attending to patients requiring emergency medical attention.

The proposed amendment prescribed that hospitals would be required to commence treatment within 15 minutes of a patient’s arrival.

It also seeks to mandate hospitals, doctors, nurses and other healthcare providers to begin basic stabilisation measures, including oxygen therapy, intravenous fluids, pain relief and preliminary diagnostic procedures, within 30 minutes of arrival.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Leading the debate on the bill, Mr Yar’adua said that, where a licensed medical doctor is unavailable, a trained and certified nurse could conduct the initial assessment of an emergency patient and immediately commence treatment.

He said the bill also provides for immediate life-saving interventions, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, airway management and bleeding control, once a life-threatening condition is identified.

The proposed legislation would prohibit hospitals from rejecting emergency patients, regardless of the circumstances, and require them to provide appropriate medical attention.

Other critical provisions

For patients requiring admission, the bill stipulates that a hospital bed should be assigned within two hours of arrival, provided bed space is available.

Where a healthcare facility lacks the capacity to admit an emergency patient, it would be required to commence resuscitation and stabilisation immediately and initiate the referral process within two hours of arrival or as soon as the patient is clinically assessed and considered stable for transfer, whichever comes first.

The bill further proposes that the transfer process be completed within three hours of arrival, except where external circumstances, including transportation difficulties, insecurity or natural conditions, prevent compliance.

To minimise delays during referrals, hospitals would also be required to commence ambulance dispatch or secure alternative patient transportation within 30 minutes of communicating a decision to refer a patient.

The proposed amendment, however, protects healthcare practitioners who document their inability to meet the prescribed requirements because of inadequate resources.

Such practitioners would be required to comply with the referral protocol and report the circumstances to hospital management or the appropriate authority.

Patients who died after alleged delays in emergency treatment

Nigeria has recorded several cases of patients who died after allegedly being denied or delayed emergency medical treatment at hospitals. Some of the most prominent cases involved victims of armed robbery and road accidents who reportedly encountered administrative barriers while seeking urgent medical attention.

In September 2009, Bayo Ohu, a journalist with The Guardian, was shot by armed men who invaded his Lagos home. He was reportedly denied treatment at a hospital because his relatives did not have a police report. He died while being taken to another hospital.

In November 2019, Moradeun Balogun, a 29-year-old podcast host, was stabbed by armed robbers in Lagos. She was reportedly denied treatment at a hospital because she did not have a police report. She was subsequently taken to another facility, where she died.

In 2021, Ebenezer Ayeni, an Ibadan-based music producer, was shot by armed robbers shortly before his wedding. He was reportedly taken to the University College Hospital and J-Rapha Hospital, both of which allegedly demanded a police report before treating him. He died about four hours after the shooting.

In October 2023, Greatness Olorunfemi was reportedly pushed out of a moving commercial vehicle by suspected “one-chance” criminals in Abuja. She was taken to Maitama District Hospital. Although, a panel set up by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesome Wike, later revealed that the victim was brought to the Maitama Hospital dead

In another case, an unidentified boy who was among victims of a road accident along the Bauchi-Jos Highway reportedly died after being denied treatment at Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital in Bauchi because of a lack of bed space. The hospital subsequently set up a committee to investigate the incident.

These incidents and several others have raised concerns about the enforcement of existing laws requiring healthcare providers to prioritise emergency medical care and the need for stronger accountability for hospitals and medical personnel.

The proposed amendment seeks to address such concerns by establishing mandatory timelines for emergency treatment, stabilisation and referral, while providing sanctions for healthcare providers who fail to comply.

World.title: Reps propose fines, licence withdrawal for hospitals that delay emergency treatment
World.content:
The House of Representatives has passed a bill for second reading that seeks to impose financial penalties, suspend licences, and shut down healthcare facilities that refuse or delay emergency medical treatment.

The proposed legislation also seeks to introduce criminal penalties for health workers who wilfully refuse to attend to emergency patients or abandon them.

Sponsored by Akin Rotimi (APC, Ekiti), the bill seeks to amend the National Health Act, 2014, to strengthen emergency medical services and establish enforceable standards for triage, stabilisation and referral across healthcare institutions.

The bill passed second reading during Wednesday’s plenary after lawmakers considered its general principles.

Presenting the bill, Mr Rotimi, the House spokesperson, said. However, ugh the National Health Act prohibits hospitals from refusing emergency treatment, “Nigerians continue to lose their lives or suffer preventable complications because of delays arising from administrative bottlenecks, demands for payment before treatment, unavailable hospital beds and poorly coordinated referrals.”

He argued that the existing legal provisions needed to be reinforced with clear operational standards and consequences for non-compliance.

According to Mr Rotimi, the proposed amendment provides for financial penalties, suspension of operating licences and possible closure or withdrawal of licences for healthcare establishments that refuse, delay or obstruct emergency medical treatment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said it also provides for criminal sanctions and professional disciplinary proceedings against health workers who deliberately refuse to attend to emergency patients or abandon them.

The bill, he said, further proposes civil compensation against healthcare facilities where a violation of the emergency treatment provisions results in injury, disability or death.

However, it seeks to protect healthcare workers from liability where they act in good faith, properly document resource limitations and comply with established referral procedures.

Beyond sanctions, the proposed legislation introduces mandatory timelines for healthcare facilities attending to emergency patients.

It requires hospitals to commence triage within 15 minutes of a patient’s arrival and begin basic stabilisation within 30 minutes.

Life-saving interventions must commence immediately once a life-threatening condition is identified. Where a medical practitioner is unavailable, trained and certified nurses may conduct triage.

The bill also requires that patients needing admission be assigned an available hospital bed within two hours.

Where a facility has no available bed, it must commence stabilisation and initiate a referral within two hours of the patient’s arrival or immediately after clinical stabilisation.

It further requires hospitals to arrange transportation within 30 minutes of a referral decision and complete the transfer within three hours, except where circumstances beyond their control prevent this.

The proposed amendment also mandates healthcare workers involved in emergency medical services to undergo training and certification at intervals not exceeding 18 months.

It assigns the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria the responsibility of jointly developing and maintaining a standardised national emergency care curriculum.

Mr Rotimi said the provisions were intended to ensure the right to emergency treatment is reflected in actual healthcare delivery rather than remaining a declaration in law.

READ ALSO: Closing the gap between healthcare availability and access in Nigeria

“In a medical emergency, time is the difference between life and death,” he said.

He added that the bill would distinguish genuine resource limitations from negligence and deliberate abandonment while strengthening institutional accountability.

Debate

Contributing to the debate, Chinedu Ogah (APC, Ebonyi) supported the bill but called for provisions linking emergency medical treatment to health insurance coverage.

He said emergency patients should not be required to make deposits or wait for payment arrangements before receiving medical attention.

Mr Ogah suggested the bill should require emergency patients to be covered under the National Health Insurance Scheme to ensure financial constraints do not delay treatment.

“They should liaise with health insurance, so that all those emergency people must be insured by the National Health Insurance Scheme, so that every moment they have sucan h emergency, they will not wait for any deposit for them to be treated,” he said.

His contribution was seconded by Makki Yalleman (APC, Jigawa).

Following the debate, Benjamin Kalu, the Deputy Speaker, who presided over the plenary, referred the bill to the House Committee on Health Services for further legislative action.

World.title: Enugu Air begins Lagos–London operation in December – Official
World.content:
Enugu Air has secured regulatory approval to commence direct flights from Lagos to London Gatwick in December 2026, marking a major milestone in the airline’s international expansion.

The state-owned airline also announced that bookings for the new route are now open, with intending passengers able to make reservations through its online booking portal.

The airline disclosed this in a statement issued on Wednesday, describing the approval as a significant step towards strengthening air connectivity between Nigeria and the United Kingdom.

The development comes barely six weeks after Enugu Air operated its maiden international flight to Douala, Cameroon, on 23 September 2026.

According to the statement, the Lagos–London Gatwick service will be operated in partnership with Omni-Blu Aviation (OBA), which has been designated as the operating partner for the route.

“Enugu Air has received approval for its Lagos–London Gatwick route, with Omni-Blu Aviation (OBA) appointed as the designated operator under a strategic partnership.

“Bookings are now open, and flights will commence in December 2026.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The approval marks a major milestone in Enugu Air’s expansion, strengthening connectivity between Nigeria and the United Kingdom and opening new opportunities for passengers and trade.

“This milestone reflects the bold vision and transformative leadership of the Executive Governor of Enugu State, His Excellency, Dr Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, whose strategic aviation agenda is positioning Enugu as an emerging gateway for international connectivity, investment, tourism and economic growth,” the statement read.

Enugu Air was launched in July 2025 with an initial fleet of three Embraer aircraft, comprising the E170 and E190 series, as part of the Mbah administration’s integrated blueprint for a modern, multimodal transport ecosystem.

The initiative is also aimed at positioning Enugu as a major regional aviation hub in West and Central Africa.

Since its launch, the airline has expanded its fleet and route network, with the latest approval signalling a further push into international operations.

The commencement of the Lagos–London service is expected to broaden travel options for passengers, strengthen business and trade links, and enhance Nigeria’s air connectivity with the United Kingdom.

World.title: Revenue: Gov Lawal approves recruitment of technical staff for Zamfara IRS
World.content:
Governor Dauda Lawal has approved the recruitment of additional technical staff across various career cadres at the Zamfara State Internal Revenue Service (ZIRS).

The decision is in line with the state government’s efforts to strengthen revenue generation.

The Service has begun the recruitment process in line with approved workforce requirements and applicable public service procedures.

The technical staff recruited are in the fields of Tax Administration, Legal Services, Public Enlightenment, Information, Photography, and Information and Communication Technology.

The written examination for the ZIRS recruitment was conducted on 11 July 2026, with 484 candidates in attendance. The scripts were independently assessed by the recruitment committee.

Candidates were assessed on their academic and professional credentials, communication skills, technical competence, presentation, attitude, and general knowledge.

After completing the various stages, including the collation and verification of results, seventy-five (75) candidates passed and were selected for appointment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Zamfara State Internal Revenue Service reiterated that the selection process emphasised merit and competence, compliance with the advertised requirements, credential verification, and, finally, fairness and transparency.

World.title: Coalition threatens mass action over Lagos govt’s planned crackdown regarding unlicensed borehole
World.content:
A coalition of civil society organisations, community groups and trade unions has threatened mass action across Lagos if the state government attempts to seal residential boreholes or prosecute residents for extracting groundwater without authorisation.

The groups, under the Our Water Our Right Africa Coalition (OWORAC), said residents had been forced to depend on boreholes because the government had failed to provide adequate public water supply.

In a statement on Wednesday, the coalition asked the Lagos State Water Regulatory Commission (LASWARCO) to clarify its position on domestic boreholes, following its warning that unauthorised drilling and groundwater extraction could lead to the sealing of facilities and prosecution of operators.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that LASWARCO’s Executive Secretary, Oluwabukola Adeyemo, had warned that anyone intending to drill a borehole or extract groundwater must first obtain the necessary permits.

Ms Adeyemo explained that unauthorised groundwater extraction was illegal under the Lagos State Environmental Management and Protection Law 2017. She also urged residents and community leaders to report unauthorised drilling and extraction through a dedicated hotline.

But the coalition said the law exempts boreholes used for domestic purposes from licensing requirements.

It cited Section 253(1), which allows residents to construct or extend wells and boreholes in residential premises without a licence, provided they are used for household water supply. It also referred to Section 259(2), which requires authorisation for boreholes intended for purposes other than domestic use.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The groups accused LASWARCO of causing unnecessary panic by threatening enforcement without explaining the exemptions in the law.

They argued that the proposed crackdown was unfair given the limited reach of the state’s public water network.

Citing figures from the Lagos Water Corporation, the coalition said the utility had 34,424 registered connections, representing about 1.03 per cent direct coverage in a state with more than 20 million residents.

Even with the corporation’s explanation that the connections serve multiple households, the groups said the network reached only about 8.3 per cent of residents, leaving the vast majority dependent on other sources.

They blamed the government for the poor performance of major waterworks in Iju, Adiyan and Ishashi, saying residents had been left to provide water for themselves.

The coalition also criticised Section 252 of the 2017 law, which it said shields the Lagos Water Corporation from liability for damages arising from the failure or interruption of public water supply.

“A government that actively absolves itself of the constitutional duty to deliver water cannot legitimately turn around to criminalise and extort citizens who were forced to become their own mini-water authorities and service providers,” the groups said.

They stated that the situation was worse in communities where groundwater had been affected by pollution.

According to the coalition, residents of Baruwa, Iludun and Ajegunle face contamination linked to petroleum pipelines, while communities along the Lekki coastal corridor contend with sewage pollution and saltwater intrusion.

It said residents in affected areas were forced to spend heavily on water supplied by private vendors.

The groups also accused LASWARCO of treating industrial water users more leniently than ordinary residents.

They recalled that the commission engaged multinational companies, including Nigerian Bottling Company, Guinness Nigeria and FrieslandCampina WAMCO, over regulatory compliance in 2024.

According to the coalition, LASWARCO had disclosed that it spent more than seven years discussing compliance with some of the companies despite outstanding issues.

The groups questioned why the commission would allow years of engagement with large companies while threatening households that depend on boreholes for their daily water needs.

They further alleged that the proposed enforcement could weaken community-managed water supply arrangements and push residents towards private water schemes and prepaid metering.

The coalition urged the state government to abandon plans to privatise the Lagos Water Corporation and instead rehabilitate existing waterworks, expand public water supply and strengthen enforcement against large-scale commercial groundwater extraction and industrial pollution.

It also called for reforms in the management of the corporation to give workers, communities, trade unions and civil society organisations a greater role in its operations.

The groups asked LASWARCO to clarify that domestic boreholes and wells were exempt from licensing and assure residents that their properties would not be sealed for extracting water for household use.

They called on community development associations, youth groups, labour unions, artisans and market women across the state to organise against any attempt to shut down domestic boreholes.

The coalition warned that any attempt by LASWARCO or government task forces to enter residential communities, demand permits or seal domestic boreholes would be met with legal action and coordinated mass resistance.

The statement was signed by 25 representatives of civil society organisations, trade unions and community groups, including Adewale Ojo, chairman of the Lagos State chapter of the Committee for the Defence of Human Rights; Zikora Ibeh of Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa; Okechukwu Nwanguma of the Rule of Law and Accountability Advocacy Centre; and Gbenga Komolafe of the Federation of Informal Workers Organisation of Nigeria.

World.title: Como record stunning 9-1 win against Lens in Champions League
World.content:
Como’s Italian midfielder #30 Mattia Liberali (C) celebrates with team mates after scoring his team’s 7th goal during the UEFA Champions League, first round day four, foobtall match between Lens and Como at the Bollaert stadium in Lens, north of France, on November 4, 2026. (Photo by Francois LO PRESTI / AFP)

Italian outfit Como claimed a stunning 9-1 win away to Lens in France in the Champions League on Wednesday, equalling the record for the most goals scored in a game by a team in the modern era in Europe’s elite club competition.

Anastasios Douvikas led the way with a hat-trick for the side coached by Cesc Fabregas, who have won three of their four games in this season’s league phase.

Bayern Munich beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in the Champions League in 2024, while Liverpool and Real Madrid have both previously claimed 8-0 wins in the group stage. It is the heaviest defeat in the competition for a French team.

World.title: Judicial Misconduct: NJC suspends 3 judges, places 6 on watchlist
World.content:
National Judicial Council

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

The National Judicial Council (NJC) has suspended three judges for one year over alleged judicial misconduct, with two of them also barred from promotion for three years.

The Council, which took the decision at its 112th meeting held on November 3 under the chairmanship of the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, also placed six other judges on its watchlist and issued them a warning.

A late-night statement by the Deputy Director (Information) at the NJC, Kemi Babalola-Ogedengbe, further revealed that, aside from dismissing 24 petitions that levelled sundry allegations against judges across the federation, the Council approved the appointment of 28 judicial officers and recommended four petitions for further investigation.

Babalola-Ogedengbe disclosed that Justice Hannatu Mohammed Kabir of the Nasarawa State High Court was suspended for one year without pay and barred from elevation for three years over the unlawful detention of a litigant for 58 days without proper contempt proceedings.

“The Investigation Committee found that she ordered the litigant’s arrest and detention for alleged disobedience of court orders without the issuance and service of the mandatory Forms 48 and 49 or the institution of proper contempt proceedings.

“It held that the alleged contempt occurred outside the court’s presence and could not lawfully be summarily tried and punished. The Committee also found that the action violated the litigant’s right to fair hearing,” the statement added.

Likewise, the Grand Kadi of the Jigawa State Sharia Court of Appeal, Mohammed Sani Salihu, was suspended without pay over his involvement in reopening a judgment delivered by the FCT Upper Area Court.

The Committee found that the Grand Kadi exceeded his authority by constituting a committee to review the judgment and subsequently assigning the matter to a Higher Sharia Court Judge, who received fresh evidence and delivered another judgment.

The Committee held that the process amounted to an appeal against a valid judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction.

The new judgment was subsequently set aside by the Jigawa State High Court.

The Committee also found the act to constitute a violation of Rule 3.3.1 of the Revised Code of Conduct for Judicial Officers, 2016.

The NJC directed that the most senior Kadi of the Jigawa State Sharia Court of Appeal should perform the functions of the office of the Grand Kadi for the period of the suspension.

For his part, Justice Sobere Biambo of the Rivers State High Court was suspended, with a restriction placed on his promotion, after it was found that he issued bench warrants and imposed fines on litigants in a civil dispute without due process.

The Committee found that he ordered the arrest of the petitioners for alleged disobedience of an interim injunction and subsequently imposed a fine of N300,000 on each without instituting contempt proceedings or serving Forms 48 and 49.

It held that the alleged contempt occurred outside the court’s presence and ought not to have been summarily tried and punished.

“Hon. Justice Kayode Agunloye of the FCT High Court was cautioned in one of the petitions over his handling of post-judgment garnishee proceedings in a suit involving First Bank of Nigeria Plc.

“The Committee found that he improperly entertained and granted a fresh ex parte application for a Garnishee Order Nisi on October 22, 2025, after an earlier, similar application had been withdrawn and struck out.

“This was while other pending applications, including the bank’s application for stay of execution, had been adjourned to November 4, 2025. The Committee held that his action created room for justifiable suspicion,” the statement added.

Meanwhile, those the NJC placed on the watchlist included a judge of the FCT High Court, Justice Bello Kawu, after it found merit in a petition establishing that he granted interim bail to the immediate former Attorney-General of the Federation, Mr. Abubakar Malami, SAN, despite a subsisting remand order issued by another judge of the same court.

The NJC directed its Secretariat to formally request the Imo State Judicial Service Commission to include the name of the Acting Chief Judge, Justice Ijeoma Agugua, in the list of candidates for appointment as the substantive Chief Judge.

World.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
World.content:
Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms.

The search engine juggernaut dominates technology in American schools. Its education apps, including Gmail, Docs and the Classroom platform, are used in classrooms across the country, and its low-cost Chromebook laptops are the devices US schools most often issue to students.

Under the changes Google announced in a blog post on Tuesday, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search will be turned off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators switch them on.

Google told AFP the new controls would be rolled out worldwide, beginning in the United States, but that it had not yet set a date.

The changes also mean schools will not be able to give students Google Search without its AI features.

Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” as AI features are now built into the company’s search engine.

If a school bans AI, he said, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google on X of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.”

“No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he wrote.

More than 150 million students worldwide use Google Classroom, according to a letter Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent to the company last month asking why AI features had been made the default on school devices.

In August, Google opened its Gemini chatbot in Classroom to students of all ages.

Students were shown starter prompts tied to their specific class and assignment, offering guided help or study guides, practice quizzes and flashcards built from their course materials.

The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini.

New York and Los Angeles both announced plans in September to restrict access to AI tools on school devices.

“We are reviewing Google’s announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students,” a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Unified School District told AFP.

The spokesperson said the district believes AI can improve teaching and learning if it is introduced carefully and with clear safeguards, and pointed to district principles requiring that technology support rather than replace teachers and protect student privacy.

In a statement on X, Google said Tuesday’s changes give “schools more choice, not less.”

“We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Google said.

World.title: Nigerian footballer Quadri Liameed discharged from hospital after head kick in Spain
World.content:
Nigerian midfielder Quadri Liameed has been discharged from hospital after medical tests ruled out serious injuries following a head kick during Sabadell’s match against Albacete in Spain.

The 24-year-old initially lost consciousness after being struck in the head by Albacete player José Corpas during the 43rd minute of the encounter at the Carlos Belmonte Stadium.

Liameed later regained consciousness and was taken to hospital for medical examinations, raising concerns among his teammates, club officials and football supporters.

However, Sabadell confirmed that the midfielder had received medical clearance shortly after midnight after further tests returned reassuring results.

In a statement published on its official X account, the club said, “The best of the news has arrived!

“@Qlimeed has received medical discharge after all the tests have come out well and will return tonight to Sabadell!

“We want to thank the medical services of @AlbaceteBPSAD for the help received at all times.”

The midfielder returned to Sabadell by car, accompanied by a member of the club’s medical staff, and went home to rest.

According to reports, the concussion protocol was deactivated after the medical examinations ruled out any injury, meaning he did not need to remain under observation overnight.

Liameed is expected to follow a specialised training programme over the next few days before fully rejoining his teammates.

The incident occurred after Corpas struck Liameed in the head with his boot while attempting to reach the ball, prompting an immediate medical response and his subsequent removal from the pitch.

World.title: Kekere-Ekun to chair presentation of Pinheiro’s 6 legal publications
World.content:
Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun

By Innocent Anaba

The Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, will chair the public presentation of six legal books authored by Dr ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, on November 20, 2026.

The publications, which draw on Pinheiro’s nearly four decades of legal practice, examine critical areas of Nigerian law, including criminal litigation, arbitration, corporate insolvency, justice administration and emerging legal issues.

The collection comprises Strategies in Criminal Trial: A Practitioner’s Guide; Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure; Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria; Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One); The Compendium; and MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN.

The book on criminal trials examines key procedural and evidential issues in criminal proceedings, including the treatment and admissibility of electronic evidence.

Similarly, Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure explores the legal framework governing corporate rescue, restructuring and insolvency proceedings under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020.

Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria examines the country’s arbitration framework, with particular attention to the Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023 and the enforcement of arbitral awards.

It also addresses the growing importance of alternative dispute resolution in settling commercial disputes.

Beyond these practice-oriented publications, Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One) chronicles Pinheiro’s professional journey and experiences in the legal profession.

The Compendium features scholarly essays by legal practitioners and academics, while MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN examines the intersection of law, faith and Nigeria’s plural legal system through contributions from various authors.

The six publications bring together practical legal guidance, academic research and professional reflections on the development of Nigerian law, with subject matter relevant to judges, legal practitioners, academics and other stakeholders in the administration of justice.

The public presentation, organised by Pinheiro LP, is expected to attract members of the judiciary, the Bar, academia and other stakeholders in the legal profession.

World.title: Valverde strike snatches Real Madrid late win at AEK Athens
World.content:
Real Madrid’s French forward #10 Kylian Mbappe (L) celebrates with teammates during the UEFA Champions League, league phase matchday 4, football match between AEK Athens and Real Madrid at the Agia Sophia Stadium in Athens on November 4, 2026. (Photo by Angelos TZORTZINIS / AFP)

Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday in the Champions League and preserve their 100 percent start.

Jose Mourinho’s side twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side, level with holders Paris Saint-Germain on four wins from four league phase games.

Aboubakary Koita sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes and Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners.

Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappe swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde’s late winner.

“Fede has that capability… (but) I didn’t ask him to shoot,” Mourinho told Movistar about his match-winner, who came on in the second half.

“I told him was that the game was wide open, it was being played at great speed… a fresh player like Fede, with his ability to cover a lot of ground, I told him to attack the space and arrive in the dangerous areas.”

Madrid have now won seven straight games across all competitions.

“We fought for (the victory), and with the score at 2–2 we didn’t settle,” added Mourinho.

“It would always be an acceptable result, we’d be on 10 points, but we wanted more.”

Mourinho started with Vinicius Junior on the left flank, after he missed the team’s previous two matches through suspension, in La Liga.

The hosts started with huge energy at the Agia Sophia stadium and it was not overly surprising when they took an early lead.

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois saved well from former Los Blancos striker Luka Jovic before Koita sent AEK ahead.

The Mauritanian winger shifted cleverly inside Marc Cucurella and thumped home at the near post, catching out Courtois.

The Belgian goalkeeper saved again from Jovic as AEK tried to make their strong start count.

However they inevitably began to tire and Madrid began to take the reins in the Greek capital.

Kylian Mbappe fired over and Bellingham netted from close range but was shown to be offside. Moments later the England international scored again and nobody could deny him this one.

Cucurella fired in a low cross and Bellingham produced a brilliant flicked finish to beat goalkeeper Alberto Brignoli.

Former Chelsea defender Cucurella tested Brignoli and Bernardo Silva nodded off-target before the interval as Mourinho’s team controlled the game.

Brignoli pushed away Eder Militao’s long-range effort early in the second half and Lazaros Rota blocked superbly to deny the heavily-involved Cucurella.

– Another fightback –

Mbappe bent a shot narrowly wide of the top corner with Italian stopper Brignoli at full stretch.

The France forward was frustrated by the AEK defence when Vinicius turned sharply and found him with a high pass, but the striker’s shot was blocked.

AEK reclaimed the lead in the 75th minute when the impressive Koita gently nudged the ball into Pilios’s path and the Albania international finished through Courtois’s legs from close range.

Madrid immediately responded with Bellingham playing Denzel Dumfries in down the right. The Netherlands defender rolled a low ball across the six-yard box and this time Mbappe was able to finish.

It was Mbappe’s fourth goal in four Champions League games this season, netting once in each, and his 16th across all competitions.

Madrid substitute Endrick sent Mbappe through on goal with five minutes remaining but Brignoli produced a sensational save to tip his strike against the crossbar.

Valverde refused to give up on the three points and in the 92nd minute he lashed home across Brignoli to keep Madrid perfect.

Koita, who had been substituted, was sent off after the game for apparent dissent.

Valverde thanked his team-mates for backing him when he gets the chance to shoot.

“Sometimes I overthink it, and well, as I always say, I’m grateful to the players, to my teammates, because they’re the ones who give me the confidence so that, in those moments, I can make that decision and have the courage to hit it,” he said.
