World.title: Rainbow Coalition: Tinubu tells Nasarawa supporters to vote only APC candidates
World.content:
Edwin Philip, Lafia

President Bola Tinubu has charged his supporters in Nasarawa State to vote for only the candidates of All Progressives Congress during the forthcoming 2027 general elections.

President Tinubu stated this during the APC Presidential Campaign rally which was held on Wednesday in Lafia, the Nasarawa

State capital.

The president who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima noted that voting candidates of the party would help to sustain the renewed hope agenda of the present administration at all levels of government.

According to him, Nasarawa State had witnessed tremendous developments under his watch as President including the construction and rehabilitation of roads, healthcare facilities, schools, among others.

Soliciting for the renewal of his mandate come 2027, he appealed to residents of the state to give him another opportunity to lead the country for another four years, by voting for him, promising to do more for the people.

“We want to assure you that if God wills and we win the upcoming elections, we will see that we support you for maximum safety. We call on you to vote for all our party’s candidates. The biggest message from the leader of the country is: APC from top to bottom, APC from bottom to top.

​

“We do not want a situation where they say vote for the president and not the governor, or vote for the governor and not the president, or the senator, or the House of Assembly.

​

“We want APC straight! APC straight! APC from top to bottom and bottom to top. May God give us peace and understanding. May God grant us peace of mind. We thank you very much,” he emphasised.

He further commended the Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule for embarking on people oriented projects that have transformed the living conditions of the people for the better.

On his part, the Chairman of the All Progressives Governors Forum and Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodinma highlighted the benefits of the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu, urging the people to ensure that the President returned to power for another four years in order to deliver more dividends of democracy.

“It is our decision to continue the deliberate trajectory of Nigeria through the architect of modern Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“We have come to Nasarawa State, we have seen the developments. We have seen that through the Renewed Hope Agenda, the Hope of Nasarawa State is renewed.

“And we are here to affirm once more that Nigeria is in good hands, that all of you should vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,

“We have worked so hard, we have 31 governors, the party is a family, we plead for peace, we plead for harmony, we plead for a peaceful Nigeria. Support our president, support our governorship candidate, support Nigeria. May God bless all of us as we support the All Progressives Congress,” he said.

In their separate remarks, the APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas and the Director General of APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari expressed optimism that Nasarawa State will give maximum support to the APC to ensure that all its candidates emerge victorious during the forthcoming

elections.

Speaking earlier, Governor of Nasarawa State, Engr. Abdullahi Sule reassured the President of the commitment of the Presidential and State Campaign Councils to deliver all its candidates in the 2027 general elections, said that the massive turnout of supporters across the State and other North Central States, shows the acceptability and endorsement of the party as well as it candidates.

World.title: 2Baba ends six-year album wait, announces ‘Oldest Young Man’ release date
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has announced November 27, 2026, as the release date for his forthcoming album, ‘Oldest Young Man’, his first studio project in six years.

The singer announced the date in a post on his Instagram handle on Tuesday, describing the project as timeless music.

“The legacy continues. OLDEST YOUNG MAN drops 27.11.26. Timeless music, no expiration date,” he wrote.

The announcement comes after months of teasing the album on social media, with 2Baba repeatedly using its title in his Instagram captions.

In August, he wrote: “I’ve lived it, I’ve seen it, I’m still here. My new album, Oldest Young Man, soon come.”

On his birthday, the singer also described himself as the “forever the oldest young man”.

The upcoming project will be his first album since ‘Warriors’, released in 2020, which was his eighth studio album.

2Baba first rose to prominence in the 1990s, composing jingles before co-founding the music group Plantashun Boiz with Blackface and Faze in 1996.

He later established himself as one of the pioneers of Afropop, influencing generations of Nigerian artistes with his music.

His album releases include ‘Face 2 Face’ (2004), ‘Grass 2 Grace’ (2006), ‘The Unstoppable’ (2009), ‘The Unstoppable International Edition’ (2010), ‘Away and Beyond’ (2012), ‘The Ascension’, ‘Rewind, Select, Update’ (2015) and ‘Warriors’ (2020).

World.title: N’Assembly Transmits Harmonised State Police Bill to President for Assent
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu yesterday said the harmonised State Police Bill, 2026 would be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

The state police bill seeks to decentralise policing architecture between the Federal and State Governments.

The bill became imperative following the deterioration of security in the country.

However, Kalu, who made the announcement during plenary on Wednesday expressed satisfaction over the endorsement of the landmark constitutional amendment by 29 of the 36 State Houses of Assembly.

The Deputy Speaker maintained that the outcome marks a historic leap toward establishing sub-national policing across the federation.

He stressed that the bill had surpassed the mandatory two-thirds concurrence threshold required across state legislatures,

Kalu stated: “The leadership of the National Assembly wishes to inform honourable members and the general public that as of the close of business yesterday, Tuesday, 3rd November, 2026, the office of the Clerk to the National Assembly had received reports from 29 State Houses of Assembly on a Bill for an Act to alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and for related matters.

“Consequently, the leadership of the National Assembly has directed the Clerk to the National Assembly to transmit the bill today, Wednesday, 4th November, 2026, to His Excellency, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for assent.”

The legislative procedure conforms with Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution (as amended), which stipulates that any constitutional alteration must secure the votes of not less than a two-thirds majority of all members in each chamber of the National Assembly and receive ratification by resolutions of at least two-thirds of the State Houses of Assembly before presentation for executive assent.

World.title: Breaking: Nigeria’s Flamingos Demolish Brazil to Reach First-ever FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup Final
World.content:
Duro Ikhazuagbe

Nigeria’s Flamingos became only the first African team to reach the final of the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup.

The Hakeem Busari cadet ladies did this in style after they shot past mighty Brazil 3-1 in the semifinal played in Rabat, Morocco on Wednesday evening.

Now, the Flamingos will aim to do better with one more win as they face Japan on Saturday.

One goal by Queen Joseph and a brace by Awawu sent Nigeria three goals above the Brazilians. Winger Greise Kelly however pulled back one for the South Americans in the added time. Flamingos were resolute in ensuring that they did not allow any more goal from Brazil as they flew into the historic final.

The Nigerian ladies were deserved winners on the night as they had at least 30 attempts at goal with eight of them on target, while Brazil were reduced to only four shots for the entire game.

Japan stopped fellow Asians and defending champions North Korea in the earlier semifinal 4-1 on penalties after both teams played out a 1-1 draw in regulation time.

World.title: NJC Recommends Appointment of 28 Judicial Officers
World.content:
*Directs Imo Judicial Service Commission to shortlist Acting CJ for interview

*Hands down one year suspension without pay to three others



Alex Enumah in Abuja

The National Judicial Council (NJC), has recommended the appointment of a Grand Kadi for Plateau State and 27 other candidates as Judicial Officers.

Meanwhile, the NJC has also recommended the suspension of three judges for one year without pay, over various infractions.

The body, took the decision at its 112th meeting held on November 3, 2026, under the Chairmanship of the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) Hon. Justice Kudirat Motonmori Olatokunbo Kekere-Ekun.

According to a statement by the NJC’s

Deputy Director (Information), Kemi Babalola-Ogedengbe, 24 out of the 28 candidates recommended for appointment as Judges came from the High Courts of Kano, Ebonyi, Edo, Adamawa and Ogun States.

“One candidate was recommended for appointment as Grand Kadi of the Plateau State Sharia Court of Appeal, while another was recommended as Kadi of the Adamawa State Sharia Court of Appeal. Two others were recommended for appointment as judges of the Adamawa State Customary Court of Appeal”, the statement read in part.

Those recommended includes; Hon Kadi, Tijjani Jibrin Zololo, as Grand Kadi, Plateau State Sharia Court of Appeal; while those recommended for appointment as Judges for the Kano State High Court are; Nafisah Yusuf Hassan; Halima Yahuza Ahmad; Abdullahi Abdulsalam Bature; Musa Ibrahim Umar.

While Amaga Dickson Edmund was recommended as a judge of the Ebonyi State High Court, the following were recommended for Edo State High Court; Osawaru, Benson Osagie; Omoruyi, Taiye Osayanmon; Adamaigbo, Dorothy Ibhade

Usiobaifo, Festus Osagie; Oiwoh, Pius Idemudia; Amune, Majebi Samuel; and Imuekemhe, Emike Jessica.

Adamawa State High Court has Sa’ad, Aminu; Musa, Ibrahim Ulenda; Giwa, Sadiq; Mijinyawa, Musa Bala; Ibrahim, Japhet; Bakari, Aliyu and Ahmadu, Yakubu.

For Ogun State High Court the following were recommended; Oke, Olakulehin Luqman Abiola; Obienu, Adebimpe Folusho; Daudu, Fatimat Adeola; Kadiri, Rafiat Bolanle; and Osho, Oludotun Olaniyi.

While Abubakar Ishaku was recommended as a judicial officer in the Adamawa Sharia Court of Appeal, Elshama Gwama Dimas; and David Benjamin Pembi are to be appointed as Judges of the Adamawa Sharia Customary Court of Appeal.

According to the statement, all recommended candidates are expected to be sworn-in by their respective State Governors without delay.

Meanwhile, the NJC has directed the Imo State Judicial Service Commission to include the name of the most senior Judge of the State High Court, the Acting Chief Judge, Hon. Justice Ijeoma Agugua, in the list of candidates for appointment as substantive Chief Judge of the State.

“The decision followed the consideration of a petition dated June 11, 2026, by Mr. Bob Kay Njemanze, who challenged the exclusion of Justice Agugua from the shortlist submitted by the Imo State Judicial Service Commission.

“In considering the petition, Council noted that although the State Judicial Service Commission has the constitutional responsibility to advise the NJC on suitable candidates for appointment as Chief Judge, the Council retains the authority to determine the suitability of persons presented to it.

“It consequently directed its Secretariat to formally request the Imo State JSC to include the name of Hon. Justice I. O. Agugua in the shortlist”, the statement added.

Meanwhile, it disclosed that in the area of discipline, the council considered nine investigation reports concerning petitions against judicial officers over their handling of cases, and subsequently approved the recommendation of one-year suspension without pay for three judicial officers as well as additional restrictions on the elevation of two of those suspended.

The suspended Judicial officers are: Hon. Justice Hannatu Mohammed Kabir, Nasarawa State High Court; Hon. Grand Kadi Mohammed Sani Salihu, Jigawa State Sharia Court of Appeal and Hon. Justice Sobere Biambo of the Rivers State High Court.

World.title: Tinubu Felicitates Zenith Bank Foinder, Jim Ovia, At 75
World.content:
.Describes him as an accomplished banker, distinguished business leader

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has felicitated the founder and Chairman of Zenith Bank Plc, Mr Jim Ovia on his 75th birthday.

The President, in a release issued on Wednesday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, commended Ovia’s remarkable contributions to Nigeria’s banking industry, economic development and private-sector growth.

Tinubu described him as a visionary entrepreneur, accomplished banker and distinguished business leader.

According to the President: “Mr. Ovia’s dedication, resilience and commitment to excellence have not only grown Zenith Bank into a banking behemoth but also helped the growth of the Nigerian financial services sector.

“His pioneering role in establishing Zenith Bank in the 90s and building it into one of Nigeria’s leading financial institutions, with significant presence across Africa, Europe and beyond is remarkable.”

Tinubu affirmed that Ovia’s entrepreneurial journey reflects the importance of innovation, discipline, sound corporate governance and long-term investment in national development.

The President also lauded his contributions to digital infrastructure, awareness and inclusion, education, youth empowerment, philanthropy and human capital development, particularly through initiatives that create opportunities for young Nigerians to achieve their potential.

Tinubu also wished him continued good health, strength and more years of productive service to Nigeria and humanity.

World.title: Tension In Sokoto As Community Guards Allegedly Shoot Two ADC Supporters En Route Atiku Rally
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

Two persons believed to be supporters of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) were allegedly shot by operatives of the Sokoto State Community Guards along the Sokoto–Wurno Road on Wednesday, amid heightened political tension ahead of the party’s presidential campaign rally in the state.

The incident reportedly occurred when the operatives barricaded the road linking Sokoto metropolis with the eastern part of the state, forcing vehicles conveying supporters to the rally venue to turn back.

The victims were said to be among those travelling to attend the campaign rally for the ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, in Sokoto.

Eyewitnesses alleged that the shooting followed an altercation between occupants of a vehicle conveying the supporters and the Community Guards.

The operatives were accused of opening fire during the confrontation, leaving two persons with gunshot injuries. The victims were subsequently rushed to a hospital for medical attention.

The development has raised concerns over the safety of political supporters and freedom of movement during campaign activities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

A source said it took the intervention of the Civilian JTF in the convoy of Senator Ibrahim Lamido, coordinator of the Sokoto State ADC Presidential Campaign Council, before vehicles were allowed to move through the checkpoint.

The latest incident comes amid existing tensions between the ADC and security operatives in the state.

The Community Guards had previously been accused of attacking the ADC governorship candidate, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto.

The latest allegation has further heightened concerns over the conduct of security personnel and the need to ensure that political activities take place without intimidation or violence.

However, when contacted, the Sokoto State Police Command Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufai, said the command had yet to receive information about the alleged shooting. He said he could not confirm the incident.

World.title: Cross River 100% for Tinubu, Otu, Says Betta Edu
World.content:
Co-director of the Directorate of Women Mobilisation for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Betta Edu, has said that Cross River is 100% in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and Governor Bassey Otu’s second-term ambition.

Speaking with journalists on the sidelines of the APC campaign rally in Calabar on Monday, Dr Edu expressed confidence in the growing political strength of the APC in Cross River, insisting that the state was prepared to deliver an overwhelming electoral mandate for President Tinubu and Governor Otu in the 2027 general elections.

She described the rally as a strong manifestation of the unity, organisational capacity and political resolve of the APC in the state, noting that the impressive turnout demonstrated the party’s determination to consolidate its political gains and advance the objectives of President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

According to her, the growing acceptance of the APC across Cross River reflects the people’s confidence in the leadership of President Tinubu and Governor Otu, particularly their commitment to development, economic transformation and improved welfare for Nigerians.

Dr Edu emphasised that sustaining the momentum would require deliberate grassroots engagement and continuous mobilisation, urging party members, women, youths and other stakeholders to intensify community outreach, voter sensitisation and political participation ahead of the 2027 elections.

She noted that the APC’s electoral strength was anchored on unity, effective organisation and the ability to translate popular support into concrete electoral victories. She consequently charged party faithful to remain focused, united and committed to the party’s collective vision.

The high-profile rally attracted an impressive array of political leaders, including Vice President Kashim Shettima; Senate President Godswill Akpabio; APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda; and the governors of Cross River, Imo, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa and Edo States.

Also in attendance were the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, members of the PCC, party chieftains, political stakeholders and enthusiastic supporters from across the state.

The gathering witnessed a massive demonstration of party solidarity, as supporters and political leaders reaffirmed their commitment to President Tinubu’s re-election and Governor Otu’s second-term aspiration.

The rally further underscored the APC’s determination to deepen its grassroots presence in Cross River, strengthen internal cohesion and mobilise widespread support for its candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

World.title: AHOBA Elects Ejeziem as 3rd President-General
World.content:
Ejeziem Chukwuemeka Joseph has been elected President General of the All Hallows Seminary Old Boys Association (AHOBA), polling 152 votes in the association’s 2026 election.

Ejeziem defeated two other candidates, Onyia Nwabueze Cyril, who scored 91 votes, and Obibuba Stanislaw Amechi, who received 29 votes.

He succeeds Nze Akachukwu Sullivan Nwankpo, who served as President General from 2022 to 2026. Nwankpo was preceded by Prof. Fidelis Okafor, who led the association from 2002 to 2022.

Okafor is a former Vice-Chancellor of Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University, while Nwankpo served as Special Adviser to former President Goodluck Jonathan on Technical Matters and Secretary of the Subsidy Reinvestment and Empowerment Programme (SURE-P).

In the other positions, Christian Ezenwa Ikedinma emerged Vice President with 144 votes, defeating Onunkwo Chukwuma Martin, who polled 110 votes.

Anthony Echibe Chukwuemeka won the Financial Secretary position with 141 votes against Ezeonyia Sebastian Emeka, who scored 120 votes.

Ezeonyia Damian Chigozie emerged as Public Relations Officer I with 159 votes, defeating Udoh Benedict Sunny, who polled 98 votes.

Other members of the new executive include Fr. Paschal Okokwo as Secretary, Ifeanyi Valerian Okechukwu as Assistant Secretary and Okafor Tobias Obi as Public Relations Officer II.

In his post-election message to members, Ejeziem, who is the youngest person elected as President-General of the association since inception thanked those who supported his emergence, describing the victory as an opportunity to build an association that would serve members across different generations.

He said the new administration would work towards designing an association that meets the needs of members and provides support for senior old boys.

Ejeziem also acknowledged the contributions of former leaders, members of different sets and those who participated in the election.

He expressed appreciation to members of his executive for accepting to serve, saying that important work lay ahead for the new administration.

In his manifesto, titled Let Love Lead, Ejeziem outlined areas of focus, including healthcare and welfare support for senior members, mentorship and opportunities for younger members, strengthening the association, supporting former teachers and domestic staff, and improving the association’s contributions to All Hallows Seminary.

He also proposed health outreaches for senior members, a mentorship programme connecting younger members with experienced professionals, and an AHOBA Business and Professional Summit.

On strengthening the association, he proposed constitutional reforms, improved representation of individual sets and more accessible voting arrangements.

Ejeziem, an alumnus of the 1997 set, is a First Class graduate of Philosophy and holds a master’s degree in Information Technology Management.

He is the co-founder of Deacons Digital Solutions Ltd, promoters of the Prep50 Past Questions Series for the Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) and Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME).

He previously served as president of his set, chairman of AHOBA Shoprite Football Club and secretary of the Centenary Fundraising Committee for the seminary’s centenary celebrations.

He said his administration would require the cooperation and support of members to translate its commitments into practical achievements.

World.title: IEC reports encouraging voter turnout as 12 million cast their votes
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa cast his vote at Hyde Park High School for the local government elections. Image: X/ANC

The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) says it is encouraged by the voter turnout at voting stations across the country, with more than 12 million people having cast their ballots by 17:00 on Wednesday, 4 November.

South Africans headed to the polls on Wednesday for the 2026 Local Government Elections, with voting stations open from 07:00 to 21:00.

IEC SAYS AROUND 12 MILLION VOTERS CAST THEIR BALLOTS

According to the IEC, preliminary figures indicated that approximately 12 million voters had cast their ballots by 17:00.



Gauteng recorded the highest number of voters at three million, followed by KwaZulu-Natal with 2.5 million, Western Cape with 1.5 million, Eastern Cape with 1.4 million and Limpopo with 1.1 million.

Other provincial figures included Mpumalanga with 854 901 voters, North West with 702 1337, Free State with 588 237 and Northern Cape with 299 381.

HOW THE VOTES WILL BE COUNTED

The IEC said counting would begin at each voting station shortly after voting closes.



The counting process will take place in the presence of party agents, independent candidate agents and accredited observers.

According to the Commission, the process will include the following steps:

Sealed ballot boxes will be opened, and ballot papers will be checked for the IEC’s security stamp.

Ballot papers will be sorted and counted separately for each electoral contest, including the proportional representation (PR) ballot, ward candidate ballot and, where applicable, the district council PR ballot.

The results for each contest will be reconciled against the ballot papers received, issued, unused, spoilt and counted at the voting station.

Results slips will be completed in duplicate, signed by the presiding officer and countersigned by party agents. They will then be displayed at the voting station once counting and tallying have been completed.

Party agents will be allowed to photograph the signed results slips.

The results will subsequently be scanned and captured at the local IEC office before undergoing verification and independent external auditing.

The IEC said its Results Operations Centres would allow political parties, independent candidates, observers and the media to monitor the capturing, verification and processing of results.



This is intended to strengthen transparency and ensure the integrity of the electoral process.

“Once counting, capturing and verification have been completed and outstanding queries resolved, the Electoral Commission will declare the final results and announce the allocation of seats in municipal councils within the prescribed seven-day period,” the Commission said.

World.title: Tumisho Masha under fire over pic of marked ballot paper
World.content:
Tumisho Masha is under fire fter posting a picture of his marked ballot paper at a voting station. Images via X

Actor Tumisho Masha is facing widespread backlash after he posted a picture of his marked ballot paper inside a voting station

His defiant act, a criminal offence, came after the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) urged the public to obey the rules ahead of Wednesday’s local government elections.

TUMISHO MASHA POSTS PIC OF MARKED BALLOT PAPER

On X, Tumisho Masha trended over his tweet, which he has since deleted, showing off his marked ballot paper.



The picture was taken at his local voting station, Lyndhurst Primary School, and revealed who the actor had voted for in the local government elections.

He captioned the tweet: “A mark has been made. ActionSA is the only party that knows how to fix Joburg”.

The veteran actor deleted the tweet, but not before it was screenshot by multiple other X users, including the account @CrimeWatch_RSA. 

The account posted the screenshot, warning Tumisho Masha that he had contravened the Electoral Act 73 of 1998.

“The matter will be further handled by the Gauteng SAPS”, the account added.

GAUTENG #LGE2026 | An actor, Tumisho Masha (@TumishoMasha), has contravened the Electoral Act 73 of 1998. The matter will be further handled by the Gauteng SAPS.



You are reminded that it is a criminal offence to photograph a marked ballot paper and/or share it. pic.twitter.com/Bq4fsulklw  November 4, 2026

Tumisho appeared to respond to the backlash with a tweet that read: “Everybody calm down. It’s really not what you think”.

Everybody calm down it’s really not what you think 😂😂😂 — Tumisho Masha (@TumishoMasha) November 4, 2026

WHAT DOES THE LAW SAY?

Under Regulation 38(1A) of the Election Regulations, 2004, under the Electoral Act 73 of 1998, making a photograph or other image of a ballot paper marked by a voter on election day or during special voting is prohibited.



Regulation 38(2) states that it is a criminal offence punishable by law.

A person convicted of contravening this regulation can face a fine or imprisonment of up to one year.

World.title: RIP | Elderly woman dies while waiting to vote in KZN
World.content:
An elderly woman died after collapsing while waiting to cast her vote in Durban on Wednesday, 4 November. Image: X

An elderly woman died after collapsing while waiting to cast her vote at a polling station in Durban on Wednesday, 4 November.

The woman, believed to be in her late 60s, collapsed at Shallcross Primary School during South Africa’s 2026 local government elections.

According to reports, she experienced a medical emergency while standing in the queue. Her family rushed her to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival.



Ambulance allegedly failed to arrive

Election observer Pretty Jwarah said people at the voting station tried to assist the woman after she collapsed.

Jwarah said they gave her water and contacted her daughter before calling for an ambulance.

However, the ambulance allegedly failed to arrive, prompting the family to arrange private transport to hospital.

Jwarah later contacted the woman’s daughter, who confirmed her mother’s death.

The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) presiding officer at the voting station confirmed the incident.

LGE 2026 | An elderly woman has died after collapsing while waiting to vote at Shallcross Primary School, south of Durban. Community members say an ambulance was called, but it did not arrive. pic.twitter.com/9lD9h4r1C8  November 4, 2026

IEC seeks answers

IEC KwaZulu-Natal spokesperson Thabani Ngwira said the commission was gathering information to establish the circumstances surrounding the woman’s death.

Vedan expressed condolences to the family and said the right to vote should never come at the expense of human life and dignity.

The woman’s identity has not been released, while the cause of her death remains unconfirmed.

World.title: KZN police probing theft of ballot papers in KwaZulu-Natal
World.content:
Ballot boxes and election materials were stolen at a second voting station in KwaZulu-Natal. Image: Nokwanda Ncwane

The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has confirmed that unused ballot papers and election materials were allegedly stolen at a voting station in KwaZulu-Natal during the 2026 Local Government Elections.

The incident reportedly happened overnight between Tuesday and Wednesday, 4 November, as South Africans headed to the polls.

BALLOT PAPERS AND ELECTION MATERIALS STOLEN IN KZN

The IEC said it received a report of the theft of unused ballot papers and a stamp at Mnyameni Secondary School in Ward 2, eThekwini.



“Unused ballots and election security materials, including the certified voters’ roll, were reported stolen at the voting station overnight.

“The Commission can confirm that the voting station had sufficient materials to continue operations, except for the voters’ roll, which needed to be reprinted for the voting station. By plan, we do issue a new security pack and ballot papers specifically for Election Day,” KZN Electoral Officer Ntombifuthi Masinga said.

POLICE INVESTIGATE THEFT OF VOTING MATERIALS

KwaZulu-Natal police spokesperson Colonel Robert Netshiunda confirmed that police had opened a burglary case after voting materials belonging to the IEC were reportedly stolen from a voting station in Hillcrest between Tuesday night and Wednesday morning.

[WATCH] Police spokesperson Col. Robert Netshiunda says investigations are underway following the theft of unused ballot papers at Mnyameni Zenex Secondary School, Durban. He adds that a police officer was removed from election operations after arriving in a vehicle displaying a… pic.twitter.com/XjshkQWKNt — Newzroom Afrika (@Newzroom405) November 4, 2026

Netshiunda said it was reported that the IEC’s presiding officer had gone to the school, which was being used as a voting station, on Tuesday evening and placed sensitive materials, including ink, the voters’ roll and ballot papers, inside an unlocked guardhouse.

“The presiding officer reportedly locked the school gate and left. According to information, there was a group of about ten people who could see what the official was doing inside the guardhouse. The school does not have a security guard overnight.



“When the presiding officer arrived at the school on Wednesday morning, she noticed that the gate of the school was open and there were people standing outside the school gate. When she proceeded to the guardhouse, she found that ballot papers and other IEC materials had been stolen. The matter was then reported to the police,” Netshiunda explained.

Netshiunda said police investigations would also seek to establish why ballot papers were transported to a voting station the night before the elections without a police escort.

“Part of police’s responsibilities during the elections is to escort presiding officers with sensitive materials from warehouses to voting stations and back without fail, and the movement of sensitive material is done on the day of the elections,” he added.

World.title: Love eating late at night? Scientists have news to share
World.content:
Love eating late at night? Your late night snacking may reveal more than you think. Image: Ron Lach via Pexels

We have all been there, feeling peckish long after dinner. Whether it’s a packet of chips in front of the television, a chocolate bar after dinner or a raid on the fridge before bed, plenty of people enjoy a late-night snack.

But scientists investigating this everyday habit have found something about eating late at night that could make you think twice before reaching for your next bite.

What researchers discovered about eating late at night

Researchers at Oregon Health & Science University in the United States analysed data from almost 200 000 people to see whether eating late at night was linked to liver disease.



The study drew on three long-running research projects: the Nurses’ Health Study, the Nurses’ Health Study II and the Health Professionals Follow-up Study.

The researchers examined participants’ reported eating habits and health outcomes over a median follow-up period of 16 years.

They found that people who reported eating late at night had a higher risk of two liver conditions: metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), commonly known as fatty liver disease, and cirrhosis, which involves serious scarring of the liver.

Their findings, published in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology, showed an association between late-night eating and a 20% to 30% higher risk of liver disease compared with not reporting this eating habit.

The researchers defined late-night eating broadly as eating after dinner or after bedtime. The study did not establish a specific cut-off time that applies to everyone.

Eating late at night: Why the timing of meals could matter

The timing of meals may matter because the body operates according to a natural 24-hour cycle known as the circadian rhythm.



This internal clock helps regulate sleep, hormones and metabolism. The liver also follows these rhythms, which influence how the body processes nutrients.

Dr Andrew McHill, an associate professor and sleep and circadian physiologist at Oregon Health & Science University, said previous research had found that eating during the biological night could reduce the body’s ability to metabolise food efficiently.

Disruptions to the body’s normal rhythms have also been linked to metabolic problems, including obesity and diabetes.

Researchers are now investigating whether meal timing could also influence liver health, potentially offering another way to address health risks without necessarily changing what people eat.

Should you stop snacking before bed?

The findings do not mean that everyone who eats an evening snack will develop liver problems.

Fatty liver disease can range in severity, and only a small proportion of people with the condition develop serious complications such as cirrhosis.

Lead researcher Dr Robert Wilechansky, a liver specialist at Oregon Health & Science University, suggested that limiting calorie intake in the hours before bedtime might be beneficial.

But there is still more work to do before researchers can establish whether changing meal times actually improves liver health.

One limitation is that the study relied on participants reporting eating habits and medical diagnoses. Although the researchers accounted for several other factors, an observational study cannot establish cause and effect.

The participants were also drawn from three specific research cohorts in the United States of America, so the findings may not apply equally to every population.

Researchers are now recruiting participants for further clinical research to investigate whether eating earlier can improve measures of liver health in people with existing fatty liver disease.

For now, the study adds to growing evidence that the timing of everyday habits may matter for long-term health.

Do you also love picking up a snack late at night?

World.title: Zimbabwe investigates luxury vehicles as Bellarmine Mugabe faces fresh arrest
World.content:
Chatunga Mugabe arrested as Zimbabwe probes two luxury cars over import permit violations. Images: X@Zimblogger

Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the youngest son of late former Zimbabwean president Robert Mugabe, has been arrested alongside four other men following an alleged assault on a Zimbabwe Anti-Corruption Commission (ZACC) investigator during an operation targeting two luxury vehicles suspected of being illegally kept in the country.

The 29-year-old was arrested on Tuesday evening at Brompton Guest Lodge in Newlands, Harare, where investigators were following up on information about a Lamborghini and a Mercedes-Benz GLE 53 registered in South Africa.

According to ZACC spokesperson Simiso Mlevu, preliminary investigations suggested that the vehicles entered Zimbabwe under temporary import permits issued by the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA).



However, investigators suspected that the vehicles had remained in the country beyond their permitted periods.

Mlevu said the Lamborghini entered Zimbabwe in June and was recorded as having exited on 12 July.

The Mercedes-Benz reportedly entered the country on the same day and was recorded as having left for South Africa on 10 October.

Despite the recorded departures, ZACC investigators found both vehicles at the Harare lodge on Tuesday.

An official was allegedly assaulted during the operation, prompting the commission to report the incident to the police.

National police spokesperson Commissioner Paul Nyathi confirmed the arrest of Chatunga and four other suspects: Munashe Mubawu, 43, Terrence Johannes Chinyemba, 42, Fredson Peter, 33, and Solomon Pamire, 34.



The five face assault charges and were expected to appear in court on Thursday.

Their alleged individual roles in the suspected vehicle smuggling case have not been established.

What Zimbabwe’s temporary import permit rules say

ZIMRA allows qualifying visitors to bring foreign-registered private vehicles into Zimbabwe under Temporary Import Permits (TIPs).

However, the permits come with strict conditions governing how long vehicles can remain in the country.

According to ZIMRA, vehicles must generally be exported when the permit holder first leaves Zimbabwe, within three months of importation, or within any shorter period specified by the authority.

Extensions may be granted under certain circumstances, but vehicles cannot simply remain in the country indefinitely.

ZIMRA has also warned that vehicles breaching temporary importation conditions may be seized.

In October 2026, the authority introduced enhanced controls requiring additional documentation and verification for certain applications, with permits ordinarily limited to 30 days.

Chatunga’s previous encounters with police

The latest arrest adds to Chatunga’s previous encounters with law enforcement in Zimbabwe and South Africa.

He was previously arrested in South Africa following a shooting incident at his Johannesburg residence in which his gardener was wounded.

He was subsequently deported to Zimbabwe after admitting to being in the country illegally.

He has also faced allegations involving cannabis possession and an incident at a police checkpoint in Bubi, near Beitbridge.

MIDRAND - Voting stations for the 2026 local government elections closed at 9 pm on Wednesday.

But the work of the Electoral Commission (IEC) continues.

Briefing the media on Wednesday night, IEC Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo outlined the nitty-gritty.

Once polls are closed, ballot papers will then be counted at the voting stations in the presence of party agents, independent agents and accredited observers.

“Sealed ballot boxes will be opened, and ballot papers are checked for the official security stamp of the Commission. Ballots are then sorted out and counted separately for each ballot type, namely whether it's a PR ballot, vote ballot and, where applicable the voting district PR ballot.”

Once the counting has been completed, officials will then move to reconcile results of each contest against the ballot papers received, issued, and those that remain unused at each station.

“That process must reconcile every ballot that was received by the station. Result slips are completed in duplicate, signed by the Presiding Officer and countersigned by party agents before being displayed at the station as soon as counting is complete."

Before the IEC can declare the election results, they are then subsequently scanned and captured at the local office of the Commission and subjected to verification and independent external auditing.

World.title: World leaders hope for reset after US midterms
World.content:
PARIS - World leaders voiced hopes for a reset with the United States on Wednesday after voters delivered a huge midterm election defeat to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

The Democrats seized control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, giving them the power to block legislation and hold up Trump's appointments.

Germany

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said he hoped to see new initiatives to end the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.

"With their majority in both chambers of Congress, the Democratic Party will likely seek to shift the political course in the United States," Wadephul said.

Through cooperation between the United States and Europe, "there may be a new opportunity to launch a fresh initiative" to resolve conflicts, he said.

Spain

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said Trump's defeat showed that the global far-right was on the wane.

"It happened in Brazil. It just happened in the US. And it will soon happen in Spain," the socialist leader said, with elections looming later this month.

The far-right wave is "no longer growing, it is unravelling," he added.

Russia

Russia hopes Trump will continue his "peacemaking efforts" after the midterm elections, the Kremlin said.

"President Trump continues to exercise his powers. We sincerely hope that he will also continue his peacemaking efforts," spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

South Africa

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the result could thaw strained ties between Pretoria and Washington.

"We're hoping that on a bilateral basis, there will be a coming together of minds where we will find a proper path forward on geopolitics as well as on trade matters and investment matters," he said.

He added that he hoped the result would "introduce a new era in world relations".

EU

The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas voiced hope the new US Congress would support Ukraine and ramp up pressure on Russia.

"I hope that the new Congress... will continue supporting Ukraine and also putting more pressure on Russia," she said, adding that Europe and the United States "are much stronger together" in pushing Moscow to end its war.

UK

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the result was an opportunity for the world to "unite" around resolving cost-of-living issues.

"President Trump has accepted the results, and I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that's the cost of living," Burnham said.

World.title: IEC puts backup power measures in place ahead of vote counting

Briefing the media on Wednesday, just a few hours before voting stations close at 9pm, IEC Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo said generators and alternative lighting facilities have been made available to voting stations in areas that have experienced power outages.

READ | Elections 2026 | Voices from the ground

Mamabolo has praised the turnout of voters for the 2026 local government elections, with its preliminary estimates recording approximately 12 million voters who have cast their votes across the country as of 5pm today.

But even so, with voting scheduled to close at 9pm, Mamabolo has urged eligible voters who have not yet cast their ballots to make their way to their registered voting stations.

World.title: eThekwini wards to watch as MK Party challenges established political loyalties
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - With only a few hours left before the 2026 local government elections close, eNCA Elections Analyst Wayne Sussman turned his attention to three key wards in eThekwini

According to Sussman, the results in Ward 26 near Durban city centre, Ward 86 in the Umlazi area and Ward 99 in the Umkomaas, Magabeni area could offer a picture of how political support has shifted since the 2021 local government elections.

He says the three wards are particularly interesting given the emergence of the uMkhonto weSizwe Party during the 2024 general elections.

First, he looked at Ward 26, which he describes as a closely contested inner-city ward.

Sussman notes that in 2021, just a few votes separated the ANC and DA in this ward.

READ | Ekurhuleni power battle: Can the MK Party weaken ANC support?

However, since the emergence of the MK Party, support has shifted significantly, with the Jacob Zuma-led MK Party leading.

He says the result makes him wonder whether the MK Party will pick up this ward.

“Can the ANC recover support and retain the ward, or will the Democratic Alliance come in here and win? This is going to be a fascinating contest to watch in the heart of Durban tonight,” he questions.

Turning to Ward 86, long an ANC stronghold, Sussman notes that in 2021 the ANC led and was tailed by EFF and IFP

But by 2024, the MK Party rattled the ground once again.

World.title: Presidency condemns political murders
World.content:
MIDRAND - The Director-General in the Presidency, Phindile Baleni, has condemned political killings.

She warned that police will deal with those responsible for these violent crimes.

“It is quite sad that certain people believe that their best way to express their political opinions is by killing others. “The democracy in the country enables us to choose our leaders at different points, and there are ways to allow for democratic principal transition between the different administrations or when people step down from positions,” she said.

Baleni's remarks come amid growing concerns about political killings. Natjoints Co-Chairperson Tebello Mosikili said they recorded 20 murders involving political representatives, party members and supporters, with seven arrests having been effected.

Mosikili indicated that SAPS has prioritised these investigations.

Baleni called on South Africans to be responsible, and if one wants to express an opinion, this must be done through established mechanisms and public participation.

World.title: CheckPoint Podcast | Is South Africa's Foreign Policy Failing Its Economy? Thembisa Fakude | 4 November 2026
World.content:
The Strategy Meeting Is Not The Strategy

Organisations often mistake activity for progress. Meetings are held, partnerships announced and influential relationships cultivated. The calendar fills up, but the fundamental question remains unanswered: what has actually changed?

This problem extends beyond business. It also affects governments, public institutions and international diplomacy.

During a CheckPoint: The Podcast conversation with Nkepile Mabuse, international relations analyst Thembisa Fakude questioned South Africa's clarity about its national interests.

“We don't know what we want.”

It is a provocative assessment, but it exposes a leadership problem that exists in organisations of every size.

The Missing Link Between Ambition And Execution

Strategy should establish what an institution intends to achieve, which resources it will commit and how success will be measured.

Yet organisations frequently separate those responsibilities.

Leadership teams establish ambitious objectives. Relationship managers secure partnerships. Operational departments are then expected to produce results without always having the necessary resources, authority or shared understanding of the intended outcome.

The result is an execution gap.

Everyone can demonstrate activity, but nobody can confidently establish whether the institution has moved closer to its objectives.

Every Partnership Needs An Owner

International relationships provide a useful illustration.

A diplomatic agreement may create an opportunity for investment or trade. But unless someone is responsible for converting that opportunity into a practical outcome, its value may remain unrealised.

Businesses face the same challenge when they announce strategic alliances without defining commercial responsibilities.

A credible partnership requires more than goodwill. It needs measurable objectives, clear ownership, delivery milestones and a process for evaluating performance.

These requirements should be established before success is announced, not after disappointment becomes obvious.

Accountability Begins Before The Announcement

The strongest organisations do not measure success by the number of initiatives they launch.

They examine whether those initiatives produce the intended results.

That means asking difficult questions before committing resources. What problem are we solving? Who benefits? What must change operationally? Who is accountable if nothing happens?

Fakude's criticism of South African foreign policy provides a useful reminder that external influence cannot compensate for internal uncertainty.

The lesson for leaders is straightforward.

If an organisation cannot explain what it wants from a relationship, it is unlikely to recognise whether that relationship is delivering.

Strategy is not demonstrated by access to important people or participation in important conversations.

It is demonstrated by the decisions, capabilities and measurable outcomes that follow.

Reference

· CheckPoint: The Podcast, Nkepile Mabuse and Thembisa Fakude, 04 November 2026.

Catch up on all CheckPoint Podcast episodes here: ⁠https://www.enca.com/checkpoint-podcast-0

World.title: In Trump's shoes: How cost of living fuels fury among relentless voters
World.content:
US President Donald Trump and President William Ruto attend the signing ceremony of a peace deal between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo at the United States Institute of Peace in Washington, DC, on December 4, 2025. [AFP]

The honeymoon for President Donald Trump, the second US president to serve two non-consecutive terms, ended in great disarray as the Democratic Party took control of both chambers of Congress in the mid-terms in stunning version on Wednesday, with the last two years of Trump’s presidency likely to be a horrible nightmare for him and for Republicans.

Gaining 7 seats in the Senate for a total of 54, well above the 50 needed to acquire a majority, and securing an extra 25 for a total of 228, comfortably above the 218-seat mark that sets a majority in the 435-member chamber, the Democrats will have the capacity to frustrate Trump’s policies which have often gone unchallenged, in what many feel is a breath of fresh air in US politic.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.
