World.title: Pantheon Data Centre Will Consume as Much Electricity as a Third of Croatia
World.content:
November the 4th, 2026 – The deeply contested Pantheon data centre in Topusko is edging closer to the start of construction despite most being against the facility that will use as much electricity as a third of Croatia.

Representatives of the Croatian Transmission System Operator (HOPS) and the investor in the Pantheon AI data centre in Topusko announced at a panel of the Green Energy Fair that they expect the contract for connection to the electricity transmission network to be signed in November. Poslovni reports that at the panel dedicated to data centres as new challenges for the electricity system, Pantheon project manager Mario Gudelj recalled that HOPS had previously accepted Pantheon’s study for connection to the network back in July this year, and that the signing of the contract is expected in November.

many are against pantheon’s construction

The contract with HOPS will enable the future controversial data centre in Topusko to receive a stable power supply of 1 GW (gigawatt) or 1,000 MW (megawatts). HOPS connection manager Igor Šumonja said that the current system load for all of Croatia stands at around 2,000 to 3,000 MW, and that connecting such a consumer will increase the load by an entire third. This is deeply concerning to the vast majority who are against the construction of harmful and environmentally catastrophic data centres.

“HOPS has approached this seriously and we know that it requires the construction of four new powerful 400-kilovolt transmission lines approximately 300 kilometres long, and the investor will build and pay all the costs of connecting to the network and nothing will be borne by HOPS and the system. In addition to them, we have another 1,600 to 1,700 requests for data centres, but of much lower power than Pantheon,” Šumonja claimed.

As the start of construction of this largest data centre campus in Croatia and the region is planned for 2027, and the start of operations in 2029, Gudelj believes that the contract with HOPS will be signed soon, as well as that the spatial plan in Sisak-Moslavina County will be adopted and the environmental impact study accepted, because without that they cannot start working. “The spatial plan is a more complex story than HOPS because there have been amendments and additions to that plan, for which a public discussion is now underway, but we believe that all those processes in the county will be completed by February or the beginning of March,” Gudelj said.

claims that “pantheon is so different” fall on the deaf ears of an increasingly concerned public

When asked whether he fears that something could ‘get stuck’ at that discussion and because of the citizens regarding this project, he replied that they are not afraid because Pantheon is “so different and brings so many benefits to society, the state and the local community that there is no reason for it to get stuck”, and that in all public appearances he emphasises that they cannot take a single step without satisfying both the residents and the requirements binding from the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

Collaborator on the project Antonio Gužvinec from the company Parsec Lab explained that this future AI campus will also be powered by energy from a solar power plant and battery systems, because the power density of the ‘cabinets’ with servers in them is significantly higher than in ordinary data centres, which is why they also need stronger cooling systems since the processors work practically constantly.

Luka Majić, product manager of the Croatian representative office of the American company Vertiv Croatia, which deals with data centre infrastructure and is also a collaborator on the project, highlighted the growing interest in investments in data centres due to the growth in demand for AI. He announced that in Croatia the company will increase the number of employees by 200, from the current 650, because they have become Vertiv’s global centre of expertise. Gudelj further emphasised that Pantheon will allegedly not buy energy that is currently consumed on the Croatian market.

Regarding the question of whether all this will lead to an increase in the price of electricity in Croatia, Šumonja from HOPS said that they do not set prices, so he cannot say anything about that either. On the question of cooling the centre, Majić from Vertiv said that in data centres a water cooling system is completely standard and that there are several models that are applied for this.

“pantheon won’t expect the topusko spa water” – residents don’t believe it

Gudelj repeated his earlier claims that Pantheon will not affect the waters in the Topusko spas, nor the water supply system. He also repeated the announcement that there will be “around 3,500 jobs” in Pantheon, of which 1,500 will be from the beginning due to construction and other jobs, including three shifts of firefighters that they will pay for, and their goal is for at least around 500 employees to also live in Topusko, which is why they plan to build apartments as well.

“All in all, Pantheon’s footprint on the local community in the county area and beyond, economically, sociologically and democratically, is much greater than the damage to the environment will be. Care will be taken to improve the roads, noise, so that we do not burden the water chemically and so on,” Gudelj claimed, but many aren’t buying his words. He also emphasised that Pantheon will apparently pay HOPS around 80 million euros annually for network fees, which is practically HOPS’s annual investment cycle, to which Šumonja from HOPS said that before Pantheon enters the network, they will test them for at least two years, as well as other customers.

World.title: Dubrovnik Airport Scandal – Wrong Pipes Used, €22 Million Must be Returned
World.content:
November the 3rd, 2026 – The Dubrovnik Airport scandal is being hailed as among the worst ever involving EU cash and an airport, with the wrong piping installed and a massive €22 million now needing to be returned.

Dubrovnik Airport must return €22 euros received of European Union funds after the uncovering of a scandal like few could have imagined. Index reports that the decision was made due to established irregularities in public procurement procedures during the airport reconstruction project, which began a whole thirteen years ago and was one of the largest infrastructure projects co-financed with EU funds.

problematic procurement processes and unusable system…

The total value of the reconstruction amounted to an enormous €230 million, of which almost €160 million was non-refundable The total amount that must now be returned represents around 14 percent of those funds. “It’s an amount of approximately €22 million that must be returned. That’s about 14 percent of the non-refundable funds provided by the European Union. The problem related to public procurement procedures and the signing of the main contracts, mostly in the period from 2013 to 2017,” explained Viktor Šober, director of Dubrovnik Airport.

Among the disputed public procurement procedures, the one for the aircraft fuel supply system stands out in particular. The problem arose because the wrong pipes were installed during construction. “We engaged a serious international company specialised in underground hydrant systems for fuel delivery to the apron. They are not optimistic,” Šober added. Dubrovnik Mayor Mato Franković confirmed the scale of the problem. “The fact is that ten public procurements were penalised, and instead of adequate pipes for aviation fuel, sewage pipes were installed, which is why the entire system is not operational,” Franković said.

information was received about the case in 2022…

The European Public Prosecutor’s Office also commented on the genuinely somewhat shocking Dubrovnik Airport scandal case. They explained that they received information from national authorities back in 2022, but decided not to take over the case because the reported facts were outside their temporal jurisdiction.

Former airport director Roko Tolić, now executive director of Airports of Montenegro, also reacted to the scandal. He claims that the fuel system was not constructed during his term. “The building permit for that facility was issued on the 3rd of September 2018, seven whole months after my departure, and the works were carried out from September 2018 and completed during 2019. Whether the installed pipes are in accordance with the permit and the project is determined by a technical inspection before the competent authority. I cannot speak about the pipes and the as-built condition from my own knowledge because I did not participate in those works,” Tolić said. The management of Dubrovnik Airport emphasises that this is a serious issue for them, given that they invested significant funds in a system that they ultimately cannot use at all.

World.title: First Snow of Winter Arrives – 20 cm Falls in Highest Croatian Settlement!
World.content:
November the 3rd, 2026 – The very first snow of the winter has arrived, with around 20 cm falling and settling in the highest Croatian settlement.

In the highest parts of Croatia, the very first snow of the winter season has fallen. Approximately 12 centimetres were measured on Zavižan, and a snow cover also formed on Platak near Rijeka and in mountainous Gorski Kotar. Index reports that the highest amount of snow, currently measuring at around 20 centimetres, has been measured in Begovo Razdolje, the highest inhabited settlement in all of Croatia.

Because of the fresh snowfall, the residents of Begovo Razdolje had to take up their shovels a little later than usual and clear the approaches to their houses and driveways. “I’m 82 years old, so this comes as recreation for me. A bit of physical activity and fresh air does me good,” local resident Franjo Štritof told Nova TV. For the twenty or so permanent residents of the settlement, snow at the beginning of November at 1,078 metres above sea level is no surprise. “Everyone chooses whether this is for them or not, but life here is good,” says farm owner Bojan Francišković.

During the day, the air temperature hovered around three degrees Celsius, meaning that eventually, the snow turned into rain. “Now, it’s raining a little and snowing a little, and at night, pure snow falls,” Franjo Štritof explained. According to current forecasts, the first snow of the season won’t stay until the weekend. “This is nothing new. Usually it turns white like this in the middle of October, lasts for about a day or two, and after that the weather improves again and autumn is still alright for a while,” concluded Bojan Francišković.

World.title: HDZ Candidate and Hospital Commission Member Arrested in Corruption Probe
World.content:
November the 3rd, 2026 – Vladimir Ovčarić, HDZ local candidate and head of the Technical and Service Activities Department of the Zabok General Hospital and Croatian Veterans’ Hospital, has been arrested in a wider corruption probe.

Ovčarić is also particularly active in local politics and holds positions in the Krapina Hunting Society. Index reports that as was shown by the official election results for Krapina, HDZ’s Ovčarić was the lead candidate of the joint HDZ and Zagorje Party list for the Podgora Local Committee in the elections for local committee councils back in May 2025.

politics, hunting and hospital fire brigade president

His list won 291 votes, or 42.61 percent, and three seats on the seven-member local committee council. Alongside Ovčarić, Slavko Vincelj and Marijo Družinec were elected. At the constitutive session held on 9 June 2025, Ovčarić was elected deputy president of the Podgora Local Committee Council, while Tomislav Pernjek from the SDP list was elected president.

Ovčarić is also active in the Krapina Hunting Society. According to publicly available data, he is listed as the society’s secretary and as one of the persons authorised to represent it. On the society’s official website he also appears among the members of the executive board and is listed on the register of full members of the society. Ovčarić was previously president of the Volunteer Fire Brigade of the Zabok General Hospital. His name appears in the data of the Firefighting Association of Krapina-Zagorje County, while publicly available data show that this function ended on the 11th of March 2020. He has worked at the hospital for very many years. Back in 2012, he was mentioned as head of the technical and service department when he took part with the police in a project to place anti-burglary warnings for cars in the hospital car park.

he was on the commission for the hospital kiosk tender

Particularly interesting are also the official minutes of the hospital’s Governing Board. From the minutes of the session held on the 10th of October 2024 it emerges that Ovčarić was appointed to a three-member commission for the implementation of a public tender for the lease of hospital premises and land. The tender concerned space for the installation of machines for hot and cold drinks and land for the installation of a fast-food facility. According to the decision of the Governing Board, the commission was responsible for preparing the tender, opening and reviewing bids, and proposing the selection of the most favourable bidder. Ovčarić was, according to the minutes from March 2025, also appointed to the commission for the implementation of the tender for the lease of parking spaces in the hospital garage. These documents confirm that Ovčarić had a role in conducting hospital tenders. For the time being, however, it has not been officially confirmed whether precisely these procedures are the subject of the current investigation.

what sort of corruption is he suspected of?

As was previously reported, Ovčarić is suspected of having accepted several hundred euros in bribes from convicts in order to enable them to avoid the community service work they were required to perform at the hospital. Investigators also suspect that he favoured companies in obtaining jobs. In one case a company allegedly received a new job with the explanation that it had leftover unused stone from previous works, which enabled it to offer a lower price.

According to information obtained by Index, the award of the contract for the hospital kiosk to the owner of a service craft business with whom Ovčarić was close is also being investigated. It is suspected that Ovčarić himself actually ran the kiosk and earned income from its turnover. Allegations that hospital employees performed work on his private properties are also being checked. According to unofficial information, the USKOK action has involved eight persons. Police are carrying out arrests and urgent investigative measures in the area of Krapina-Zagorje County, Zagreb and Osijek. The Zabok General Hospital and Croatian Veterans’ Hospital confirmed that the police had requested documentation relating to one employee. They said they are cooperating with investigators but that, due to the ongoing investigation, they currently cannot comment on media reports.

World.title: 56,000 People in Croatia Diagnosed With a Disability in One Year
World.content:
November the 3rd, 2026 – There has been a staggering increase of 56,000 people across Croatia diagnosed with some kind of disability in just one year. As things currently stand, every fifth person in Croatia is disabled.

In just one single year, the number of recorded persons with disabilities in Croatia rose by as many as 56,000, according to a new report by the Croatian Institute of Public Health (HZJZ). Ivana Krnic reports for Jutarnji that according to the report, on 28 September this year there were 730,987 persons with disabilities living in Croatia, compared with 675,213 one year earlier. In other words, almost every fifth resident of Croatia is now officially recorded as a person with a disability.

Such a worrying and high increase is primarily, according to those familiar with the matter, a consequence of the introduction of the inclusive allowance. Namely, the Register of Persons with Disabilities is actually a database of persons who exercise some right on the basis of disability: persons who have not been assessed or do not exercise any right cannot be in that database, regardless of their actual disability.

Since the criteria for obtaining the inclusive allowance are incomparably milder than the criteria for the personal disability benefit or the allowance for another person’s assistance and care — rights that preceded the inclusive allowance — the number of persons receiving the inclusive allowance is significantly higher than the number of persons who previously received cash assistance. Specifically speaking, before the introduction of the inclusive allowance, around 150,000 persons received the personal disability benefit and the allowance for another person’s assistance and care, while the inclusive allowance is now received by around 240,000 persons, with around another hundred thousand applications still pending. The majority of persons receiving the inclusive allowance had the same or very similar difficulties earlier, but did not meet the strict criteria for receiving cash assistance and were therefore not registered as persons with disabilities.

The HZJZ response also confirms that the new rights have significantly increased interest in assessments.

new rights prompted an assessment increase

“It covers a wide range of rights and that has attracted a large number of persons who hadn’t previously been assessed to undergo assessment and try in this way to exercise some of the mentioned rights,” doc. dr. sc. Tomislav Benjak, assistant director of the HZJZ for the quality of healthcare and author of the Report on Persons with Disabilities, told Jutarnji list.

In addition to the inclusive allowance, he also mentions other rights, such as priority in employment, transport privileges, scholarships and tax reliefs, which can be exercised on the basis of an established disability. The method of collecting data also influenced the increase. Today almost all findings and decisions arrive digitally, practically immediately after the assessment, whereas previously they were partly delivered by post. Such a system did not guarantee that all of the data was indeed recorded in the Register. The largest part of the increase relates to persons over the age of 65. Their number rose in one year from 317,164 to 358,806, i.e. by 41,642 persons. That is almost three quarters of the total annual increase.

Today almost half of all persons recorded in the Register are over 65 years old, and disability has been established in approximately 40 percent of the population of that age. Benjak says that the ageing of the population is one of the main reasons for the long-term increase in the number of persons with disabilities. In older age, difficulties with mobility, impairments of sight and hearing, and the consequences of chronic diseases occur more frequently. However, part of the increase also stems from the fact that persons who were already recorded eventually move into the older age group.

“The natural transition from the age group up to 65 years into the age group of 65 years and over affects this distribution by approximately 30 percent,” he explains. Croatia is also not helped by the health habits of the population. Benjak warns of the high frequency of cardiovascular and malignant diseases, smoking, obesity and insufficient physical activity.

how much does croatia actually deviate from global trends?

Despite this, he emphasises that Croatia does not deviate significantly from international trends. When the first Register data was published back in 2007, the share of persons with disabilities was 10.7 percent, and today it is 18.9 percent. According to the data he cites, the World Health Organisation estimates that persons with disabilities make up around 16 percent of the world’s population, while Eurostat for the European Union cites 23.9 percent. These data, however, are not necessarily completely comparable because they are based on different methods of establishing disability. The new HZJZ report for the first time also brings a division according to the severity of disability. According to that classification, 106,724 persons have severe disability and 142,722 persons have more severe disability. Together that is almost 250,000 people. However, for as many as 206,902 persons, or 28.3 percent of all those recorded, the severity of disability has not been classified.

Benjak explains that these are mostly persons who were assessed many years ago, when the findings from the then social welfare centres did not contain the data needed for today’s classification.

Interestingly, a large part of these persons, despite the possibility of exercising these new rights, have not undergone a new assessment. It is also possible that they are not sufficiently informed. “What somehow surprises us as well is that around 200,000 persons assessed at that time with rights from social welfare and elements for entry into the Register have not requested new assessments in order to exercise the right to, for example, the inclusive allowance or rights in transport,” Benjak is also surprised.

He emphasises that this is not a matter of double entries or of deceased persons. Every person is tracked by personal identification number (OIB), and the HZJZ also has data on deaths. He confirms that all 206,902 persons are alive and that there is a legal basis for their entry into the Register. The new division according to the severity of disability serves exclusively for statistical purposes and does not affect the exercise of rights. Nevertheless, the fact that data needed for classification are missing for more than a quarter of the recorded persons shows how difficult it is to obtain a complete picture of the structure of disability in Croatia.

huge differences on a county by county basis

There are also large differences among counties. In Šibenik-Knin County disability is recorded in 24.4 percent of the population, almost twice as much as in Istria County, where that share is 12.3 percent. The range is even greater among those over 65 years of age. In Šibenik-Knin County 49.6 percent of the population of that age have a disability, in Požega-Slavonia County 49.5 percent, and in Istria County 25.1 percent.

Data for children and young people in Sisak-Moslavina County are particularly worrying. There the prevalence of disability in the age group up to 19 years rose from 17.9 to 20.5 percent, while the Croatian average is 12.3 percent. This means that disability is recorded in approximately every fifth child or young person in that county. Asked why the differences are so large, Benjak says that a special study would need to be conducted. Nevertheless, he warns that Sisak-Moslavina is one of the most deprived Croatian counties, with lower wages, weaker employment, higher unemployment and unfavourable demographic trends.

“All of the above certainly also has as a consequence the occurrence of disability and developmental difficulties in children,” Benjak believes. Without additional analysis it is not possible to determine how much health and social conditions, and how much the availability of diagnostics, assessments and the method of recording, influence such a high prevalence.

the case with children across croatia

Another seemingly unusual piece of data appears in the report. Although the total number of children and young people with disabilities is rising, the number of persons for whom decisions on an appropriate form of schooling arrived in the Register has decreased from 57,703 to 49,847. Nevertheless, it seems that the reason is not necessarily a smaller number of children with difficulties, but a change in the records.

According to Benjak’s explanation, the Ministry of Education requested the deactivation of records of persons up to the age of 21 whose only basis for entry into the Register was a decision on an appropriate form of schooling, and who after 2015 weren’t ever reassessed. Among them are persons who during childhood had developmental difficulties such as dyslexia, dysgraphia, behavioural disorders or learning difficulties, which over time may have decreased or disappeared. Changes in the records also explain the decrease in the number of Croatian war military invalids. Their number fell from 54,640 to 46,132, i.e. by 8,508 persons.

According to instructions from the Ministry of Croatian Veterans, only persons who are in its official database remain in the HRVI category. Some previously recorded persons no longer appear in that database, so their HRVI status in the Register has been deactivated. Despite such changes, Benjak claims that the annual reports have been prepared using the same methodology and that it is possible to track trends. In fact, the only novelty in the 2026 report is the additional statistical division according to the severity of disability. However, precisely the changes in the records of children and veterans show how much administrative decisions can influence the statistics.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports rise to 3.35 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil shipments increased in October by 9.5 percent to 3.35 million barrels per day, which is close to pre-war levels.

The rise is associated with an increase in the oil exports of the region’s main Arab oil-producing countries, supporting global supply and reducing pricing pressure.

According to tanker-tracking data and energy market analysis, the total oil exports from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, and Kuwait during October increased by 10 percent to 15.53 million barrels per day, a rate roughly equivalent to the levels seen at the beginning of the year.

However, for the second month in a row, there were no exports from Iran due to a naval blockade imposed by the United States, Bloomberg reported.

The increase reflects a rebound in oil supplies from Arab producers in the Gulf region, which is due to the use of new transport channels that helped them avoid the risks associated with navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq’s oil exports saw the second largest increase following Saudi Arabia’s, which rose to approximately seven million barrels per day in October, a 13 percent rise compared to September.

Oil supplies from the southern port of Basra have surged since Baghdad declared that its exports were getting close to pre-conflict levels, while those via the northern route—which passes through Turkey—have almost doubled.

This increase in Iraqi exports represents a larger attempt by Gulf producers to regain the quantities and income that the military conflict in the Middle East has affected.

Despite ongoing concerns about possible military escalation and supply disruptions, oil exporting countries are looking to bolster their position in international markets.

World.title: Big money flops as Democrats sweep US Congress
World.content:
Washington – Hundreds of millions of dollars spent, with little to show for it.

The rout of President Donald Trump and his Republicans in the US midterm elections was also a defeat for Elon Musk and for the massive campaign spending meant to sway voters.

Democrats captured both the Senate and House of Representatives on Tuesday in a stunning rejection of Trump’s political agenda, winning races in which conservative groups had poured in far more outside money than their liberal counterparts.

“This might have been the biggest defeat for big money in American political history,” Logan Phillips, founder of the election forecasting site Race to the White House, wrote on X.

“Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” Musk said on X, with a shrug emoji.

Musk contributed nearly half a billion dollars to Republican efforts, making him the largest individual contributor in a federal election cycle since 2010, according to campaign finance tracker OpenSecrets.

That year, the Supreme Court ruled that the government cannot limit political spending by corporations, unions and other groups acting independently of candidates, opening the way for big donors to pour vast sums into elections, sometimes anonymously.

– ‘Our own Goliaths’ –

More than $200 million of Musk’s money went to support Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate candidate in Texas.

Democrat James Talarico defeated Paxton, a close Trump ally, to become the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994.

“In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths. The richest man in the world, the most powerful man in the world and the entire Washington, DC establishment,” Talarico said.

He also targeted billionaires “who own the social media algorithms, who own the cable news networks, who own the politicians fighting on our screens” and who “want us at each other’s throats.”

In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown unseated Republican Senator Jon Husted in the country’s second most expensive race, with more than $500 million spent.

In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated billionaire health care executive Rick Jackson in the governor’s race, after he poured more than $200 million of his fortune into his bid, according to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution.

In Ohio, biotech billionaire Vivek Ramaswamy lost the governor’s race to Democrat Amy Acton after putting an estimated $36 million of his own money into it.

AI industry money also fell short.

In South Carolina, American Mission, the Republican arm of the Leading the Future network backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and venture firm Andreessen Horowitz, put about $2.7 million behind Senator Darline Graham, who lost to Democrat Annie Andrews in a state Trump won by 18 points.

Building the Future, a new data center industry super PAC tied to Leading the Future, had made Graham its first candidate to back.

– ‘Cannot yield’ –

Democrats also had billionaire backing. Former New York mayor Michael Bloomberg spent $80 million on House, Senate and governor races, then added $36 million in the final days, Politico reported.

Bloomberg’s political adviser Howard Wolfson told CNN that “money is not determinative, but it is helpful,” noting that Republicans held a significant financial advantage.

LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, who put $11.5 million into the super PAC backing Talarico, said “we should get money out of politics.”

“And while people like Elon are spending outrageous amounts to keep authoritarian clowns in power, those of us who believe in the ideals of America cannot yield,” Hoffman wrote on X late Tuesday, defending his largesse.

In California, a ballot proposal for a one-time 5 percent tax on the state’s billionaires seemed to have failed after some of its wealthiest residents spent hundreds of millions of dollars to defeat it.

World.title: Iraqi PM pays first visit to Bahrain since 2003
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Bahraini Prime Minister Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa headed their countries’ delegations on Wednesday during expanded discussions held in the capital, Manama.

The meeting addressed strategies to promote bilateral relations and measures to develop partnerships in different sectors to serve mutual interests and enhance prospects for coordination between the two countries, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi reaffirmed the Iraqi government’s commitment to enhancing bilateral ties with Bahrain and broadening the scope of cooperation in the political, social, and economic areas to serve the interests of the citizens of both countries.

Additionally, al-Zaidi highlighted Iraq’s efforts to establish regional peace and stability, seeing them as the essential foundations for attaining prosperity and economic integration among the countries of the region.

As it marks the first trip by an Iraqi prime minister to the country since 2003, Al Khalifa welcomed al-Zaidi’s historic visit to Bahrain.

The prime minister of Bahrain underlined that the visit would be a crucial beginning for future collaboration and the growth of business alliances.

Al Khalifa also emphasized Iraq’s crucial role in the region, pointing out the two friendly countries’ dedication to deepening their connections to improve the future of the people.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Bahraini king to boost bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Wednesday with the King of Bahrain, Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, during his official visit to the capital, Manama.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), al-Zaidi stated that his trip to Bahrain aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation in economic, trade, political, and social sectors.

Al-Zaidi extended an invitation to the king of Bahrain to visit Iraq, emphasizing that his visit aims to revive the historical relations between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi confirmed that both Iraq and Bahrain are striving to achieve stability in the region. He emphasized the importance of promoting dialogue as the main approach to establishing peace and alleviating tensions.

The king of Bahrain indicated that al-Zaidi’s visit would open new horizons for the relationship between the two countries.

Al Khalifa reaffirmed his country’s support for the Iraqi government and emphasized the need to pursue peace and stability, defend common interests, and strengthen bilateral ties to support coordinated Arab action.

As part of the Iraqi government’s effort to foster regional economic integration, handle cross-border security issues, and foster confidence, al-Zaidi has made recent regional visits to Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Syria, Turkey, and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports via Turkey rise to 500,000 barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has increased its oil exports via the Turkish port of Ceyhan to 500,000 barrels per day—a step aimed to bolster crude oil export outlets away from the Strait of Hormuz, according to the energy-focused website OilPrice.

Iraq has started using tanker trucks to deliver Basra crude to the country’s northern pipeline network. The port of Ceyhan is now exporting about 200,000 barrels of Basra crude per day. The oil is transported from southern oil fields to collecting facilities in Iraqi Kurdistan before being pumped toward the Turkish port.

Since the start of the military conflict in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz in March 2026, which significantly disrupted oil production and shipments from the Gulf region, Iraq has become more dependent on alternative export routes.

Crude oil production from Iraq’s southern fields fell by 70 percent during the first weeks of the war, averaging 1.3 million barrels per day—down from approximately 4.3 million barrels per day prior to the conflict—before showing signs of recovery in the past few months as exports via alternative routes increased.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair reported last month that the country’s oil exports reached pre-war levels in October, surpassing 3.4 million barrels per day.

Khudair mentioned that Iraq aims to revive a long-term pipeline project designed to transport crude oil to the Syrian coast along the Mediterranean, thereby bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. However, he noted that the project’s implementation could take three to four years.

World.title: Over 92% of Iraq’s issued dinar remains outside banks at 100.18 trillion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The volume of physical banknotes circulating outside Iraq’s commercial banking system remained above the 100-trillion-dinar mark through late August 2026, accounting for 92.8% of the country’s total currency in circulation despite a minor month-on-month contraction, according to Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) monetary indicators.

Data published by CBI revealed that cash holdings outside banks edged down by 609 billion dinars, slipping from 100.792 trillion dinars in late July to 100.183 trillion dinars at the end of August 2026.

Out of an aggregate 107.998 trillion dinars in total issued currency, commercial bank vault reserves totaled just 7.815 trillion dinars, leaving nearly 93% of liquid supply in the hands of the public and informal commercial channels.

On an annualized trajectory, cash hoarded outside formal deposit institutions expanded significantly, increasing by 7.623 trillion dinars compared to the 92.560 trillion dinars registered at the close of 2025.

The persistent concentration of liquidity outside banking vaults underscores deep-rooted structural reliance on paper cash, highlighting the ongoing institutional headwinds facing financial inclusion, electronic payments, and domestic deposit mobilization in Iraq.

World.title: Economist details 9 major challenges facing US firms in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi economic expert Nabil Al-Marsoumi outlined nine structural challenges confronting American companies operating in Iraq on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, noting that these operational hurdles continue to restrict foreign direct investment and complicate Baghdad’s efforts to diversify international partnerships outside the traditional hydrocarbon sector.

Al-Marsoumi structured the obstacles across three primary operating environments:

1. Legal and Regulatory Bottlenecks

Contractual Disputes: Persistent deadlocks and difficulties in resolving disputes arising from contractual terms with state institutions.

Absence of Dispute Resolution Mechanisms: The lack of streamlined, locally recognized international arbitration frameworks, resulting in protracted legal proceedings.

Frequent Changes in Regulations and Directives: Continuous shifts in administrative rules and sudden regulatory revisions that destabilize long-term corporate planning.

2. Financial and Administrative Pressures

Administrative and Financial Corruption: Bureaucracy and institutional rent-seeking that inflate the cost of doing business.

Cumbersome Customs Procedures: Protracted border-clearance delays impacting the transit of essential equipment and technical supplies.

High Tax Liabilities: Rising tariffs, fiscal duties, and aggressive tax assessments that compress operational profit margins.

Difficulty in Accessing Financing: Underdeveloped local capital markets and a rigid banking sector unable to provide advanced corporate credit instruments.

3. Infrastructure and Field Operating Risks

Power Supply Deficits: Ongoing instability in the national electrical grid, imposing heavy cost burdens for auxiliary power generation.

Security Concerns and Arms Proliferation: Lingering security vulnerabilities and uncontrolled weapons that necessitate substantial expenditures on physical security and site protection.

Al-Marsoumi’s diagnostic comes at a time when the federal government is attempting to attract Western enterprise to execute technical joint ventures in captured gas, modern transport networks, and urban logistics, underscoring that institutional and legal reforms remain critical prerequisites to safeguarding foreign private capital.

World.title: Expert warns CBI $3,000 traveler quota will drain reserves
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi economic expert Ziyad Al-Hashemi issued a sharp warning regarding the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) decision to raise the official cash dollar quota for outbound travelers from $2,000 to $3,000 per trip, arguing that the policy will needlessly erode sovereign foreign currency reserves while failing to address the fundamental structural drivers of parallel market dollar demand.

The Central Bank’s decision followed deliberations by the Ministerial Council for the Economy in Baghdad, attended by key cabinet ministers and senior financial officials to review currency volatility.

The measure comes less than three weeks after the CBI announced a regulatory framework on October 15, 2026, which had capped the traveler allocation at $2,000 every two months, with an annual ceiling of six disbursements.

In an analytical statement published on his social media platforms, Al-Hashemi characterized the reversal as institutional capitulation to government political pressure.

He described the move as a short-sighted monetary intervention intended to narrow the spread between the official peg (1,520 IQD per dollar) and the parallel rate (trading near 1,680 IQD) by injecting additional physical banknotes into the market.

Al-Hashemi stressed that while the increased allocation may generate a modest, short-lived dip in the parallel exchange rate, it exposes the treasury to net losses amounting to tens or hundreds of millions of dollars without absorbing parallel demand.

He argued that the parallel rate will quickly rebound under any fresh surge in commercial demand or regional geopolitical volatility.

Instead of draining cash reserves through informal secondary market leakage, Al-Hashemi contended that monetary authorities should prioritize resolving compliance bottlenecks for commercial wire remittances.

By broadening trade finance facilities and removing operational barriers for merchants, the central bank could systematically redirect legitimate commercial demand into formal banking channels rather than subsidizing cash transactions that ultimately feed parallel liquidity.

World.title: Two sisters among 4 Kedartal victims, search on for 4 others
World.content:
Two sisters from Lucknow were among four trekkers found dead following an

on the Kedartal trekking route in Uttarkashi district, with rescue teams recovering two more bodies on Wednesday, taking the toll to four, report Gaurav Talwar & Ashish Mishra. The deceased sisters were identified as Deepika Verma, 29, and Vartika Verma, 28, while the identities of two men remained unconfirmed.

World.title: Andhra, Kerala top ease of vehicle ownership index; UP, Bihar at bottom: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu have emerged as the top-performing states in ease of vehicle ownership, while Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal rank at the bottom, reflecting wide disparities in procedures for transferring ownership of used vehicles.

The findings are part of the Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index (EVOI) 2026, prepared by Consumer Voice and Indiatech, which assessed systems and procedures across 15 major states and Delhi, covering more than 85% of Indiaâs organised pre-owned vehicle market.

None of the states figured in the âhigh easeâ or excellent category, with Andhra Pradesh, the highest-ranked state, scoring only 5.9 on a scale of 0-10. Kerala scored 5.7, followed by Tamil Nadu and Delhi at 4.6 each.



Karnataka (4.3), Gujarat (4.2), Madhya Pradesh (4.1), Maharashtra and Telangana (4.1 each) and Punjab (4) occupied the next positions.

Rajasthan (4) and Haryana (3.9) were also in the lower half of the rankings, while West Bengal (2.6), Bihar (2.5) and Uttar Pradesh (2.5) brought up the rear.

The report comes as Indiaâs pre-owned vehicle market is expanding rapidly and is projected to grow from $36.4 billion in 2025 to over $73.5 billion by 2030.





The market has overtaken new vehicle sales in volume. However, fragmented state-level rules, incomplete digitisation and cumbersome procedures continue to impede seamless vehicle ownership transfers.

The report, which also included interviews, found that 39% of citizens reported delays in receiving their registration certificates after completing vehicle transfers, while 61.5% were unaware of the requirement for a party-pusher until they reached the respective RTO.

As many as 63% could not accurately estimate the total cost of completing an ownership transfer, reflecting widespread opacity in transaction charges.

Interestingly, all respondents said they relied on intermediaries or agents to complete ownership transfers because of administrative complexity.

The report has called for a unified digital vehicle records system, standardised no-objection certificate procedures, real-time integration between banks and transport departments for automatic removal of hypothecation after loan repayment, and transparent, time-bound service delivery across RTOs.

World.title: Two scrap collectors die in Srinagar fire, CM Omar Abdullah announces Rs 4L relief
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Two scrap collectors, including a minor, were killed in a fire that engulfed around 80 makeshift shelters in Durbal, Bemina, on the outskirts of Srinagar early Wednesday, officials said.

The blaze erupted around 12.30am. Police identified the deceased as Mohammad Noor Alam (27) and Al Ameen (16), both from Delhi. The flames also damaged an empty poultry farm and a tipper.

J&K CM Omar Abdullah condoled the deaths and announced ex-gratia relief of Rs 2 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased. He also directed authorities to ensure immediate relief and all necessary assistance to the affected families.

World.title: Trump’s ‘Freedom In Space’ signals new contest for Moon; India’s challenge is safeguarding strategic autonomy
World.content:
Trump's space declaration sparks a new Moon rules contest, forcing India to balance Artemis ties and 2047 ambitions against strategic autonomy.

Competing frameworks, competing interests

Indiaâs strategic dilemma

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: As Americans voted in the midterm elections, US President Donald Trump issued a proclamation titled âThe American Declaration of Freedom in Spaceâ, declaring that the US would lead the exploration, development, use and settlement of space.Promising a return to the Moon by 2028, a permanent American lunar presence and an eventual human mission to Mars, the proclamation links space leadership directly to economic prosperity and national security.But beneath its rhetoric of freedom and exploration lies a larger geopolitical question: who will set the rules for humanityâs expansion beyond Earth, and will space remain a global commons or become an arena of competing national interests? For India, which has its own ambitions for human spaceflight and lunar exploration, the declaration brings this question into sharper focus.Susmita Mohanty, director general of space think tank Spaceport SARABHAI, says: âTrump describes space as âthe province of all humansâ while, almost in the same breath, declaring his intention to establish a âpermanent presence by American citizensâ. The tension between these two assertions is difficult to ignore: a domain ostensibly belonging to all humanity is simultaneously being framed as a sphere for enduring American dominance,â she said.She also questioned the assertion of American superiority, pointing to the history of international contributions to space exploration. Russia, for instance, remained indispensable to American human spaceflight for nearly nine years after the retirement of the Space Shuttle fleet in 2011, transporting US astronauts to the International Space Station until SpaceX's Crew Dragon began crewed flights in 2020.Mohanty also pointed to Chinaâs growing capabilities. Since 2007, China has completed six lunar missions, including two sample-return missions, and is working towards landing astronauts by 2030. âSpace exploration has historically been a collaborative endeavour, one that repeatedly reminds terrestrial superpowers that their dominance has its limits,â she said.The implications extend beyond the US-China lunar race. Lt Gen AK Bhat (retd), director-general of the Indian Space Association (ISpA), believes the proclamation signals a shift towards competing frameworks for governing space activities.âThereâs now a clear divide of two groups: the Artemis-led group and the ILRS-led (China-Russia) group. Space colonisation, ownership and other things that have been talked about will definitely sow the seeds for future contests and maybe confrontation,â he said.The legal question is particularly important. Article I of the 1967 Outer Space Treaty describes space as the province of all mankind, while Article III prohibits national appropriation of celestial bodies. The proclamation, however, explicitly speaks of establishing a permanent American presence and developing resources, subject to international obligations. It does not itself confer ownership of lunar territory.Indiaâs position is complicated by its participation in multiple international frameworks. It signed the Artemis Accords in June 2023, but also signed the 1979 Moon Agreement, which it has not ratified. The two frameworks have different approaches to aspects of lunar resource governance.In Aug 2026, Nasa invited Isro to join its Moon Base programme, building on the Artemis partnership. India, meanwhile, has its own Space Vision 2047, including the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and a human Moon landing by 2040.For Bhat, this calls for a wider national debate on India's positioning. âThe issue is basically where India aligns its cards. Though signing of the Artemis Accords was an indicator of our inclination, there has to be an internal debate within the Indian community,â he said.He also cautioned against dismissing the proclamation as political rhetoric. âIt does not matter whether we take Donald Trump seriously or not. The signature on the paper is that of the President of the United States, aligning the policy for the future.âFor India, the challenge may be to work with competing space powers without being confined to their geopolitical choices, while ensuring it has a say in the rules governing the next frontier.

World.title: UN report finds huge gap in adaptation finance ahead of COP31
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Even if the developed countries triple their money available to support developing nations to adapt to climate change by 2035, it would still cover less than a third of what is actually needed to protect people from disastrous consequences of

, the UN Environment Programme flagged in its annual Adaptation Gap Report on Wednesday.

It estimates that the developing countries will need around $305 billion annually by 2035, or approximately $420 billion once future inflation is taken into account, to adapt themselves. But the collective pledge of the rich nations to triple international public finance flows could reach only $85-120 billion a year by 2035. So, this would only cover 20-29% of what the developing countries need to deal with intensifying climate impacts.



If one looks at the actual contribution of rich nations in 2024, they provided only $28.2-31.7 billion in 2024, a $1 billion increase over the previous year. It practically means for every dollar developing countries need to adapt, they receive just 10 cents.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âThe world is not ready to adapt to current climatic conditions, never mind what overshoot of 1.5 degrees Celsius will bring,â said Inger Andersen, executive director of UNEP, referring to the inevitability of global warming exceeding the 1.5 degree C threshold (above 1850-1900 levels).





Such warming has the potential to increase the number of extreme weather events, leading to worsening impacts of climate change.

The report ahead of the 31st session of the UN climate change conference (COP31), scheduled to take place in Antalya, Turkiye, from Nov 9 to 20, may help negotiators from participating countries to put additional focus on adaptation finance.

The report finds that adaptation finance continues to fall far short of needs, implementation remains constrained by institutional barriers, and loss and damage are mounting as climate impacts intensify. âAction on all these fronts is essential to build resilience in a rapidly changing climate,â it said.

World.title: 'Normalise, recognise and formalise': Nadda accuses Congress of opposing SIR to legitimise outsiders, destabilise country
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union health minister

on Wednesday accused the

of opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists to protect outsiders whose support, he alleged, had helped the party remain in power for a long time.

âBJP's Amit Shah favours 'detect, delete and deport'. And what does Congress say? What does INDIA bloc say? They say 'normalise, recognise and formalise',â Nadda said, addressing the 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' padyatra in Bhopal.

The senior

leader said the Congress was attempting to undermine constitutional institutions, including the

Election Commission

, because it was unable to secure public support, PTI reported.

Additionally, he alleged that the opposition wanted outsiders to be issued Aadhaar and ration cards and settled in the country so they could become voters.



âThese people who have come from outside, normalise them. Make Aadhaar cards for them, make ration cards for them, settle them down,â Nadda jibed at Congress.

âTell me, should we detect them or not? Should we deport them or not?â Nadda asked the public, urging it to âdeleteâ the Congress and the INDIA bloc.

Nadda accuses Congress of undermining EC credibility

The BJP leader accused the Congress of attempting to weaken the Election Commission, alleging that the party blamed the poll body whenever it lost elections.





âRealising that the electorate is unlikely to grant them any space in the political landscape for the next 20 to 30 years, they have resorted to blaming the Election Commission,â he said.

He also accused the Congress of adopting different positions depending on election results, claiming that the party praised Rahul Gandhi when it won in Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh but questioned the Election Commission when it lost.

He said Booth Level Officers (BLOs) visiting households to facilitate voter registration reflected the strength of India's electoral system.

World.title: SC rejects woman's plea to terminate six-month pregnancy over marital discord
World.content:
The woman's husband opposed the termination, arguing that he too had a right over the unborn child.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to allow a woman's plea for medical termination of her pregnancy which was over six months along citing marital discord with her husband.The case came before a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan, which had expressed concern over the request during an earlier hearing on Monday.The woman's husband opposed the termination, arguing that he too had a right over the unborn child and was willing to take care of the baby after birth.The bench said the case was different from those involving rape, sexual assault or foetal abnormalities, where termination may be permitted under the law.It questioned whether marital discord or alleged mistreatment by a husband and in-laws could, by itself, be grounds for ending an advanced pregnancy.âIt is normal that wife talks against husband and husband talks against wife but it does not mean that you have to terminate the pregnancy on that ground. It is not a case of sexual assault or single woman becoming pregnant. Where are we heading as a society if the wife says that she wants termination of pregnancy because of her fight with the husband and in-laws...What about the right of the father,â the bench had said on Monday.The woman, who appeared before the bench virtually, said she did not want to continue the pregnancy and wanted a divorce. Her husband, however, urged the court not to allow the termination. He told the bench that he would take custody of the child after birth and look after it.

World.title: Five years after alleged torture of labour activist during farmers’ agitation, Haryana Police book three personnel
World.content:
More than five years after a labour rights activist was allegedly kept in illegal confinement and tortured by the Sonipat Police during the farmers’ agitation against the three farm laws, the Haryana Police have registered an FIR against three police personnel, including two Inspectors and a Sub-Inspector.

The accused have been identified as then Kundli Station House Officer (SHO) Ravi, Sub-Inspector Shamsher Singh and CIA Sonipat Inspector Ravinder. The case has been registered on charges including voluntarily causing grievous hurt and wrongful confinement, following the findings of a judicial inquiry ordered by the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

The inquiry was initiated after the victim Shiv Kumar’s father, Rajbir Singh, approached the High Court alleging that his son had been tortured in police custody. The court subsequently directed a medical examination of Mr. Kumar by a medical board at the Government Medical College Hospital, Chandigarh. The examination revealed injuries, following which the court ordered a judicial probe.

In an affidavit filed before the court last month, Sonipat Police Commissioner Mamta Singh said a three-member Special Investigation Team had been constituted to ensure a “fair, impartial and expeditious investigation”.

According to the judicial inquiry report, Mr. Kumar was picked up by the police on January 16, 2021, and kept in illegal confinement until January 23, when he was formally shown as arrested and produced before a Magistrate.

“SI Shamsher Singh, then Additional SHO, Kundli, was the Investigating Officer of all three cases and had taken the police remand of Shiv Kumar on the night intervening January 23-24, 2021, which was granted till February 2, 2021,” the report said. It held him “directly responsible for the torture meted out to Shiv Kumar, along with the other police officials associated with him”.

The report also questioned the conduct of doctors who examined Mr. Kumar during his police remand. “Shiv Kumar was examined as many as five times from January 24, 2021 to February 2, 2021, but none of the doctors of the Government Hospital, Sonipat, or the doctor deputed in jail performed their duty, and they apparently danced to the tune of the police officials,” it said. It further observed that Vinay Kakran, who was posted as Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMIC), Sonipat, at the time, appeared not to have discharged his duty as required.

On the role of Inspector Ravi, the report said he headed the police team that picked up Mr. Kumar on January 16 and kept him in illegal confinement. Regarding Inspector Ravinder, then in-charge of the CIA, Sonipat, the report noted that he had denied Mr. Kumar was ever brought to the CIA premises. However, it said Mr. Kumar’s testimony indicated that the torture had taken place there.

Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Kumar described the FIR as “weak” and demanded that appropriate provisions relating to torture and caste-based abuse be added, including sections of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

He also sought an independent investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or an inquiry monitored by a sitting or retired judge, arguing that an investigation by the Haryana Police would not be effective.

Mr. Kumar further alleged that pressure was being exerted on him and his family. Claiming that his brother had been picked up again and that he was being kept under surveillance, he demanded an immediate end to such actions.

Ms. Singh could not be reached for her comments despite repeated attempts to contact her till the time of filing this report.

World.title: Schools must address bullying based on gender identity, sexual orientation: High Court
World.content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Department of School Education, Haryana, and the Central Board of Secondary Education to ensure that all schools situated within the territorial jurisdiction of the court comply with the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in Sukdeb Saha’s case and that the mechanism and internal committee in every school cover complaints of bullying and harassment on the basis of gender, gender identity and sexual orientation.

The court gave directions after hearing a petition by the mother of a 16-year-old boy, a student of a prominent school in Faridabad, who died on February 24, 2022, accusing the school authorities and the headmistress of it. Also, his artistic inclination was misunderstood by his peers as being effeminate, and he was bullied and physically and sexually assaulted by a group of students within the school premises, as per the petition.

In her petition, the teenager’s mother had demanded laying down of guidelines for sensitisation of the authorities and the educational institutions to prevent harassment of students belonging to the LGBTQIA+ community and ensuring execution of such guidelines in the schools and colleges across the country, besides seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the case.

Saying that the prayer for framing fresh guidelines cannot be accepted, the court observed that the Supreme Court in Sukdeb Saha’s case had taken note of the growing crisis of student deaths in the country and, in view of the binding guidelines of the apex court holding the field, no useful purpose would be served by this court laying down a separate set of guidelines on the same subject.

However, the court said the facts of the present case showed that “guidelines which remain on paper offer little protection to a child in distress”.

“The CBSE circular of the year 2015 was in force throughout the period during which the deceased child is alleged to have suffered. As per the record, the school was informed about his condition by his mother and his treating psychologist,” said the court, saying that the “real issue, therefore, is the effective implementation of the existing guidelines at the level of the schools.”

The court directed the Haryana School Education Department to ensure that complaints of bullying and harassment are “dealt with promptly and confidentially, and that the cases in which a cognisable offence is disclosed are reported to the police as required by law.”

The order said the CBSE must ensure that the annual reports required to be submitted to it as per the Supreme Court guidelines are called for and duly scrutinised, and that appropriate action is taken in accordance with its bye-laws in case of non-compliance.

Those in distress could seek help and counselling by calling helplines from this link.

World.title: Eleven tribals arrested for seeking rehabilitation for a proposed land port project in West Bengal
World.content:
Eleven people, all residents of Torsa Tea Garden located in West Bengal’s Alipurduar district, were arrested on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) for protesting against the construction of a land port at the India-Bhutan border. Locals have been protesting at the site demanding rehabilitation and compensation for the past 100 days.

Those arrested include four women and seven men, all hailing from adivasi/tribal communities. The family members of those arrested said that they were not aware of their whereabouts for about 18 hours and were moved to four to five police stations before registering their arrest. The FIR (Jaigaon PS Case No. 326/26), registered on 3 November, was based on a written complaint by Rakesh Kumar Meena, an LPAI Junior Engineer, dated November 2.

Construction at the Land Ports Authority of India (LPAI) site in Gotabari, Torsa Tea Garden, had been going on for nearly five months and during the period the locals maintained a peaceful, indefinite dharna beside the project site for over 100 days.

A press statement by Paschim Banga Cha Majoor Samity (PBCMS), a registered non-political union of tea garden workers, points out that there was no police complaint of obstruction or violence during the preceding 100 days when the locals were protesting against land acquisition. According to PBCMS, the confrontation occurred when bulldozers arrived on November 2 to proceed with work on disputed land, ignoring the families’ repeated demands for compensation. People protested and argued with officials.

“There was no violence, assault or damage to government property. Protest and disagreement cannot be criminalised as violence,” the union said in a press statement.

The FIR names prominent social activist Anuradha Talwar, Binoy Kerkatta and Mahesh Xalxo as having allegedly “provoked and instigated” the crowd, however, neither of the three was present at the protest site.

Earlier this year, an independent fact-finding team with Professor Virginius Xaxa, Siraj Dutt and Anuprada Singh visited Torsa from August 1-3 2026, and the findings confirm that generations of affected families have cultivated this land without ownership documents. Protesting against the arrests, locals from the tea garden have started protests against the administration at the proposed land port site.

Observing that the West Bengal government has chosen bulldozers and police action instead of dialogue, PBCMS has called for immediate release of all 11 arrested persons and withdrawal of the “false charges” against the 11 residents and three others.

The demands by PBCMS include an immediate halt to further eviction until land rights, compensation and rehabilitation claims are resolved and recognition of tea garden workers’ land rights and ownership of the land they have occupied and used for generations.

World.title: Ladakh bureaucrats worse than Britishers, says activist Wancghuk’s wife Angmo on stalling of kindergarten
World.content:
Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife, Gitanjali J. Angmo, on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) accused the Ladakh bureaucrats of being “worse than Bristishers for stopping a kindergarten school under different pretexts” and termed it “a witch-hunt”.

“This government is incompetent and indulges in witch-hunting. They do not know how to run educational institutes but are good at stalling others from doing so. On the one hand, national institutions ask us to impart lectures on setting up similar educational institutes; on the other, the Desert Flower School, which is a kindergarten level, is stopped from starting admissions,” said Ms. Angmo.

On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), the Ladakh administration said the Himalayan Institute of Alternatives, Ladakh’s (HIAL) Desert Flower School commenced functioning “without necessary approvals from the competent authority”. It asked the HIAL to strictly maintain the status quo and avoid causing any prejudice to the land lease case pending before the High Court of J&K and Ladakh.

She said the construction of the school started in 2023 with the donations of Public Sector Units “after due diligence and compliance”. “We could not start admissions last year due to the September 24 incident. We have followed the process of approvals but were directed to get a no-objection certificate from the Deputy Commissioner on not having any political members in the managing committee. While one office says it is a requirement, another denies the same,” said Ms. Angmo.

She said the official approvals “ideally should be granted after the school is functional and its infrastructure and teaching staff were evaluated”.

“I challenge this government to set up a school like Desert Flower School in five years. Bureaucrats are supposed to facilitate the public-private partnership. However, they are stalling it. Do we have any university featuring among the top 10 in the world? We want answers,” said Ms. Angmo.

Questioning the Ladakh administration’s statement on land lease to the HIAL, Ms. Angmo said the claims made in the government order were “baseless”.

“We have already informed the court about the land lease. In August last year, we informed the court about the eight applications, 10 rounds of the offices and 50 calls made to officials on the issue of the extension of land lease, which was pending for other institutes including government institutes. In its order, the court underlined that the third-party rights cannot be established and the HIAL activity could continue and highlighted the official delay in the extension,” said Ms. Angmo.

Mr. Wangchuk, who reacted to the latest official notice, also described it as a witch hunt. “It seems my association with the struggle to establish democracy and seek constitutional safeguards is being pointed out. Ever since V.K. Saxena took over as Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, the administration goes after all those who raise their voice against their policies, whether it’s liberal liquor policy, nautor land or rock dams on the Sindh river, which is an ecological disaster,” said Mr. Wangchuk.

He said the latest notice is to scare parents from admitting their wards into the school. “I hope the honourable courts will go into the substance of it. The notice is to tarnish us and confuse the parents,” he added.

World.title: Spend more time in India: Rijiju takes jibe at Rahul, list conditions for Congress to ‘win more MPs’
World.content:
Taking a jibe at Rahul Gandhi, Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) listed some conditions for Congress, saying if the Opposition party wants to "win more MPs", then their senior leader must spend more time in India and stop meeting anti-India people.

Mr. Rijiju has been taking on Mr. Gandhi and other Congress leaders for demanding an open debate with the Prime Minister.

In a post on X on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), he said that Congress can "win more MPs" if Mr. Gandhi meets seven conditions.

Listing these conditions mockingly, Mr. Rijiju said Mr. Gandhi should "spend more time in India and avoid secret foreign vacations frequently."

He also asked the Congress leader to respect seniors and gain valuable wisdom from the elders, which is Indian tradition.

The senior BJP leader further advised Mr. Gandhi not to meet "anti-India people and stop promoting their agenda."

As the fourth condition, the Minister asked Mr. Gandhi to "end deep hatred against BJP, RSS and Modi Ji" and "treat BJP as political opponent, not enemy."

He also asked the Congress leader to take "Parliament more seriously" and let MPs take part in debates and discussion. "Respect Constitution of India, and honour Constitutional Institutions, and allow Congress party to function as a democratic party and smash dynastic politics," he listed them as the last two conditions.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Rijiju had posted a video clip of his speech in Parliament when the Opposition leaders had walked out of the house.

"Parliament is the House for debates & discussion. But people who don't believe in democracy, debates and discussion are talking about debate," the Parliamentary Affairs Minister said.

Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) dared Prime Minister Modi once again to debate him openly and said he guaranteed that it would be proved in five minutes that the PM was a traitor, inviting a sharp response from Union finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

After Mr. Gandhi's challenge, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Prime Minister should come forward and face the questions on "vote theft" that the nation was posing.

"PM Modi is parroting his flop line of Dimaagi Naxal'! He has NO answer on Vote Chori and the Open Challenge by Rahul Gandhi to discuss how he mortgaged Indian interests to Foreign powers!" Mr. Kharge said.

Mr. Rijiju hit back in a post on X, saying, "Kharge Ji, Dimaagi Naxal is a term, not a narrative. Only following are Dimaagi Naxals: Who support Maoists agenda, and reject Indian Constitution. Who stand with the separatists & support Article 370. Who want to stop the development projects of India. Who conspire to cut chicken neck to separate North-East from India."

Mr. Gandhi on Tuesday (November 4, 2026) had challenged Mr. Modi to an open debate on his charge that the opposition is anti-national and asked why the Prime Minister has not filed a defamation case against him over his foreign connections allegation.

He accused Mr. Modi of occupying the PM's chair with foreign help, within a day of his earlier challenge for an open debate with the Prime Minister for accusing the opposition of taking foreign help to destabilise the country.

World.title: Israel President urges compromise after divisive election
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) doubled down on accusations of foreign interference in last week’s election, despite calls for compromise from the President.

More than a week after Israel’s first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, President Isaac Herzog began meeting party leaders to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government in the deeply polarised country.

Mr. Eisenkot, who won the endorsement of a major Arab party, vowed to “deepen” the U.S.-Israel partnership across bipartisan lines and to work with President Donald Trump to stabilise the region if selected as Prime Minister.

Mr. Netanyahu, meanwhile, pointed to “serious suspicions that foreign states have spent considerable sums to influence the outcome of the elections in Israel”.

The premier has gone on the offensive against Arab-majority lists, who have the power to put Eisenkot in power if they team up.

Mr. Netanyahu has pointed to the arrests of several people with envelopes of cash on election day in what authorities called localised incidents, and accused leaders of accepting money from Qatar, an allegation also levelled against the Prime Minister’s own aides.

With neither bloc holding a majority in the 120-seat parliament after the October 27 vote, Mr. Herzog said both sides needed to accept that “not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled” and to avoid new elections.

“In the current reality, in which there is no clear winner after the elections, I ask for originality and creativity, courage and goodwill, so that the State of Israel emerges the winner,” Mr. Herzog said.

The election saw soaring support for lists from the Arab minority, descendants of Palestinians who stayed in Israel after its 1948 creation and who have often been outraged by the harsh rhetoric and actions of Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

Without naming any leader, Mr. Herzog, whose role is usually ceremonial, said he had “great respect” for the Arab minority, which makes up around 20% of Israel’s population.

“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently,” he said.

U.S.-Israel partnership

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief who has vowed to turn the page on Mr. Netanyahu’s long, divisive reign, meanwhile vowed to “renew and deepen” Israel’s partnership with the United States and “strengthen the bipartisan foundations that have long sustained it”.

“I look forward to working closely and constructively with President Trump and his administration,” he continued on X.

“Together, we can advance our shared security interests, strengthen regional stability, and open new doors to prosperity for the peoples of the Middle East.”

His remarks follow criticism after Mr. Trump announced that he had agreed with Mr. Netanyahu to end nearly $4 billion in annual US military aid to Israel by the end of the year.

A leading Arab-Israeli party, Raam, officially endorsed Eisenkot to form a new government, ahead of a meeting with Mr. Herzog.

Mr. Eisenkot has warned Mr. Netanyahu against launching a new war with Mr. Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli Prime Minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.

Opposition lawmakers said Tuesday’s (November 4, 2026) midterm elections in the United States, in which Democrats trounced Mr. Trump’s Republicans, reinforced the need to remove Mr. Netanyahu.

Democrats have vowed a tougher line on Israel amid outrage over the devastation wrought by the war in Gaza.

“The continued tenure of Netanyahu and (Itamar) Ben Gvir could lead Israel down a path of international sanctions, international isolation and a clash with the U.S.,” said Yair Golan, who heads the most left-wing party within the opposition bloc.

No evidence found

The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and found no evidence that would question the results’ integrity.

The committee, which reflects the makeup of the outgoing parliament, approved the results with 15 members in favour and two against but 14 others abstaining.

Ben Gvir, the ultranationalist national security minister known for his provocative calls for Palestinian suffering, said his party did not accept the results and urged the arrest of Arab-Israeli party leaders.

Several Israeli media outlets said authorities were investigating Arab lawmaker Ayman Odeh for allegedly taking foreign money. He is part of the largest Arab group, the Joint List, which in a statement denounced “political persecution”.

Mr. Eisenkot accused the Prime Minister of trying to “undermine Israeli democracy” and inflame sentiment against elected officials.

“We will not allow the State of Israel to be dragged into a dark abyss, far beyond the bounds of democratic conduct,” Eisenkot said, as he marked the 1995 assassination of Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.

Mr. Herzog will hold an initial two days of consultations and then give a contender 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension.

World.title: Cyclone Murasu impact on Telangana | Extremely heavy rains lash Bhadradri on November 4
World.content:
A mandal each in Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem in Telangana, which were under red alert due to the impact of cyclone Murasu on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), received extremely heavy rainfall between 204 mm and 235 mm on the intervening night of Tuesday and Wednesday (November 3 and 4, 2026). And, some more mandals in the two districts received very heavy rainfall between 150 mm and 204 mm.

Of the two, Bhadradri Kothagudem did not get a break from the extremely heavy rain on Wednesday as a mandal there received 278.5 mm, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s rainfall data till 8.00 p.m.

The highest of 278.5 mm in Aswaraopet was followed by 188.3 mm in Malkaram in Dammapeta mandal, 175 mm in Ankampalem in Dammapeta and 149.8 mm in Mulakalapally.

India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centres in its impact weather bulletin issued at 11 a.m. has placed Bhadradri Kothagudem under orange alert indicating heavy to very heavy rain on Wednesday. Moderate to heavy rain was predicted in Mulugu and Khammam.

The highest amount of rainfall in Khammam was 13.5 mm in JVR OCP I&II, 6.3 mm in Pedapalli and 4.5 mm in Mancherial.

World.title: US Vice President JD Vance says Iran war is 'the reason we lost' midterms
World.content:
US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that the Iran war had doomed Republicans in the midterm elections, moving to distance himself from the unpopular conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run.
